title: Integrity
content:
Goal:

Implement policies and procedures to protect electronic protected health information from improper alteration or destruction.

Implementation specification:  Mechanism to authenticate electronic protected health information (Addressable). Implement electronic mechanisms to corroborate that electronic protected health information has not been altered or destroyed in an unauthorized  manner.

Policy Statement

HUBzero must include considerations in its Software Management Plan, Incident Response Plan, filesystem Security Model, and Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan that support integrity by preventing, detecting and remediating the alteration or destruction of data.

HUBzero should, wherever practical, use good practices that maintain the integrity of data, such as database foreign key constraints.  In addition, where such implementation will not duplicate already existing controls provided by a computing environment (e.g., SDSC Sherlock or AWS), HUBzero must implement the minimum requirements of the NIST control family "SI System and Information Integrity", in controls SI-1, SI-2, SI-3, SI-4, SI-5 and SI-12.

Implementation

Fail2ban will be employed to monitor ssh logs, apache logs, and the mail system, which are all login mechanisms. The integrity of system packages will be verified at least quarterly by using utilities provided by the operating system. In addition, in the HUBzero "publications" functionality, publications will be stored with a hash for integrity verification purposes.

HUBzero will attempt to detect system-level attacks as described in the other technical safeguard sections (164.312). HUBzero’s response to successful unauthorized modification or destruction of EPHI is to restore data from the last backup, as described in the Incident Response Plan, and if applicable, the Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan.

Custom applications developed for a particular hub must implement their own protection scheme (e.g., database foreign key constraints, hashes, etc...) to protect EPHI information, as appropriate for the application.  Developers of applications hosted on HUBzero infrastructure should develop procedures for detecting attempts to modify or destroy EPHI by attacking the application.

 

For historical purposes, an old version of this policy is stored in the old wiki.

title: Transmission Security
content:
Definition

Implement technical security measures to guard against unauthorized access to electronic protected health information that is being transmitted over an electronic communications network.

1. Integrity Controls

The goal of integrity controls is to “implement security measures to ensure that electronically transmitted electronic protected health information is not improperly modified without detection until disposed of.”

HUBzero shall use a version of TLS (Transport Level Security) considered secure, and SSH for command shells. The TLS "cipher suites" shall be selected based on the recommendations of the Qualys SSL server test, which shall be run at least yearly.  The allowed SSH ciphers, key exchange mechanisms, and MACs shall be selected using well-recognized and up-to-date recommendations, and shall be reviewed yearly. The encrypted communication provides sufficient protection against man-in-the-middle-attacks. Hosted covered applications must ensure to use these or equivalently secure methods.

Further, TLS guarantees to web application users that the data comes from the genuine HUB, and not from a malicious server. These measures prevent improper unauthorized modifications to electronically transmitted PHIs during transmission. 

2. Encryption

All communication between HUB web servers and users is encrypted using TLS as described above. Any other communication mode created by applications not part of the HUBzero software core must be secured by the developers. Backups of covered hubs are done according to Sherlock policies and procedures.  In addition, all staff desktops, laptops and mobile/portable devices must employ whole disk encryption or container encryption.  All storage media must be encrypted as well, e.g., USB keys or drives, CD-ROMs, DVDs, unless it contains only public files, such as a Linux distribution installation DVD or CD.

3. Forbidden transmissions

EPHI MUST NOT be transmitted via email or text (SMS) messages, or any feature offered by Slack (slack.com) or KanbanFlow (kanbanflow.com). HUB software MUST NOT allow EPHI to be transmitted via those technologies. Hubzero staff MUST NOT store any EPHI on a workstation (including laptop) unless that is part of their job description and the workstation has been properly setup (e.g., encryption). This makes transmission via email impossible in the first place, except as noted. If EPHI is stored on a workstation, it MUST be segregated from other files and stored encrypted to diminish the likelihood and impact of an accidental transmission.

HIPAA-covered hubs MUST NOT use NFS v3 services anywhere, because NFSv3 does not provide encryption and has weak authentication, unless a dedicated direct cable connection is used between the systems, or a dedicated isolated network where only the NFS server and clients are connected.

4. Use of HTTP(S)

Websites and services available over HTTPS shall enable HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) to instruct compliant browsers to assume HTTPS going forward.  Allowing HTTP connections for the sole purpose of redirecting clients to HTTPS connections shall be acceptable and encouraged. HSTS headers must specify a max-age of at least 1 year.

title: 164.314 Organizational Requirements
content: HUBzero shall comply with SDSC and UCSD policies, and for HIPAA-covered hubs, with Sherlock policies. Additional organizational requirements need to be managed by the particular covered hub.

title: 164.316 Policies and Procedures and Documentation Requirements
GDPR
content:
PRELIMINARY DRAFT -- THOUGHTS

Implications of the EU General Data Protection Regulation for HUBzero and Individual Hubs

GDRPR Enforcement date: 25 May 2018

GDPR Key Changes


Increased Territorial Scope (extra-territorial applicability)

The language indicates that they want it to apply to any HUB that has data from EU citizens.  The most onerous clause seems that "Non-Eu businesses processing the data of EU citizens will also have to appoint a representative in the EU".  I see no reasonable way for HUBzero, individual hubs or even small businesses to comply with this.

Penalties

Both HUBzero and individual Hubs would fall under the  €20 Million maximum fine.  There is a possibility that they will consider that Purdue University is liable instead and go for 4% of Purdue's annual global turnover.

Breach Notification

Notifications must be done " within 72 hours of first having become aware of the breach", without consideration of holidays or weekends, which may make compliance difficult.

Right to Access, Right to be Forgotten, Data Portability, Privacy by Design

This will require the creation of new procedures and capabilities, in addition to ongoing operational expenses to respond to requests.  In addition, compliance with Privacy by Design is difficult to prove.

Strategy

Risks are high.  Compliance will increase operating costs, as new procedures will need to be developed and a representative retained, and even then fines are possible.  Detaching HUBzero from Purdue University completely might provide risk reduction through isolation for Purdue.  The alternative is to block IP addresses associated with the EU, like we're already doing for E-nations.

title: FISMA Security Control Traceability Matrix
content:
A Security Control Traceability Matrix (SCTM) is part of a particular System's Security Plan (SSP).  Controls are sets of policies and procedures defined and followed to achieve a security goal.  The SCTM has 3 types of "controls":

  • Common: "A security control that is inheritable by one or more organizational information systems."  That means we can define these controls once for all, or a group of, systems operated by HUBzero in the Sherlock environment.
  • System: "A security control for an information system that has not been designated as a common security control or the portion of a hybrid control that is to be implemented within an information system."  That means the control is specific for a particular system's requirements and is not applicable to others.  For example, ncihub has hub-specific policies described at https://ncihub.org/projects/policies/notes.
  • Hybrid: "A security control that is implemented in an information system in part as a common control and in part as a system control."

At the time of this writing, HUBzero only operates one FISMA-certified system, ncihub.org, so all controls for this FISMA-Low system will be described here.  If more FISMA-certified systems were to be operated, this document should define "common" controls that would apply to all systems hosted by HUBzero in the Sherlock environment, and separate documents should define the "system" controls for each. 

This SCTM provides a mapping of controls to existing HUBzero policies defined elsewhere, and as needed defines additional policies and procedures for the implementation of a control.    Should this document conflict with a particular System's Security Plan and this document contains more recent versions of controls, the SSP shall be examined for any needed updates, and the updated SSP shall be followed.

This document was prepared using the NCI System Security Plan template that used NIST Special Publication 800-53 revision 4, which is valid but to be withdrawn on September 23, 2021.  At time of this writing (January 2021), the NIST Special Publication 800-53 revision 5, "Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations" is the most recent version, but we do not use it yet.  Please refer to revision 4 for the definitions of controls and control enhancements.  The NVD has a particularly useful organization of the controls, by family and by impact baseline.

Important: The text used in the NCI System Security Plan template does not match exactly the SP 800-53 control descriptions because "assignments" have been made.  These assignments represent decisions made by NCI, and the text in the SSP template takes precedence over the more generic SP 800-53.

title: (AC) Access Control
content:
AC-1 Access Control Policy and Procedures

NCI SSP description:

"The organization:
a. Develops, documents, and disseminates to personnel/roles identified in Appendix A: Roles and Responsibilities of the NIH InfoSec Handbook:
1. An access control policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance;
2. Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the access control policy and associated access controls; and
b. Reviews and, if necessary, updates the current:
1. Access control policy at least once every three (3) years.; and
2. Access control procedures at least once every three (3) years."

Current implementation details:

This is documented in, and disseminated from, the web pages in help.hubzero.org/documentation for:

  • "164.308 a 4 Information Access Management"
  • "164.310 a 1 Facility Access Controls"
  • "164.312 a Access Control"
  • The Hubzero webserver filesystem security model, utilizing "access-*" groups to grant capabilities based on roles
  • Procedures documented at help.hubzero.org/documentation under "Information Technology Policies and Procedures", e.g., "Account Management"

Historical, for reference only:

  • Purdue University's Information Security and Privacy (VII.B.8) (supersedes "Data Security and Access Policy (C-34)" as of November 2017)

AC-2 Account Management

NCI SSP description:

"The organization:

a. Identifies and selects the following types of information system accounts to support organizational missions/business functions: [Assignment: NIH-defined information system account types located in the NIH Account Lifecycle and Password Policy. The account types are Primary, Secondary, Resource, Service, Training, and Shared];
b. Assigns account managers for information system accounts;
c. Establishes conditions for group and role membership;
d. Specifies authorized users of the information system, group and role membership, and access authorizations (i.e., privileges) and other attributes (as required) for each account;
e. Requires approvals by [Assignment: an NIH or IC Administrative Officer or an Administrative Officer’s Designated Representative] for requests to create information system accounts];
f. Creates, enables, modifies, disables, and removes information system accounts in accordance with defined and documented procedures in the NIH Account Lifecycle and Password Policy.
g. Monitors the use of information system accounts;

h. Notifies account managers:
1. When accounts are no longer required;
2. When users are terminated or transferred; and
3. When individual information system usage or need-to-know changes;

i. Authorizes access to the information system based on:
1. A valid access authorization;
2. Intended system usage; and
3. Other attributes as required by the organization or associated missions/business functions;

j. Reviews accounts for compliance with account management requirements [Assignment: at least within every 365 days]; and
k. Establishes a process for reissuing shared/group account credentials (if deployed) when individuals are removed from the group."

Current implementation details:

a. (Reference to the NIH Account Lifecycle and Password Policy which we don't have access to)
b. Gateway managers, CMS managers and the ISO act as account managers.
c. The HUBzero policy "164.308 a 4 Information Access Management" establishes conditions for group and role membership.
d. The authorized administrative users, group and role memberships, and access authorizations for each privileged OS account are specified in Ansible.  Likewise, web accounts are specified in the HUBzero software database.
e. Please refer to the Sherlock policies and SSP for administrative users.  Web accounts are created automatically as required by the science gateway mission of the HUBzero software.  Additional privileges are granted by approval of CMS administrators.
f. (Reference to the NIH Account Lifecycle and Password Policy)
g. Usage of information system accounts is logged
General usage is logged in the database table "jos_activity_logs".  This is supplemented with additional logging implemented by "components".  Each software component is responsible for logging the usage of the functionality they provide.
h. Please refer to the Sherlock policies and SSP.
i. Please refer to the Sherlock policies and SSP.
j. This is documented in the HUBzero policy "164.308 a 4 Information Access Management"
k. This is documented in the HUBzero policy "164.308 a 4 Information Access Management"

Historical, for reference only (2016 certification implementation details):

"Partially addressed by

  • Web server filesystem security model (HUBzero production environment access-* groups)
  • HIPAA 164.308 Administrative Safeguards (a) (4) Information Access Management: Implement policies and procedures for authorizing access to electronic protected health information that are consistent with the applicable requirements of subpart E of this part.
  • Whereas HUBzero policies define appropriate broad policies and procedures, NCIPhub may want to refine details or redefine intervals (e.g., between audits). For example, NCIPhub may want some NCI personnel to have administrator privileges on the web interface, and some other groups of users to have different levels of access on the web interface. HUBzero supports and provides the mechanisms for these optional refinements. It is up to NCIPHub to decide to use them or not, and to refine policies or add procedures for managing the access it wants to grant to some members of its community. The “Policies” project on NCIPhub.org contains such refinements to policies that NCIP wants to make."

AC-3 Access Enforcement

NCI SSP description:

The information system enforces approved authorizations for logical access to information and system resources in accordance with applicable access control policies.

Current implementation details:

The HUBzero science gateway web application uses identity-based and role-based policies, and access
enforcement mechanisms (e.g., access control lists, authentication/authorization, cryptography) to control user access to web pages, downloadable objects (e.g., videos, presentations, pdf documents, etc...) and other functionality.

AC-7 Unsuccessful Login Attempts

NCI SSP description:

The information system:

a. Enforces a limit of [Assignment: six] consecutive invalid logon attempts by a user during a [Assignment: sixty minutes]; and

b. Automatically [Selection: locks the account/node for an [Assignment:Locks the account for 30 minutes or until reset by an administrator or by using the self-registration website utility]; locks the account/node until released by an administrator; delays next logon prompt according to [Assignment: organization-defined delay algorithm]] when the maximum number of unsuccessful attempts is exceeded.

Current implementation details:

The HUBzero science gateway web application enforces configurable limits to consecutive invalid logon attempts in a certain period of time.  It automatically locks the account and delays the next logon until the number of failed attempts/time interval drops below the same treshold, or until released by an administrator.  The NCH ncihub.org sets these values in its policy at https://ncihub.org/projects/policies/notes to 6 during a 1 hour window, after which an account will be locked. Accounts will be automatically unlocked when the number of failed attempts during the 1-hour window falls below 6.  The procedure to manage controls for compliance is documented in the "Account Management" HUBzero InfoSec procedures.

AC-8 System Use Notification

NCI SSP description:

The information system:

a. Displays to users the HHS Warning Banner Policy (note, this banner policy is not publicly accessible) before granting access to the system that provides privacy and security notices consistent with applicable federal laws, Executive Orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and guidance and states that:
1. Users are accessing a U.S. Government information system;

2. Information system usage may be monitored, recorded, and subject to audit;

3. Unauthorized use of the information system is prohibited and subject to criminal and civil penalties; and

4. Use of the information system indicates consent to monitoring and recording;

b. Retains the notification message or banner on the screen until users acknowledge the usage conditions and take explicit actions to log on to or further access the information system; and

c. For publicly accessible systems:

1. Displays system use information [Assignment: organization-defined conditions], before granting further access;

2. Displays references, if any, to monitoring, recording, or auditing that are consistent with privacy accommodations for such systems that generally prohibit those activities; and

3. Includes a description of the authorized uses of the system.

Current implementation details:

NCH ncihub.org has banners meeting the NCI requirements for all public-facing services, which all have customizable banners.  CMS administrators can customize the banner to suit. The procedure is documented under the "System Use Notifications" of the "Account Management" HUBzero InfoSec procedures.

AC-14 Permitted Actions without Identification or Authentication

NCI SSP description:

The organization:

a. Identifies [Assignment: that no user actions can be performed] that can be performed on the information system without identification or authentication consistent with organizational missions/business functions; and

b. Documents and provides supporting rationale in the security plan for the information system, user actions not requiring identification and authentication.

Current implementation detail:

The HUBzero web application does not allow user actions to be performed without identification or authentication consistent with organizational missions or business functions.  As the mission of science gateways with self-registered users such as the NCH ncihub.org is to provide some public information, the HUBzero web application allows searching for and accessing public information, as well as submitting support tickets, without authentication.  All other actions require authentication.

AC-17 Remote Access

NCI SSP description:

The organization:
a. Establishes and documents usage restrictions, configuration/connection requirements, and implementation guidance for each type of remote access allowed (including access to internal networks by VPN);
b. Authorizes remote access to the information system prior to allowing such connections; and
c. Access to HHS and/or NIH Webmail using personally-owned equipment is authorized. Access to other systems/networks using personally-owned equipment is prohibited without written authorization from the NIH or IC CIO, or an approved policy allowing the use of personally-owned equipment. If the NIH allows the use of personally-owned equipment on HHS or NIH systems or networks:
1. Personally-owned equipment must be scanned before being connected to HHS or NIH systems or networks to ensure compliance with HHS, NIH and IC system requirements (such as patch management requirements); and
2. Personally-owned equipment must be prohibited from processing, accessing, or storing HHS, NIH or IC sensitive information unless it is approved in writing by the NIH SOP and NIH CISO and employs FIPS 140-2-compliant encryption capabilities.

Note: In accordance with NIH Policy Manual Chapter 2814 – NIH Policy on the Prohibited Use of Non-Government Furnished (Non-GFE) IT Equipment, NIH phased out the use of Non-GFE in 2013. The content above is provided to preserve the integrity of the control as stated in NIST SP 800-53, Rev 4.

Current implementation detail:

The HUBzero web application is a browser-accessed web application for collaboration.  Web access via HTTPS on port 443 is available world-wide to all users at all times with any equipment.  HUBzero staff is provided UCSD-owned equipment but is allowed to use personally-owned equipment for administrative purposes provided that this equipment is kept continuously up-to-date with security patches, has anti-virus installed, and uses encryption at rest.  Remote access privileges for administrative purposes are documented in the Web server filesystem security model (HUBzero production environment access-* groups).

AC-18 Wireless Access

Current implementation detail:

HUBzero does not provide wireless access.   Administrative access requires the use of the Sherlock VPN.


AC-19 Access Control for Mobile Devices

Current implementation detail:

The HUBzero web application has no knowledge of the nature of the devices accessing its web service.  HUBzero staff may use personal mobile devices under the restrictions described in AC-17.

AC-20 Use of External Information Systems

The organization establishes terms and conditions, consistent with any trust relationships established with other organizations owning, operating, and/or maintaining external information systems, allowing authorized individuals to:

a. Access the information system from external information systems; and

b. Process, store, or transmit organization-controlled information using external information systems.

Current implementation detail:

The HUBzero terms and conditions satisfy this requirement for user-owned equipment. The NCH (ncihub.org) does not use external information systems outside of Sherlock.

AC-22 Publicly Accessible Content

The organization:

a. Designates individuals authorized to post information onto a publicly accessible information system;

b. Trains authorized individuals to ensure that publicly accessible information does not contain nonpublic information;

c. Reviews the proposed content of information prior to posting onto the publicly accessible information system to ensure that nonpublic information is not included; and

d. Reviews the content on the publicly accessible information system for nonpublic information bi-weekly and removes such information, if discovered.

Current implementation detail:

By virtue of its mission objective of collaboration, NCH (ncihub.org) allows all to post information.  Users are responsible for knowing which information is nonpublic before posting, and for reviewing contents.  Because the information has many data owners from different agencies and organizations, it is impractical for NCH (ncihub.org) to attempt to review the posted contents for nonpublic information.

title: (AR) Accountability, Audit, and Risk Management
content:
(AR) Accountability, Audit, and Risk Management

(AR-2) Privacy Impact and Risk Assessment

A Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) has been conducted for NCIPHub.  The PIA for NCIPHub was submitted to the NCI Privacy Coordinator May 29, 2015;  nothing related to privacy changed since. The NCIPHub does not contain any PII besides the account's contact information and user profile.  The user profile is optional and the account creation process doesn't even attempt to collect that information.

(AR-4) Privacy Monitoring and Auditing


"Control: The organization monitors and audits privacy controls and internal privacy policy
[Assignment: organization-defined frequency] to ensure effective implementation."

NCIPhub has a privacy policy at https://nciphub.org/legal/privacy.  It behooves NCIPhub, instead of HUBzero, to review it.

(AR-5) Privacy Awareness and Training

"Control: The organization:
a.  Develops, implements, and updates a comprehensive training and awareness strategy aimed at
    ensuring that personnel understand privacy responsibilities and procedures;
b.  Administers basic privacy training [Assignment: organization-defined frequency, at least
    annually] and targeted, role-based privacy training for personnel having responsibility for
    personally identifiable information (PII) or for activities that involve PII [Assignment:
    organization-defined frequency, at least annually]; and
c.  Ensures that personnel certify (manually or electronically) acceptance of responsibilities for
    privacy requirements [Assignment: organization-defined frequency, at least annually]."

Purdue HUBzero annually undergoes HIPAA privacy training and certification.

(AR-6) Privacy Reporting

"Control: The organization develops, disseminates, and updates reports to the Office of
Management and Budget (OMB), Congress, and other oversight bodies, as appropriate, to
demonstrate accountability with specific statutory and regulatory privacy program mandates, and
to senior management and other personnel with responsibility for monitoring privacy program
progress and compliance."

This is a hybrid control.  Through HUBzero's completion of the Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) and the annual review as directed by the NCI Privacy Office, the NCI Privacy Office has the information needed to report up to the OMB as required.


(AR-7) Privacy-enhanced System Design and Development

"Control: The organization designs information systems to support privacy by automating privacy
controls."

Information collected by NCIPhub is private by default, and the user profile is optional.  The system automatically allows users editing access to their profile.

title: (AT) Awareness and Training
content:
The HUBzero policies relevant to the AT control family are described in:

  • 164.308 Administrative Safeguards (a) (5) Security Awareness and Training

AT-1 Security Awareness and Training Policy and Procedures

The HIPAA 164.308 Administrative Safeguards (a) (5) Security Awareness and Training addresses the security awareness training policy documentation.

 

AT-2 Security Awareness Training

The HIPAA 164.308 Administrative Safeguards (a) (5) Security Awareness and Training addresses the new user initial training and changes to the system training.

 

AT-3 Role-Based Security Training

HUBzero will provide role-based security training to personnel with assigned security roles and responsibilities:

a. Before authorizing access to the information system or performing assigned duties;

b. When required by information system changes; and

c. Within three (3) months of entering a position that requires role specific training, and at least once every 365 days thereafter."

For this purpose, HUBzero will:

  • Identify security responsibilities that would benefit from training
  • Identify roles that have security responsibilities requiring training beyond that provided by the mandatory UCSD cybersecurity training.
  • Procure training, creating it if necessary, and maintaining a list of needed training material and their status
  • Create and maintain a map of which roles people have
  • Maintain training records showing how training was pursued and that record completion date or any training waivers

The implementation of the above policy is described at https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/itppr/procedures/administrative/role-based-training

Last Updated: March 18, 2022

AT-4 Security Training Records

Requirements: "The organization:

a. Documents and monitors individual information system security training activities including basic security awareness training and specific information system security training; and

b. Retains individual training records for a minimum of five (5) years after completing a specific training course."

The HIPAA 164.308 Administrative Safeguards (a) (5) Security Awareness and Training addresses the security awareness training policy documentation.

title: (AU) Audit and Accountability
content:
This is not a policy document. 

This document describes implementation details for controls, i.e., control requirements in comparison to implementation status in relation to responsibilities of HUBzero and the providers of the environments we are using (e.g., Sherlock).

AU-1 Audit and Accountability Policy and Procedures

The organization:

a. Develops, documents, and disseminates to [Assignment: personnel/roles identified in Appendix A: Roles and Responsibilities of this Handbook]:

1. An audit and accountability policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and

2. Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the audit and accountability policy and associated audit and accountability controls; and

b. Reviews and updates the current:

1. Audit and accountability policy [Assignment: at least once every three (3) years; and

2. Audit and accountability procedures [Assignment: at least once every three (3) years].

Current Implementation Details:

HUBzero implemented the above requirements in the following policy and procedures documentation:

  • 164.312 Technical Safeguards b Audit Control
  • 164.308 a1 (ii) D: Information System Activity Review

Historical: 

for Purdue hosting, see Purdue policies:

  • IT Resource Logging (S-11)

AU-2 Audit Events

The organization:

a. Determines that the information system is capable of auditing the following events;
• Server alerts and error messages
• User log-on and log-off (successful or unsuccessful)
• System administration activities;
• Modification of privileges and access
• Start up and shut down
• Modifications to the application
• Application alerts and error messages
• Configuration changes
• Account creation, modification, or deletion
• (Moderate and High only) Read access to sensitive information
• (Moderate and High only) Modification to sensitive information
• (Moderate and High only) Printing sensitive information;

b. Coordinates the security audit function with other organizational entities requiring audit-related information to enhance mutual support and to help guide the selection of auditable events;

c. Provides a rationale for why the auditable events are deemed to be adequate to support after-the-fact investigations of security incidents; and

d. Determines that the following events are to be audited within the information system at least weekly:
• Unsuccessful log-on attempts that result in a locked account/node;
• Configuration changes;
• Application alerts and error messages;
• System administration activities;
• Modification of privileges and access; and
• Account creation, modification, or deletion.

Note: these are the minimum set of events that should be audited, but OpDivs, System Owners, or applicable organization components are free to expand this list if necessary based on organizational risk.

Current Implementation Details:

HUBzero policies conform to this control but determination that auditing all events listed is possible hasn’t been done, and procedures haven’t been created to audit and review weekly all these events.

AU-3 Content of Audit Records

The information system generates audit records containing information that establishes what type of event occurred, when the event occurred, where the event occurred, the source of the event, the outcome of the event, and the identity of any individuals or subjects associated with the event.

Current Implementation Details:

The HUBzero policy meets these requirements;  however, the implementation details haven’t been verified for all the events defined in control AU-2

historical, for reference only (2016 SSP):

HUBzero must define the auditable events that are relevant to the security of the information system, coordinate the audit function with other groups within the university, and provide rationale as to why the auditable events are adequate to support investigations of security incidents.

The primary goal of HUBzero incident response is to restore integrity and availability and protect confidentiality, not to provide forensic evidence for law enforcement's use. For that reason, all authentication attempts (successes and failures) across all mechanisms supported by the Apache web service are logged, including use of cookies, WebDAV, SVN over HTTP, Google and Shibboleth. Repeated failures result in bans to protect against brute force attacks, except for Google and Shibboleth because these authentication mechanisms have their own protection mechanisms. HUBzero also logs mail (SMTP) events. The IP addresses of servers attempting to deliver spam; this is used to block repeated attempts to abuse the mail system. HUBzero also logs all requests made to the web server, which are processed with regular expressions to detect unusual activity and automatically block some forms of attacks (e.g., SQL injection scans). Similarly, SSH activity is logged and processed with regular expressions to automatically block repeated attacks, as well as flag that activity in automated emails sent to administrators.

AU-4 Audit Storage Capacity

The organization allocates audit record storage capacity in accordance with [Assignment: at a minimum, audit record storage capacity should be enough space to preserve 90 days of audit records.

Current Implementation Details:

HUBzero relies on the virtual environments where it is deployed to provide disk space as needed (e.g., SDSC Sherlock, SDSC RDS and AWS).

historical, for reference only (2016 SSP):

HUBzero uses LVM to flexibly manage storage space, in combination with monitoring of storage status every 5 minutes and alarms with the Xymon system. Currently NCIPhub has a dedicated logical volume for logs (/dev/ncip/log) of 20 GB, which is only filled at 18% capacity. This usage level is expected to be constant or scale with site usage because log rotation retains logs for only 30 days on the server itself. Monthly backup images kept for a year effectively provide log coverage for a year.

AU-5 Response to Audit Processing Failures

The information system:

a. Alerts [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] in the event of an audit processing failure; and

b. Takes the following additional actions: [Assignment:Overwrite oldest audit records].

Current Implementation Details:

HUBzero policies meet the requirements of this control, and there is appropriate response to any lack of logging storage, but the implementation is incomplete.

AU-6 Audit Review, Analysis, and Reporting

The organization:

a. Reviews and analyzes information system audit records [Assignment:weekly] for indications of [Assignment:
• Changes to sensitive system files
• 50 or more failed logons within 10 minutes
• Creation of user accounts outside NIH established process
• Improper or unauthorized usage of administrator privileges
• Use of service accounts for interactive log on
• File access attempts by unauthorized user accounts
• Deletion of files that user accounts have permission to access
• Installation or execution of unapproved software
• Access attempts with unauthorized devices
• Hardware or software inventory change; and

b. Reports findings to [Assignment: the IC System Owner, IC CIO, IC ISSO, and NIH CISO.]

Note: The analysis of audit records must be integrated with analysis of vulnerability scanning information; system monitoring information; and data/information collected from other sources (as appropriate) to further enhance the ability to identify inappropriate or unusual activity. Information from audit records must be correlated with information obtained from monitoring physical access to further enhance the ability to identify suspicious, inappropriate, unusual, or malevolent activity.

Current Implementation Details:

HUBzero relies on the Sherlock environment policies and procedures for this control.

 

AU-8 Time Stamps

The information system:

a. Uses internal system clocks to generate time stamps for audit records; and

b. Records time stamps for audit records that can be mapped to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) or Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) and is synchronized to within two (2) seconds of the relative reference clock.

Note: Per NIST SP 800-53, Rev 4 guidance, it is best practice select a secondary time source that is in a different geographic region. However, this is not explicitly required by this control.

Current Implementation Details:

HUBzero relies on the Sherlock environment policies and procedures for synchronizing internal system clocks.  All HUBzero logging mechanisms use internal system clocks to generate time stamps for audit records.

 

AU-9 Protection of Audit Information

The information system protects audit information and audit tools from unauthorized access, modification, and deletion.

Current Implementation Details:

The Sherlock SSP states that " Central log host access is restricted to Sherlock Security staff."  In addition, the HUBzero filesystem security model utilizes a role-based model to configure access permissions to protect audit information and audit tools from unauthorized access, modification and deletion.

AU-11 Audit Record Retention

The organization retains audit records for [Assignment: at least 30 days or longer if there is an after the fact investigation of security incidents to meet regulatory and organizational information retention requirements] to provide support for after-the-fact investigations of security incidents and to meet regulatory and organizational information retention requirements.

Current Implementation Details:

The Sherlock SSP states that " Sherlock System log records shall be kept for six years."  HUBzero policies comply with the above; see the policy "164.312 b Audit Control".

AU-12 Audit Generation

The information system:

a. Provides audit record generation capability for the auditable events defined in AU-2 a. at [Assignment: in AU-2 (d), at a minimum, for Servers, Databases, Applications, and Network components (e.g., switches, routers);;

b. Allows [Assignment: NIH and IC System Administrators, System Owners, Network Administrators, ISSOs, CIO, and NIH Threat Mitigation & Incident Response Team and NIH CISO.] to select which auditable events are to be audited by specific components of the information system; and

c. Generates audit records for the events defined in AU-2 d. with the content defined in AU-3.

Current Implementation Details:

The Sherlock SSP states that "systems are configured to provide a level of event logging to support the investigation of inappropriate activities. Audit records from Sherlock information system components are compiled into a system-wide audit trail that is time-correlated."  New HUBzero policies conform to this control but the implementation of AU-12 depends on completing the implementation of AU-2 and AU-3.

title: (CA) Security Assessment and Authorization
content:
See 164.308 Administrative Safeguards a 1 Security Management Process,

  • 164.308 a 1 ii (A) Risk Analysis
  • 164.308 a 1 ii (B) Risk Management
  • 164.308 a 1 ii (D) Information System Activity Review

(CA-1) Security Assessment and authorization policy and procedures

This policy is documented in the SDSC Sherlock System Security Plan. HUBzero has a master Information Security Policy documenting roles, responsibilities and management commitment, disseminated at the URL https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/itppr/master-information-security-policy.  Supporting policies and procedures implementing controls are documented in the "Information Technology Policies, Procedures and Resources" at https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/itppr. 

(CA-2) Security Assessments

HUBzero will lever the Sherlock assessments to include the HUBzero context whenever possible.  Failing that, separate assessments will be done, either by a third-party or as an internal self-assessment. 

(CA-3) System Interconnections

HUBzero is a web browser-based system and clients access it through existing browsers at the customer site.  HUBzero does not use system interconnections where an Interconnection Security Agreement would be meaningful (e.g., to other federal entities).  The system interconnections listed in Table 2-9 are internal to HUBzero and the Sherlock environment, and addressed by CA-9. 

(CA-5) Plan of Action and Milestones

A POA&M should be produced at the conclusion of the SA&A testing phase, and maintained on a regular basis to ensure identified weaknesses are remediated in accordance with agreed upon milestones. The POA&M will be updated quarterly based on the findings from security controls assessments, security impact analyses, and continuous monitoring activities.

Findings resulting from a security assessment, audit, vulnerability scan, etc. shall be documented as weaknesses in a relevant POA&M after the assessment/final audit report is approved, or the vulnerability scan report is produced, whether applicable to a system or a program, and tracked until remediated/mitigated.
Findings/weaknesses shall be documented in the POA&M and remediated/mitigated by the timelines below:
• Critical within 30 days;
• High within 60 days;
• Medium within 1 year; and
• Low within 1 year.
where HUBzero defines critical findings as those with a CVSS score greater than 9 on an internet-facing system (e.g., webserver).  For vulnerabilities detected by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) National Cybersecurity Assessments and Technical Services (NCATS) team, remediation/mitigation timelines specified in the HHS Memorandum Remediation of High DHS-Discovered Scan Based Vulnerabilities shall be implemented.

(CA-6) Security Authorization

A Security Plan detailing controls in place is developed as part of the hub's FISMA assessment and authorization. Authority to operate the hub will be granted by the Designated Approving Authority.  A HUBzero Science Gateway Manager will keep track of the current DAA's contact information, ensure that the DAA contact information in the Security Plan matches, and maintain a working relationship with the DAA.

The security authorization will be updated every three (3) years or when there is a significant change to the system (defined as significant change that is likely to affect the security state of that information system).

(CA-7) Continuous Monitoring

The policy "164.308 a 1 ii (D) Information System Activity Review" documents the continuous monitoring which is the responsibility of HUBzero. 

(CA-8) Penetration Testing

Not applicable for on-premises FISMA Low (note that it would be applicable for a cloud deployment).

(CA-9) Internal System Connections

HUBzero deployments require that "execution hosts" (an optional class of system component) be allowed to connect to the webserver (a required component) via the LDAP protocol, via NFS, and via SSH. The LDAP and NFS connections do not need to be encrypted if all hub components are within a very small network dedicated to that hub to the exclusion of all VMs or components that are not a part of the hub, and if the network is protected by a network firewall preventing external LDAP and NFS connections. Otherwise, LDAPS must be used instead, and additional mitigations deployed for NFS that are appropriate for the security requirements of the hub in question. Execution hosts must also be able to connect to designated external data sources for tool simulations, which vary depending on the hub.

Management hosts must be able to communicate with all hub hosts via SSH to run commands needed by the configuration management system(s) in use.  A management host typically serves for multiple hubs.

title: (CM) Configuration Management
content:
See:

  • Workforce security (management and configuration of access privileges):  https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/itppr/policies/mapping-to-national-standards-and-regulations/hipaa-view/164308-administrative-safeguards/a-3-workforce-security
  • Change management procedures:  https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/itppr/procedures/administrative/change-management-procedures
  • Configuration management system requirements:  https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/itppr/policies/configuration-management-system-requirements
  • Host configuration policy:  https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/itppr/policies/host-configuration-policy

CM-2 Baseline Configuration

Hubzero has documented the baseline configuration of HUBzero software in public documentation, using HUBzero packages.  HUBzero uses Ansible under revision control  for configuration control.  Ansible roles, playbooks, and inventory variables ("host_vars" and "group_vars") are all under git version control and should cover and describe all applicable configuration items, so that any host can be rebuilt identically by creating a new instance and running the applicable Ansible playbooks on it.  No configuration should be done manually outside of Ansible.

CM-4 Security Impact Analysis

"The organization analyzes changes to the information system to determine potential security impacts prior to change implementation."

The HUBzero change management procedures at https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/itppr/procedures/administrative/change-management-procedures explicitely address this control.

CM-6 Configuration Settings

The HUBzero Configuration Management System Requirements describe how configuration settings will be implemented, monitored and controlled.  HUBzero will review and verify configuration settings using security configuration checklists provided by NIH or NCI, using the suggested schedule, and will identify, document, and approve any deviations based on operational requirements.

CM-7 Least Functionality

HUBzero:

a. Configures the information system to provide only essential capabilities; and
b. Prohibits or restricts the use of the following functions, ports, protocols, and/or services:

  • Unencrypted traffic entering or leaving a specific hub's dedicated subnet, except:
    • HTTP traffic supporting redirect functionality to HTTPS services or serving public data
    • ICMP traffic required to support "MTU discovery"
    • ICMP ping and "ICMP host redirect" traffic within the SDSC network
    • Traffic used by monitoring systems such as PRTG
    • Read-only database (e.g., MySQL) services serving public data, restricted to authorized destinations or from authorized sources
  • Prohibited or Restricted list provided by NCI:
    • Domain Name System (DNS)
      • Port 53 / Transmission Control Protocol (TCP), User Datagram Protocol (UDP)
    • File Transfer Protocol (FTP)
      • Ports 20, 21 / TCP
    • Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP)
      • Port 80 / TCP
    • Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP)
      • Port 143 / TCP, UDP
    • Internet Relay Chat (IRC)
      • Port 194 / UDP
    • Network Basic Input Output System (NetBIOS)
      • Port 137 / TCP, UDP
    • Post Office Protocol 3 (POP3)
      • Port 110 / TCP
    • Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP)
      • Port 3389 / TCP
    • Network Time Protocol (NTP)
      • Port 123 / UDP
    • Secure Shell (SSH)
      • Port 22 / TCP
    • Server Message Block (SMB)
      • Ports 139 & 445 / TCP
      • Ports 137 & 138 / UDP
    • Session Initiation Protocol (SIP)
      • Port 5060 / TCP, UDP
    • Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP)
      • Port 25 / TCP
    • Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP)
      • Port 161 / TCP, UDP
    • Structured Query Language (SQL)
      • Port 118 / TCP, UDP
        Port 156 / TCP, UDP
        Port 1433 / TCP
        Port 1521 / TCP
    • Telnet
      • Port 23 / TCP

The configuration management system shall only install needed packages, shall support a blacklist of packages, and will configure information systems to provide only essential capabilities.  It will also prohibits or restricts the use of the functions, ports, protocols, and/or services that are not defined in a white list automatically derived from the host's declared functions, using host and network firewalls.

CM-11 User-Installed Software

Description:  "The organization:

a. Prohibits the installation of software by users on all government-furnished equipment (GFE).
b. Enforces software prohibition policies through:
    1. the monthly examination of user accounts,
    2. automated methods, and/or
    3. the collection of application inventory controls; and
c. Monitors policy compliance at least monthly.

Note: Policy enforcement methods include procedural methods (e.g., periodic examination of user accounts), automated methods (e.g., configuration settings implemented on organizational information systems), collection of application inventory controls, or a combination of these methods."

Possibly this control does not apply because the customized NCI description above is concerned only with “government-furnished equipment”,  and NCH and SDSC HUBzero staff don’t use any.  The only monitoring performed on NCH is by the anti-virus Sentinel One.  Besides that, NCH doesn’t monitor the software that users may have in their home directories.  Rules governing user-installed software:

  • Through the use of a NCH-provided tool session, users are allowed to compile or install software within the container environment only (e.g., in their home directories), provided  that it isn't flagged as malware by AV software.

title: (CP) Contingency Planning
content:
The Contingency Planning Policy and Procedures are documented in the SDSC Sherlock Contingency Plan, supplemented with the HUBzero Disaster Recovery and Business Continuity Plan for considerations particular to HUBzero science gateways.  The Sherlock SSP provides implementation details of the CP family of controls.

 

Procedures supporting contingency planning:

  • Restoring MySQL Databases
  • Ansible for Configuration Management, Provisioning and Disaster Recovery

title: (IA) Identification and Authentication
content:
HUBzero identification and authentication-related policies:

  • Account Management Policies at https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/itppr/policies/account-management
  • 164.312 a Access Control defines a "Unique user identification" policy at https://help.hubzero.org/groups/hubzero_hipaa/wiki/164312aAccessControl

HUBzero authentication-related procedures:

  • Account Management Procedures at https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/itppr/procedures/administrative/account-management-password-quality-resets-and-hashing--login-failures-and-bans
  • Access Request Procedure https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/itppr/procedures/administrative/access-request-procedure

NCH custom policies:  https://ncihub.org/projects/policies/notes


The SDSC Sherlock System Security Plan also describes the policies related to the IA control family.

IA-8 Identification and Authentication (Non-Organizational Users)

People can abuse a hub to by creating "spam" accounts, i.e., accounts abused to create blogs, profiles, projects or other content that promote some unrelated financial or illegal scheme, most often fraudulent.  One way to combat this is to limit the scope of account registration approval.  This can be phrased as "Email domains need to be screened during the account creation process."  One way to do that is, instead of auto-approving all accounts, accounts can be set to require manual approval, except accounts from some domains like .edu and .gov.  The plugin "User - Auto-Approve" ("autoapprove") can approve users with email addresses matching configurable domains:

 

Historical, for reference only: While at Purdue, HUBzero used Purdue's identification and authentication policy documented in the archived Authentication and Authorization (VII.B.1) which was superseded on July 15, 2019 by the standard on Authentication, Authorization and Access Controls (S-13).

title: (IR) Incident Response
content:
Most of the controls are addressed in the incident response plan.  Below are supplemental details.

IR-2 Incident Response Training

Control: The organization provides incident response training to information system users
consistent with assigned roles and responsibilities:
a.  Within [Assignment: organization-defined time period] of assuming an incident response role
    or responsibility;
b.  When required by information system changes; and
c.  [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] thereafter.

Training is provided within one month of assuming an incident response role or responsibility, when required, and as needed thereafter.

IR-5 Incident Monitoring

Control: "The organization tracks and documents information system security incidents."


Information system security incidents are tracked and documented in the ticketing system.  The ticketing system has features that support this, such as private comments visible only to the hub administrators, and the capability to only send notifications that a ticket was changed without emailing sensitive details or the comments themselves.  In addition, the ticketing system provides statistics at the "/support/stats" URL.

IR-8  Incident Response Plan

For HIPAA-covered hubs, the Sherlock Program maintains an Incident Response Plan that is distributed & updated yearly (if needed).  HUBzero also has and maintains an IRP for HUBzero science gateways, which will engage the Sherlock IRP whenever an incident exceeds the scope of the HUBzero software or whenever HUBzero staff have difficulty responding or require support from the Sherlock team.

Incident response for other hubs is also described in the HUBzero team's IRP.

title: (MA) Maintenance
content:
MA-1 System Maintenance Policy and Procedures

This policy is documented in the SDSC Sherlock System Security Plan, and supplemented by HUBzero policies and procedures documented at https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/itppr.  See in particular:

  • Ansible HUBzero CMS Update
  • Ansible for Configuration Management, Provisioning and Disaster Recovery
  • Code Deployment
  • Code Repository Policies
  • Git Deployment Process
  • Configuration Management System Requirements

MA-2 Controlled Maintenance

The SDSC Sherlock System Security Plan states that "Maintenance of Sherlock on premise and AWS Production systems, including system patching, will occur starting the third Tuesday of each month. No Sherlock equipment will be removed to perform maintenance offsite without Sherlock Program Management approval."

In addition, HUBzero maintains its software according to the "CMS Maintenance schedule" documented at https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/itppr/code-deployment .  Non-production hosts are patched one week ahead of schedule,  to detect problems before they reach production.

MA-4 Nonlocal Maintenance

Please refer to the SDSC Sherlock System Security Plan.  HUBzero has no additional policies and procedures for that control.

MA-5 Maintenance Personnel

Please refer to the SDSC Sherlock System Security Plan.  HUBzero has no additional policies and procedures for that control.

title: (MP) Media Protection
content:
This policy is documented in the SDSC Sherlock System Security Plan.  For HIPAA-covered hubs, HUBzero has no additional policies or procedures for these controls.

 

As HUBzero doesn't handle physical servers directly anymore, responsibility for this family of controls is delegated.  See also "164.310 Physical Safeguards, d Device and Media Controls"

For historical purposes, HUBzero also had this policy when handling physical servers:

(Historical) MP-6 MEDIA SANITIZATION

Control: The organization:
     a.  Sanitizes [Assignment: organization-defined information system media] prior to disposal, release out of organizational control, or release for reuse using [Assignment: organization-defined sanitization techniques and procedures] in accordance with applicable federal and organizational standards and policies; and
     b.  Employs sanitization mechanisms with the strength and integrity commensurate with the security category or classification of the information.

HUBzero’s media sanitization procedures are described in "Disposal for Electronic-Based Media" at https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/infosec/procedures/technical/disposal-for-electronic-based-media . These procedures satisfy the Purdue’s “Media Disposal Guidelines“ documented at https://www.purdue.edu/securepurdue/bestPractices/mediaDisposalGuidelines.html by using the “enhanced secure erase” or, if not available, “secure erase” hard drive functionality, or 3-pass DoD erasure, physically destructing storage devices or reusing media (after wiping) only within HUBzero. Hard drives replaced under warranty for servers with FISMA or HIPAA requirements are also subjected to the “enhanced secure erase” or “secure erase” operation, whenever possible, before shipping to Dell by courrier. However, these operations are not guaranteed to succeed on faulty drives. To maximize the likelihood of "secure erase"-type operations succeeding, whenever possible HUBzero replaces drives as soon as predictive failures are detected, before the device fails completely.

title: (PE) Physical and Environmental Protection
content: Controls PE-1 to PE-18 are addressed in the Sherlock environment as described in the Sherlock System Security Plan.  Please refer to it, as HUBzero uses these facilities unmodified.

title: (PL) Planning
content:
PL-1 Security Planning Policy and Procedures

Security planning policies and procedures are defined as found on hubzero.org documentation under "Information Technology Policies, Procedures and Resources".

PL-2 System Security Plan

System security plans (SSPs) appropriate to support FISMA certification of specific hubs will be developed from the NCI templates provided at https://wiki.nci.nih.gov/display/NSCI/FISMA+Security+Templates+and+Forms, and will be stored on hubzero.org and on the hub in question.  There can likely be variations between the plans of different hubs, due to different security requirements, FISMA certification levels, and assignments made to controls by the certifying federal organization, so multiple SSPs are to be expected, with a common core provided in this documentation.


The SSPs developed by HUBzero will build on the Sherlock SSP and will:

1. Be consistent with the organizations enterprise architecture;

2. Explicitly define the authorization boundary for the system;

3. Describe the operational context of the information system in terms of missions and business processes;

4. Provide the security categorization of the information system including supporting rationale;

5. Describe the operational environment for the information system and relationships with or connections to other information systems;

6. Provide an overview of the security requirements for the system;

7. Identify any relevant overlays, if applicable;

8. Describe the security controls in place or planned for meeting those requirements including a rationale for the tailoring decisions; and

9. Be reviewed and approved by the authorizing official or designated representative prior to plan implementation;

b. Be distributed, as well as subsequent changes, to the NIH CIO, CISO, System Owners, and NIH ISAO at the enterprise level and IC CIO, ISSO; System Owner, and IC InfoSec Program at the IC level;

c. Be reviewed every 365 days or when significant changes occur;

d. Be updated to address changes to the information system/environment of operation or problems identified during plan implementation or security control assessments; and

e. Be protected from unauthorized disclosure and modification.

PL-4 Rules of Behavior

"Control: The organization:
a.  Establishes and makes readily available to individuals requiring access to the information system, the rules that describe their responsibilities and expected behavior with regard to information and information system usage;
b.  Receives a signed acknowledgment from such individuals, indicating that they have read, understand, and agree to abide by the rules of behavior, before authorizing access to information and the information system;
c.  Reviews and updates the rules of behavior [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]; and
d.  Requires individuals who have signed a previous version of the rules of behavior to read and re-sign when the rules of behavior are revised/updated."

When users sign up for an account, they must agree to terms of use before they are granted an account. The implementation of signed acknowledgments is not feasible for non-organizational users. Instead, and in accordance with NIST 800-53, this control can be satisfied for non-organizational users through System Use Notification (AC-8) as well as through required security awareness training if such training includes rules of behavior.

title: (PS) Personnel Security
content:
PS-1 Personnel Security Policy and Procedures

SDSC HUBzero relies on SDSC Human Resources for personnel security, supplemented with additional procedures and policies as described below.  The Sherlock policy is documented in the SDSC Sherlock System Security Plan. SDSC complies with all UC San Diego and UC personnel controls and applicable federal and state laws and regulations.

PS-2 Position Risk Designation

All SDSC staff with access to the Sherlock environment are able to access the sensitive data hosted within the Sherlock environment, are therefore assigned the same risk designation, and are subject to background checks prior to system access. Per both Amazon and Microsoft, they conduct criminal background checks, as permitted by law, as part of pre-employment screening practices for employees and commensurate with the employee’s position and level of access.

PS-3 Personnel Screening

All SDSC staff with access to the Sherlock environment must first successfully pass an identity and criminal check prior to access approval. Per both Amazon and Microsoft, they conduct criminal background checks, as permitted by law, as part of pre-employment screening practices for employees and commensurate with the employee’s position and level of access.

HUBzero relies on SDSC's Human Resources policies and procedures.

PS-4 Personnel Termination

1. HUBzero Employees: Access privileges to the science gateway web application will be removed or disabled as soon as possible upon notification from an employee’s supervisor that the access is no longer needed.
2. Hub users with elevated privileges: Access credentials in the science gateway web application will be removed or disabled as soon as possible upon notification from a credible and authoritative source (e.g., the owner of a hub) that the access is no longer needed or that it should be withdrawn.  If applicable, HUBzero staff will notify Sherlock staff, via email, of any users who are terminated or transferred. Sherlock staff disable accounts within one business day of notification.
3. SDSC Employees: SDSC terminates information system access; conducts exit interviews; retrieves all security-related organizational information and system-related property; and retains access to organizational information and information systems formerly controlled by the terminated individual.

Detailed HUBzero termination procedures are documented at https://help.hubzero.org/groups/production/wiki/TerminationProcs

PS-5 Personnel Transfer

SDSC reviews logical and physical access authorizations to information systems/facilities when personnel are reassigned or transferred to other positions within the organization and ensures accurate assignment of privileges.  Additionally, this is addressed by HUBzero under the policy to grant and review access to systems. Personnel roles are defined in the webserver security model. Full details can be found at:

https://help.hubzero.org/groups/hubzero_hipaa/wiki/164308a3WorkforceSecurity

PS-6 Access Agreements

Sherlock policies are defined in the Sherlock SSP.  Hub users must agree to an initial terms of use, e.g., https://ncihub.org/aboutus/terms, which includes an Abuse Policy (see https://ncihub.org/legal/abuse).  Hubs have functionality to force users to agree again to the terms of use;  hub administrators can trigger this whenever the terms of use change, or every year.

PS-7 Third-Party Personnel Security

Any subcontractor with unsupervised access to the Sherlock environment is subject to the same background check requirements as SDSC staff.  HUBzero, as part of SDSC, utilizes the same HR procedures.

PS-8 Personnel Sanctions

SDSC staff are subject to sanctions, as defined in UC policy, if it is determined that they are non-compliant with Sherlock or HUBzero policies.

content:
(SA-1) System and Services Acquisition Policy and Procedures

Description in NCI template: "The organization:

Policy Handbook:
1. A system and services acquisition policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and

b. Reviews and, if necessary, updates the current:
1. System and services acquisition policy at least every three (3) years; and
2. System and services acquisition procedures at least every three (3) years."

Implementation Description:  All required federal acquisition security language is reviewed by the respective issuing government agency ISSO both in initial solicitation and contract award stages for compliance with FISMA, Section 508, and privacy requirements. Internally, Sherlock and HUBzero rely on the SDSC (San Diego Supercomputing Center) acquisition and procurement policies and procedures, supplemented with the policies and procedures described in the following subsections and in the Sherlock System Security Plan.

Historical 2016 text (for reference only): "All require (sic) federal acquisition security language is reviewed by the respective issuing government agency ISSO both in initial solicitation and contract award stages for compliance with FISMA, Section 508, and privacy requirements. Internally, HUBzero relies on Purdue acquisition and procurement policies and procedures and the Ariba purchasing system. A summary of these acquisition policies will be provided upon request."

(SA-2) Allocation of Resources

Description in NCI template: "The organization:

a. Determines information security requirements for the information system or information system service in mission/business process planning;

b. Determines, documents, and allocates the resources required to protect the information system or information system service as part of its capital planning and investment control process; and

c. Establishes a discrete line item for information security in organizational programming and budgeting documentation."

Implementation Description: (Partially in place) The decision to deploy hosted hubs in one of several available environments is based on security requirements.  Deploying HIPAA-covered hubs in the security-oriented Sherlock environment results in the proper resources being determined, documented and allocated for NCIhub.  HUBzero has a line item for the Sherlock environment.  However, HUBzero doesn't have a discrete line item covering information security in organizational programming and budgeting documentation, separate from the Sherlock environment. 

Historical 2016 text (for reference only): "HUBzero must determine information security requirements for the information system with respect to mission/business process planning. Organizational programming and budgeting documentation must have a discrete line item for information security. Renewal documents for NCIPhub will contain a line item for charges in information security."

(SA-3) Life Cycle Support

Description in NCI template: "The organization:

a. Manages the information system using [Assignment: a formally defined and documented system development life cycle (SDLC) process] that incorporates information security considerations;

b. Defines and documents information security roles and responsibilities throughout the system development life cycle;

c. Identifies individuals having information security roles and responsibilities; and

d. Integrates the organizational information security risk management process into system development life cycle activities.

Note: The organization may formally define and document its own SDLC process; however, at a minimum, the process must conform to HHS Department-wide SDLC requirements (including the HHS Enterprise Performance Life Cycle (EPLC)). The organization may adopt the Department-wide SDLC or customize it to meet additional, organization-specific requirements."

Implementation Description:  HUBzero has a batch and revision process to push code to production.  The code deployment schedule is documented at https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/itppr/code-deployment and the code deployment itself is automated with an Ansible playbook. Code repository policies are documented at https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/itppr/coderepospolicies and define which code repositories are approved for use, and which are publicly accessible.

Individuals having information security roles and responsibilities are identified in the Incident Response Plan and the Emergency Contact Information document.  The integration of security risk management into the SDLC activities consist of:

  • All software is managed by a version control system.
  • The web application scanner "Detectify" (detectify.com) is employed monthly and before every major release.
  • Yearly Sherlock audits include a scan of the NCIhub science gateway.

Sherlock's management of the underlying infrasctructure and operating systems uses monthly package updates and reboots, staggered between non-production systems and production systems.

Historical 2016 text (for reference only): "HUBzero has a batch and revision process to push to production. All software is managed by a version control system. IBM Appscan is employed before every major release. Yearly audits include a scan of the site."

(SA-4) Acquisition Process

Description in NCI template: "The organization includes the following requirements, descriptions, and criteria, explicitly or by reference, in the acquisition contract for the information system, system component, or information system service in accordance with applicable federal laws, Executive Orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards, guidelines, and organizational mission/business needs:

a. Security functional requirements;

b. Security strength requirements;

c. Security assurance requirements;

d. Security-related documentation requirements;

e. Requirements for protecting security-related documentation;

f. Description of the information system development environment and environment in which the system is intended to operate; and

g. Acceptance criteria.

Note: Required security configurations and settings should also be included (see SA-4 c.e.5).
"

Explanation: This is about providing to the hub owner documentation describing the properties of the security controls to be employed within the hub, in sufficient detail to permit analysis and testing of the controls.

Implementation Description: SDSC HUBzero will provide to the hub owner the hub's system security plan, configuration management plan, system diagram, data flow diagram, and contingency plan, which will cover the above
