title: Restoring LDAP service
content:
The LDAP service is provided by slapd.  Every day we dump the LDAP database to /var/ldap/dump_all.ldif.gz.

Reload the LDAP server (slapd) from a backup or dump:

This assumes that Ogre setup files in /etc/ldap and /etc/default/slapd.  If Ogre isn't running, first restore /etc/ldap and /etc/default from backups.

/etc/init.d/slapd stop
# create a new copy and save the old one just in case
rm /var/lib/oldldap -rf 
mv /var/lib/ldap /var/lib/oldldap
mkdir /var/lib/ldap
# we need DB_CONFIG
cp /var/lib/oldldap/DB_CONFIG /var/lib/ldap
# load from the last dump
gunzip --to-stdout /var/ldap/dump_all.ldif.gz | slapadd
chown -R openldap:openldap /var/lib/ldap
/etc/init.d/slapd start

Load from a file:

/etc/init.d/slapd stop
# create a new copy and save the old one just in case
mv /var/lib/ldap /var/lib/oldldap
mkdir /var/lib/ldap
# we need DB_CONFIG
cp /var/lib/oldldap/DB_CONFIG /var/lib/ldap
# Load from this file:
slapadd -l /root/ldap.toload
chown -R openldap:openldap /var/lib/ldap
/etc/init.d/slapd start

Save, change, and reload:

/etc/init.d/slapd stop
slapcat > /root/ldap.dump
cp /root/ldap.dump /root/ldap.toload
vi /root/ldap.toload

then reload as above.

title: Hubadmin passwordless SSH login to stage
content:
This procedure aims to support CMS updates.  Time required:  about 30 minutes/hub

0. Which hub is this?

Identify the hub and hubset for later commands.  Logon control.hubzero.org and use these commands or similar:
 

hub=catalyzecare.org
hubset=catalyzecare
home=`ssh root@$hub getent passwd hubadmin | cut -d ":" -f6`
grab-ogre $hub dev.$hub stage.$hub

1. Verify hubadmin's home makes sense

If this hub uses NFS, change hubadmin's home to /home/hubadmin on production, dev and stage so it's not shared over NFS or otherwise exposed to attacks from the network.  User hubadmin usually has an entry in /etc/passwd, but may also have a redundant entry in the CMS and in LDAP.

echo $home
# if needed:
# change home directory to /home/hubadmin

# create the directory on both production and dev:

ssh root@$hub "mkdir -p /home/hubadmin/.ssh/"
ssh root@$hub "chown hubadmin:public -R /home/hubadmin"
ssh root@$hub "chmod 700 /home/hubadmin"
ssh root@$hub "chmod 700 /home/hubadmin/.ssh/"

ssh root@dev.$hub "mkdir -p /home/hubadmin/.ssh/"
ssh root@dev.$hub "chown hubadmin:public -R /home/hubadmin"
ssh root@dev.$hub "chmod 700 /home/hubadmin"
ssh root@dev.$hub "chmod 700 /home/hubadmin/.ssh/"

ssh root@stage.$hub "mkdir -p /home/hubadmin/.ssh/"
ssh root@stage.$hub "chown hubadmin:public -R /home/hubadmin"
ssh root@stage.$hub "chmod 700 /home/hubadmin"
ssh root@stage.$hub "chmod 700 /home/hubadmin/.ssh/"

# Change hubadmin account info
vi /etc/passwd
# getent passwd hubadmin
hubadmin:x:1000:3000:Hub Admin User:/home/hubadmin:/bin/bash
# login to /administrator to make sure CMS information matches

2. SSH key for production hubadmin

# Create hubadmin.pub or import it from production
# if needed create a key pair on production
ssh root@$hub "su hubadmin -c 'ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 3072 -f /home/hubadmin/.ssh/id_rsa'"

# store it as the public key for the set
scp $hub:/home/hubadmin/.ssh/id_rsa.pub /usr/share/adm/ogre/secret/sets/$hubset/hubadmin.pub

# allow only logins from production -- quotes should be escaped for the "from=" option
sed -i "s/^/from="$hub" /" /usr/share/adm/ogre/secret/sets/$hubset/hubadmin.pub

# verify that the "from" looks correct in the public key -- watch out for missing quotes
cat /usr/share/adm/ogre/secret/sets/$hubset/hubadmin.pub

# Check number of bits in key.  If less than 2048 regenerate it:
ssh-keygen -l -f /usr/share/adm/ogre/secret/sets/$hubset/hubadmin.pub

3. SSH key for dev hubadmin

The process is similar to that for production.

scp dev.$hub:$home/.ssh/id_rsa.pub /usr/share/adm/ogre/secret/sets/$hubset/devhubadmin.pub
if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
  # create new key pair
  ssh root@dev.$hub "su hubadmin -c 'ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 3072 -f /home/hubadmin/.ssh/id_rsa'"
  scp dev.$hub:/home/hubadmin/.ssh/id_rsa.pub /usr/share/adm/ogre/secret/sets/$hubset/devhubadmin.pub
  # allow only logins from dev -- quotes should be escaped for the "from=" option
  sed -i "s/^/from="dev.$hub" /" /usr/share/adm/ogre/secret/sets/$hubset/devhubadmin.pub
fi
# verify the "from" option in the public key -- watch out for missing quotes
cat /usr/share/adm/ogre/secret/sets/$hubset/devhubadmin.pub

# Check number of bits in key.  If less than 2048 regenerate it as above:
ssh-keygen -l -f /usr/share/adm/ogre/secret/sets/$hubset/devhubadmin.pub

4. Ogre configuration

The following modifies stage's configuration in /usr/share/adm/ogre/private/config/hosts/stage.$hub.  As a result /etc/security/access.conf gets modified to allow hubadmin logins from dev and prod, and the authorized_keys file for hubadmin on stage is created or updated.

hubip=`host $hub | cut -d ' ' -f4`
devip=`host dev.$hub | cut -d ' ' -f4`
if [ -e /usr/share/adm/ogre/private/config/hosts/stage.$hub.def ]; then
  echo "@define HUBADMIN_LOGINS '$hubip $devip'" >> /usr/share/adm/ogre/private/config/hosts/stage.$hub.def
  echo "@define HUBADMIN_KEYFILES {}" >> /usr/share/adm/ogre/private/config/hosts/stage.$hub.def
  echo "@append HUBADMIN_KEYFILES 'hubadmin.pub'" >> /usr/share/adm/ogre/private/config/hosts/stage.$hub.def
  echo "@append HUBADMIN_KEYFILES 'devhubadmin.pub'" >> /usr/share/adm/ogre/private/config/hosts/stage.$hub.def
else
  echo no stage
fi

# verify
grep HUBADMIN_LOGINS /usr/share/adm/ogre/private/config/hosts/stage.$hub.def
grep HUBADMIN_KEYFILES /usr/share/adm/ogre/private/config/hosts/stage.$hub.def

There is no need to add hubadmin manually to the line @define MEMBER_HOSTLOGIN, it should already be in the access-host group.

5. Push configuration

preflight

iro stage.$hub

 

6. Test

 

First set some variables so you can use the commands below.  Repeat this on both dev and stage:


hub=catalyzecare.org
hubset=catalyzecare
home=`getent passwd hubadmin | cut -d ":" -f6`

a) On production:
# ssh -i $home/.ssh/id_rsa hubadmin@stage.$hub
All activity on this system is subject to HUBzero policies and procedures.
Last login: Wed Jun 28 15:47:24 2017 from control.hubzero.org
stage ~ logout

b) On dev:
# ssh -i $home/.ssh/id_rsa hubadmin@stage.$hub

(you should see output like the above)

title: Debian-Specific
content:
Software Updates

On control.hubzero.org, run the scripts /root/bin/patch_pkgs to patch infrastructure systems and restart services on non-production hosts.  Run /root/bin/patch_production to patch production hosts.  Do this every business day as early as possible during the day because usage is low at that time.

/boot gets full

Sometimes software updates install new kernels and fill up /boot, causing yellow or red alerts. This command will remove extra, unneeded kernels that can consume all the space on /boot. This removes all kernels except the one running and the most recent installed one besides the one running:

aptitude  --disable-columns search linux-image | grep '^i A' | sort -V | grep -v `uname -r` | head -n -2 | awk ' { print $3 }' | xargs aptitude purge -y

The above uses "n-2" to make sure it won't delete the most recent, just installed kernel that's not active yet.  This could happen with n-1 when you have more than one kernel series installed, e.g., linux-image-3.16.0-6-amd64 and linux-image-openvz-amd64.

The sort by version is necessary so that “stab120.18” is listed after “stab120.6” and doesn’t get purged.

nanoHUB Secondary Package Update Problems

Because several filesystems are read-only on the secondary, packages that expect to be able to modify them fail to install.  Also, packages that expect Apache to restart (e.g., hubzero-trac) fail to install.

hubzero-filexfer-xlate

It fails to install because:

chown: changing ownership of '/var/log/filexfer-xlate': Read-only file system

Fix:

nanohub2:~# zfs set readonly=off localzfs/varshared
nanohub2:~# dpkg --configure -a
nanohub2:~# zfs set readonly=on localzfs/varshared

hubzero-trac or "Apache unpacked but not yet configured."

It fails to install because:

Job for apache2.service failed. See 'systemctl status apache2.service' and 'journalctl -xn' for details.
invoke-rc.d: initscript apache2, action "force-reload" failed.


Fix:

# delete all Include except /etc/apache2/sites-available/hub
if [ -f /etc/i_am_secondary ]; then
  sed -i 's/128.46.19.160/127.0.0.1/' /etc/apache2/sites-available/*
  sed -i '/hub-webdav/d' /etc/apache2/apache2.conf
  sed -i '/hub-ssl/d' /etc/apache2/apache2.conf
  mkdir -p /var/log/apache_temp/
  sed -i 's#/var/log/apache2#/var/log/apache_temp#g' /etc/apache2/apache2.conf
  sed -i 's#/var/log/apache2#/var/log/apache_temp#g' /etc/apache2/sites-available/hub
  sed -i '/nanohub.conf.d/d' /etc/apache2/sites-available/hub
fi
/etc/init.d/apache2 stop
/etc/init.d/apache2 start
# install the packages
dpkg --configure -a
/etc/init.d/apache2 stop
# restore the configuration
ogre

Put or Remove a hold on packages

To hold a list of packages to the installed version and prevent updates, do:

tohold="package1 package2 ..."
for p in $tohold ; do 
  echo "$p hold" | dpkg --set-selections
done
aptitude -q hold $tohold

To force a package upgrade, do:

apt-get install $tohold

or:

aptitude unhold $tohold
aptitude install $tohold

To install a specific version, do:

apt-get install package=version

To check which packages are held:

dpkg --get-selections | grep hold
aptitude search ~ahold

Failed to fetch ... Hash Sum mismatch

If the mirror is OK and only one host is affected, reset apt by doing:

apt-get clean
apt-get update -o Acquire::CompressionTypes::Order::=gz
/usr/share/adm/scripts/auto_apt

title: Building Render Servers
content:
To do: Updated copy of what's at https://nanohub.org/infrastructure/rappture/wiki/BuildingRenderServer

See also 

render_nvidia_driver_x86_64-384.59_gcc-4.8_install.sh    
  render_server_release_20170203.sh

at https://github.com/hubzero/hapi

Render servers won’t work while the console is active. When connecting a crash cart to a render server, the procedure is to connect to one of the graphics cards. Onboard video can’t be enabled due to software conflicts. Then, switch the virtual console 1. When done, the VT must be switched back to 7 or else the render server won’t work.

Upgrades

Render server upgrades must be coupled with driver upgrades for the Nvidia GPUs. See the documentation on Rappture.

Preventing Upgrades

tohold=`aptitude --disable-columns search linux-headers linux-image mesa | grep ^i | sed 's/i..//' | awk '{print $1}'`
for p in xorg xserver-xorg xorg-dev xserver-xorg-core xserver-xorg-dev $tohold; do 
  echo "$p hold" | dpkg --set-selections
done
aptitude -q hold xorg xserver-xorg xorg-dev xserver-xorg-core xserver-xorg-dev $tohold

Verify Held Packages

Aptitude and dpkg should return the same list:

dpkg --get-selections | grep hold
aptitude search ~ahold

Forcing Upgrades

tohold=`aptitude --disable-columns search linux-headers linux-image mesa | grep ^i | sed 's/i..//' | awk '{print $1}'` 
apt-get install xorg xserver-xorg xorg-dev xserver-xorg-core xserver-xorg-dev $tohold

Or

aptitude unhold $tohold
aptitude install $tohold

title: Ansible and Hubadmin
content:
Ansible can run playbooks on production hosts by using the system automation account "hubadmin".  To allow people to control the hubadmin account, public keys are added to the authorized_keys file on the hosts.  For HIPAA hubs, Ansible runs on control.hubzero.org.  For other hubs it runs from lando.aws.hubzero.org.

 

Create an account on lando.aws.hubzero.org

Described elsewhere?

Create an account on control.hubzero.org

 

name=zooley
uname=su-$name
adduser --home /home/$uname --disabled-login --ingroup staff --shell /bin/bash  $uname
mkdir -p /home/$uname/.ssh/
chmod go-rwx /home/$uname/.ssh/
chown $uname:staff /home/$uname/.ssh/
cat /usr/share/adm/ogre/private/content/$name.key.pub > /home/$uname/.ssh/authorized_keys
chmod go-rwx /home/$uname/.ssh/authorized_keys
chown $uname:staff  /home/$uname/.ssh/authorized_keys

# immediately allow SSH logins (need to add to MEMBER_HOSTLOGIN to make this permanent)
usermod -aG access-host $uname

# disable password-based logins
passwd -l $uname
chage --mindays 7 $uname

Modify the Ogre configuration for control.hubzero.org.def:

  1. Add the user to the MEMBER_HOSTLOGIN variable to allow SSH logins
  2. Add the user to the NO_LDAP_EXCEPTIONS to stop alerts about an unexpected home directory

@define MEMBER_HOSTLOGIN "su-kwojo314,su-pmeunier,su-zachweidner,su-zooley"
@define NO_LDAP_EXCEPTIONS "-e su-kwojo314 -e su-pmeunier -e su-zachweidner -e su-zooley -e lost+found"

Create SSH key pairs for automation

The user should communicate an SSH key pair for each of lando and control:


vi /usr/share/adm/ogre/private/content/su-zooley-lando.pub
vi /usr/share/adm/ogre/private/content/su-zooley-control.pub
Prefix the key for control with from="128.46.19.9".

Configure Ogre to include the keys in hubadmin authorized_keys

On control, prepare to modify the configuration of all the hosts setup for Ansible control through hubadmin:

cd /root/.predict
grab-ogre `grep -l HUBADMIN_KEYFILES *`

In /usr/share/adm/ogre/private/config/classes/defaults.def there is a condition for HIPAA hosts.  Add line like this for HIPAA hosts:
@append HUBADMIN_KEYFILES 'su-zooley-control.pub'

and like that for others:

@append HUBADMIN_KEYFILES 'su-zooley-lando.pub'

RHEL hosts running OpenVZ, where production and qa are OpenVZ containers (e.g., purr.ogre.hubzero.org), need to have:

@define HUBADMIN_LOGINS " "

It works by triggering a case in /usr/share/adm/ogre/private/config/classes/defaults.def to set default values for HUBADMIN_KEYFILES and HUBADMIN_LOGINS, allowing access from both Lando and control.   In the case of HIPAA-covered hosts like ncip2.ogre.hubzero.org, if FLAG_HIPAA_SERVER is defined only logins from control.hubzero.org are allowed.

 

 

Test the configuration with "preflight", when ready push the configuration with "release-ogre".

 

Testing and Debugging

This should work:

su-zooley@control:~/.ssh$ ssh hubadmin@ncip2.ogre.hubzero.org
All activity on this system is subject to HUBzero and NCIPhub
policies and procedures.
[hubadmin@ncip2:PRODUCTION:~]$

as well as:

su-zooley@control:~/.ssh$ ansible-playbook playbooks/sync_qa.yml --limit=ncip2.ogre.hubzero.org

 

Make sure that "getent passwd hubadmin" agrees with the directory where the authorized_keys file is put.  For example, if Ogre puts it at "/home/hubadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys" but

ncip2:~/.ssh# getent passwd hubadmin
hubadmin:x:1000:3000:hubadmin:/home/nciphub/hubadmin:/bin/bash

Then it's not going to work.  The fix is to go in /administrator for the hub and change the home directory for user hubadmin.

title: Dataviewer:  Databases within Projects
content:
Databases within projects are also known as "dataviewer".  This is a plugin called "Projects - Databases".  This software uses different database users, one to write, and one to view data. 

Setting up dataviewer

 

# /usr/bin/hzcms configure dataviewer --enable
enabling dataviewer
creating database user: dataviewer, password = ...
creating database user: datawriter, password = ...

 

The above should setup the passwords also, which can be verified by looking at  /administrator -> Plug-in Manager: Plug-ins -> Projects - Databases

This should do something equivalent to: 

function generate() {
  openssl rand -base64 15
}

function rand_alnum() {
  generate | sed 's/[^a-zA-Z0-9]//g' | cut -c1-16
}

MYSQL_PASS_VIEW=`rand_alnum`
MYSQL_PASS_WRITE=`rand_alnum`

echo run the echoed statements below in MySQL and copy the passwords into Plug-in Manager: Databases
echo "GRANT USAGE ON *.* TO 'dataviewer'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY '$MYSQL_PASS_VIEW';"
echo "GRANT SELECT ON `prj_db_%`.* TO 'dataviewer'@'localhost';"

echo "GRANT USAGE ON *.* TO 'datawriter'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY '$MYSQL_PASS_WRITE';"
echo "GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, DROP ON `prj_db_%`.* TO 'datawriter'@'localhost';"

echo "flush privileges;"

 

Symptoms that this needs to be setup:

Log entries in /var/log/syslog like:

Sep 22 11:32:14 dev.qubeshub.org mysqld: 170922 11:32:14 [Warning] Access denied for user 'datawriter'@'localhost' (using password: YES)

title: MySQL
content:
See also the policy on database accounts.

See Backups for how to restore MySQL Databases

Performance

MySQL queries by the CMS should not take more than 4 seconds. Slow queries should be logged. The relevant my.cnf settings are:

slow_query_log = 1

slow_query_log_file = /var/log/mysql/mysql-slow.log

long_query_time = 4

This matters because NetForecast’s APDEX uses 4 seconds as the dividing line as to where users become frustrated.  This is not a policy but an operational guideline, and the above is to help meet that guideline.

Security

See the network services policy for details of which access method is appropriate.

Access to Existing MySQL Accounts

Direct remote access to a MySQL account requires SSL to protect the connection.  The MySQL account is protected by setting mysql.user.ssl_type to a value like “ANY”.  Our production MySQL servers use our own CA;  the CA certificate is copied on every host, as it's the same that supports Bacula backups.  The client software must use a copy of that certificate to verify the connection to the server.

Remote Access through SSH

With this method, SSH to an account on the OS, provides security to an otherwise insecure connection to a MySQL account.  This uses "SSH port forwarding".

  • SSH port forwarding can be done with a command like this one, which puts SSH in the background without executing a remote command: 
    ssh -f user@hostname -L 2000:127.0.0.1:3306 -N
    Then connect with the MySQL client of your choice to port 2000 on your local machine (use a different port for every destination) 
    mysql -p -h 127.0.0.1 --port=2000
  • Dedicated OS accounts can be created solely for the purpose of protecting a MySQL connection.
useradd -c "MySQL tunneling" --no-user-group --base-dir /hometunneler --create-home --shell /bin/rbash pascalmysqltun

The dedicated account is prevented from getting a terminal or doing much by using restrictive options for the SSH keys in authorized_keys file:

from="dev29.hubzero.org",command="/bin/false",no-pty,no-X11-forwarding,permitopen="127.0.0.1:3306"

on a remote client:

ssh -f pascalmysqltun@bfd -L 2000:127.0.0.1:3306 -N 
mysql -p -h 127.0.0.1 --port=2000

 

Grant Read-only MySQL access to Hub users

See this administrative procedure

Useful queries

select user, host, password, ssl_type from user;

select user, host, db, Insert_priv from db;

select user, host, db, Table_name, Table_priv from tables_priv;

Useful references

  • http://www.percona.com/files/white-papers/preventing-mysql-emergencies.pdf

They recommend not using views, temporary tables (we use statement-based binary logging and replication), the query cache, etc…

Fixing Corrupted Tables

Sometimes tables are repeatedly reported as corrupted. This may happen a few days or a week after running “/usr/bin/mysqlcheck —auto-repair -A”. That command is not able to repair everything, and will not report what it can’t fix. In that case the best action is to dump the table and reload it. For example:

mysqldump -a --events --routines -e habricentral jos_xgroups > /var/backups/habricentral.jos_xgroups;  mysql habricentral < /var/backups/habricentral.jos_xgroups

or

dbname=ccehub
table=jos_content
echo "mysqldump -a --events --routines -e $dbname $table > /var/backups/${dbname}.${table}; mysql $dbname < /var/backups/${dbname}.${table}"
mysqldump -a --events --routines -e $dbname $table > /var/backups/${dbname}.${table}; mysql $dbname < /var/backups/${dbname}.${table}

Replication

Setting up replication with an LVM Snapshot

The file /usr/share/adm/scripts/mysql-replication-setup-onLVM contains copy/paste-able commands that will setup replication between nanohub2 and nanohub3 (or vice-versa). The idea is to create an LVM snapshot of the MySQL files, while holding a read lock. Then the snapshot is mounted, rsync’ed, and replication is started on the slave.

Example: Use "screen" to start the script on nanohub3.ogre with:

/usr/share/adm/scripts/mysql-replication-setup-onLVM nanohub2.ogre.hubzero.org

title: Setting up DMARC, DKIM and SPF for mail
content:
The relevant policy for this procedure is the Host Configuration Policy

First you should setup DMARC with a "none" policy so no action will be taken in case SPF or DKIM are misconfigured or missing SPF permissions.  Only after running from some time with "none" and no legitimate emails being flagged, should the policy changed to "quarantine".

Verification of DKIM and SPF from "Report domain:" emails sent by Google and other providers:

  • Create directory with date

  • Save attachments from all Report domain emails

  • Upload all reports to https://us.dmarcian.com/xml-to-human-converter/

  • Examine anything that's not 100%, create tickets as needed

  • It may help to check that the DKIM records appear correct in DNS by using
    https://dmarcian.com/dkim-inspector/

     

UPDATE (July 20, 2020): operations equivalent to those described below are now performed at SDSC with the Ansible role "hubzero.opendkim".

Setting up DMARC for the first time

Add a TXT record in DNS for that domain (right near the top below the A record for the domain), specifying a "none" policy, and where to send reports:

_dmarc                  IN TXT "v=DMARC1; p=none; sp=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@help.hubzero.org; pct=100; ri=86400"


Upload reports to dmarcian to present them in human-readable form.  Make sure that hubzero.org is setup to accept reports from that domain, by adding a DNS record like this one, where "nanohub.org" should be replaced by the name of the new domain:

nanohub.org._report._dmarc.help    IN TXT "v=DMARC1"

Setting up SPF

Add a TXT record for every host that needs to send mail.  There are 2 cases:

  1. Send email as originating from the domain itself. 
  2. Send email as originating from a subdomain.

A simple example for the first case would be for citscibio.org:

@                       TXT     "v=spf1 +ip4:128.46.21.119 -all"

Where 128.46.21.119 is the IP address for citscibio.org and no other host is allowed to send mail.  There is no MX record because the host that receives mail is the same as the domain host, so the TXT record for SPF doesn't specify "+mx".  Verify the validity of the record by using "SPF Record Testing Tools".

An example of the second type, to allow ccehub.ogre.hubzero.org (a subdomain of hubzero.org) to send mail, this TXT record is added after the A record:

ccehub.ogre             A       128.46.22.50
ccehub.ogre             TXT     "v=spf1 +mx:hubzero.org +ip4:128.46.22.50 -all"

It allows the mx for hubzero.org, help.ogre.hubzero.org, to relay mail for ccehub.ogre.hubzero.org.  It also allows ccehub.ogre.hubzero.org to send mail directly.  Execution hosts should get SPF records in order to send alerts to administrators.  There should be no need to setup SPF records for "extra" hostnames like proxy.hubzero.org.


Use the DMARC reports to figure out if you need to add more records.

 Setting up DKIM

The overall process is:

  • Create a key pair (e.g., /etc/exim4/dkim2.private.key and /etc/exim4/dkim2.public.key, see below).  Note that keys longer than 1024 bits need to be broken up on separate lines.
  • Put the public key in a TXT DNS record
  • Put the private key in exim4's configuration (or whichever MTA you use)
  • On our systems, set the Ogre variable EXIM_DKIM so exim signs emails

The following commands, when run on control.hubzero.org, will create the key pair, and output the public key in the format needed by our DNS server (note, backslashes are missing due to a /documentation bug)

domain=nciphub.org
hostname=ncip.ogre.hubzero.org
cd /usr/share/adm/ogre/secret/hosts/${hostname}
openssl genrsa -out /usr/share/adm/ogre/secret/hosts/${hostname}/${domain}.dkim.key 2048
openssl rsa -in /usr/share/adm/ogre/secret/hosts/${hostname}/${domain}.dkim.key -pubout -out /usr/share/adm/ogre/secret/hosts/${hostname}/${domain}.dkim.pub
(
echo put the following in /etc/bind/chroot/etc/bind/master/db.${domain}
echo Backslashes are missing from this script due to issues with the documentation escaping mechanism
echo do not use as is
#echo -e "mail._domainkeytIN TXT" '(' "v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p="
#while read line; do
#  echo $line | grep -q PUBLIC
#  if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
#    echo -e "ttt"$line""
#  fi
#done < /usr/share/adm/ogre/secret/hosts/${hostname}/${domain}.dkim.pub
#echo ')'
)

Also add this TXT record in DNS, which means "some e-mails from this domain are signed".  This allows the SPF test to succeed when emails aren't signed.  We require either signed emails or a successful SPF test.

_domainkey              IN TXT "o=~"

 

Setting up DMARC

Add a TXT record in DNS for that domain, specifying the policy (none, quarantine, reject), and other options like where to send reports:

_dmarc                  IN TXT "v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; sp=quarantine; rua=mailto:dmarc@help.hubzero.org; ruf=mailto:dmarc@help.hubzero.org; pct=100; ri=604800"

Mailman Compatibility

For all mailing lists, set the dmarc_moderation_action to "Wrap Message", in the Privacy, sender filters section (privacy/sender).  The mailing list will send emails originating from a different host that has a DMARC policy, as an attachment to the mailing list.  This prevents breaking the DKIM signature.  Emails generated on the host will not be sent as attachments, they will be sent as normal.  Emails sent from domains without DMARC policies will also be sent as normal.  This script can help:

# current status:

for l in `/usr/sbin/list_lists -b`; do
  echo $l
  /usr/sbin/config_list --outputfile - $l | grep ^dmarc
  echo
done

# change dmarc_moderation_action to "Wrap Message"
for l in `/usr/sbin/list_lists -b`; do
  echo $l
  rm -f "/root/${l}"
  echo "/usr/sbin/config_list --outputfile - $l | sed 's/^dmarc_moderation_action.*$/dmarc_moderation_action = 2/' > /root/$l"
  /usr/sbin/config_list --outputfile - $l | sed 's/^dmarc_moderation_action.*$/dmarc_moderation_action = 2/' > "/root/${l}"
  grep ^dmarc_moderation_action "/root/${l}"
  if [ $? -eq 0 ] && [ -f "/root/${l}" ]; then
    /usr/sbin/config_list -i "/root/${l}" ${l}
  fi
  echo
done

Testing

Send an email to yourself through Google, e.g., on the hub being tested, run:

echo "testing DMARC/DKIM/SPF" | mail -s "test for `hostname`" pmeunier100@gmail.com

In the raw source of the email you receive, there will be a header like "ARC-Authentication-Results".  This example indicates a failure of DKIM and a successful SPF test:

 ARC-Authentication-Results: i=1; mx.google.com; spf=pass (google.com:
 domain of root@diagrid.org designates 128.46.21.43 as permitted sender)
 smtp.mailfrom=root@diagrid.org; dmarc=pass (p=NONE sp=NONE dis=NONE)
 header.from=diagrid.org

Whereas this one indicates success for both DKIM and SPF:

 ARC-Authentication-Results: i=1; mx.google.com; dkim=pass
 header.i=@citscibio.org header.s=mail header.b=YSXYMd41; spf=pass
 (google.com: domain of root@citscibio.org designates 128.46.21.119 as
 permitted sender) smtp.mailfrom=root@citscibio.org; dmarc=pass (p=NONE
 sp=NONE dis=NONE) header.from=citscibio.org

Troubleshooting Ideas

Did you:

  • add "@define EXIM_DKIM" in the host.def Ogre configuration file?
  • push the Ogre config ("iro")?
  • restart exim (/etc/init.d/exim4 restart?)

title: Termination Procedures
content:
The policy pertaining to these termination procedures is https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/itppr/policies/termination-policy


These procedures does not deal with physical assets (e.g., keys and equipment), for which UCSD policies and procedures should be followed.  Several people may need to cooperate to complete each section of this procedure, depending on who has administrative rights.

The old wiki version is at https://help.hubzero.org/groups/production/wiki/TerminationProcs

Ansible Operating System Management (SDSC RDS and AWS environments)

  1. Connect to the UCSD VPN
  2. SSH to the SDSC RDS management host
  3. Update your Ansible copy with "git pull"
  4. In the file "roles/sdsc.user_management/defaults/main.yml" add the username to the list "obsolete_users:"
    • In the same file, remove the user from the list "default_users:"
  5. In the file "roles/hubzero.aws_user_management/defaults/main.yml" repeat the previous step
  6. Run the playbook "hubzero/user_management.yml" on all hosts accessible from the RDS management host
  7. Edit the Ansible inventory
    • grep for all instances of the username and remove it from the inventory, especially in the file inventories/group_vars/all/access-control.yml
    • run the playbook "hubzero/access-groups.yml" (this can be delayed until the end of the next step)
    • remove IP addresses associated with this user to grant access to nonprod hosts
    • If any IP addresses were removed, run the roles:
      • hubzero.hubzero-apache2
      • hubzero.iptables
      • hubzero.mailman
  8. Edit the playbook file "hubzero/access-groups.yml":
    • Remove the username from the list "access_roles:" and anywhere else it might appear
    • Run the role on all hosts
  9. Commit all the changes to git
  10. Disconnect from UCSD VPN

AWS

  • Check if an account exists for that person
  • delete the account in AWS IAM control panel
  • remove any Ansible Tower account
  • remove user accounts on particular instances (e.g., lando, rpmbuilder)
  • remove public keys belonging to the staff member from any service accounts
  • terminate personal AWS instances of machines

CMS Supergroup Page Approvers

For all hubs, make sure that the staff member wasn't on the list to receive emails.  See the settings for com_groups.

Go to  /administrator/index.php?option=com_groups , click on the "Options" icon, go to the "Pages" tab, and check the "Page approvers" for accounts that need to be removed.

CMS Roles and Group Memberships

The staff member needs to be demoted (e.g., not superuser or admin) and removed from relevant groups.  This can be done as follows:

  • Login to the /administrator site
  • Navigate to Users -> User Manager
  • Search for user accounts used by the staff member and remove any access (“Assigned User Groups” area, in Joomla! parlance) greater than “Registered”
  • Navigate to Users -> Members
  • Search for user accounts used by the staff member
  • For each account:
    • On the “hosts” tab, remove any host login capabilities
    • On the “groups” tab, get the list of all groups and remove the user from these groups (this will remove VPN access through the “vpn” group membership)
    • In com_tools, User Preferences, the number of sessions should be 3 for those users.
    • In com_support, check the ACL tab and see if they have ticket access.
  • Remove ACL (ticket) access (if not done by removal from a group). Sometimes users are added directly.
  • Reassign all tickets assigned to other liaisons/staff members.
  • Remove email/username from Options area on administrative in components (if it was added) — This applies to components like support, wishlist, answers, resources
  • Removal from Internal Projects. — Projects can be owned by groups. You would think that if a user was removed from said group, the user would also be removed from the project. Tests show that this does not appear to be true (this should be pursued).
  • Change Project roles. There must always be one project manager. If a Manager is removed, someone else must be the manager.
  • Removal from courses if added as a manager for administrative purposes
  • Remove from Page Approver role in group options, pages tab: Super groups have the ability to allow php and javascript in the content page, but it must be scanned and approved.

Detectify

Go to https://detectify.com/app/members and in the "Actions" column select "Remove" under the 3 dots menu

Encryption records

Remove records pertaining to the employee from the current version, but keep previous versions of the wiki showing that the employee did have laptops or external disks encrypted.

GitHub.com

Remove from organization

Gitlab.hubzero.org

Block the account.  Find all the groups owned by the user; promote another user to owner and remove the terminated user.  Examine personal projects;  ignore forks. Move other personal projects to a group, creating one if necessary, owned by current staff.

 

Google Docs / Drive

Remove Staffer access

Should use UCSD login to Google Drive (add to policy)

Move any docs in personal space to Common Hubzero Space

Special privileges

Backups of the HUBzero Google Drive are done via service accounts created in the Google project "HZ Google Drive Backups", aka manifest-ocean-363114  (in the UCSD.edu namespace).  Remove access to this project, if applicable.  See the IAM section of the project at https://console.cloud.google.com/iam-admin/iam?project=manifest-ocean-363114&supportedpurview=project

Group Hubzero-g

We have a group called "hubzero-g@ucsd.edu".  Remove the person from that group as described below.

"
This is how you can manage your Group and add members.
Login at:
https://groups.google.com/my-groups.

Make sure you are logged out of any personal Gmail accounts first.
Log in with your email address and AD password.
Instructions for adding members and managing your group here:
https://support.google.com/groups/answer/2465464?hl=en

UCSD GOOGLE GROUPS TRAINING:

You can see a UCSD Google groups quick start guide here:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1McXVwmsK2of6OmIDD4e3G9ZPEsKU0dq34rv8R-9neyk/view
"

Go to People -> Members, hover over the image of the user to show the hidden checkbox interface, click it, then to remove the user click on the "forbidden" icon in the upper right.

Hubadmin System Account Access

The system account "hubadmin" is used for PHP code updates and other operations in the Apache document root.  It can be accessed via SSH, via sudo for members of the "access-php" group, and a few operations can be performed by the Apache service user as "hubadmin", as specified by /etc/sudoers.  SSH logins cannot use passwords and require an SSH key stored on a local filesystem.  Therefore, removal of an individual implies removal from the "access-php" group and removal of an individual's SSH key credentials from the list of authorized keys.  Both are controlled by the configuration management system "Ansible".  This is handled above as part of the "Operating System" termination procedures.  It can also be done on its own, for example for personnel reassignments.  The best method is to "grep" for the user's account name in the Ansible configuration.

Hubzero.org web site (promo)

Remove the staff member's picture and name from web site.  For this, use /administrator, got to the Article Manager and edit the "about us" article.

Mailman Lists

Make sure that when removing people from lists, they don't become empty!

sudo su
cd /usr/lib/mailman/bin
for l in `./list_lists -b`; do
  echo -n $l ": "
  ./list_members $l | wc -l
  ./list_members $l
  echo
done

Ansible Commands for Mailman

Find Mailman mailing lists (use a substring of usernames or email addresses) for both prod and nonprod inventories:

ansible webservers -l rds_env,aws_env -i inventories/prod_hosts.ini -a "sudo /usr/lib/mailman/bin/find_member $name"
ansible webservers -l rds_env,aws_env -i inventories/non_prod_hosts.ini -a "sudo /usr/lib/mailman/bin/find_member $name"
ansible webservers -l sherlock_env -i inventories/prod_hosts.ini -a "sudo /usr/lib/mailman/bin/find_member $name"
ansible webservers -l sherlock_env -i inventories/non_prod_hosts.ini -a "sudo /usr/lib/mailman/bin/find_member $name"

Make sure to repeat this from all management hosts (RDS and Sherlock)!

To remove an address from all lists:

/usr/lib/mailman/bin/remove_members --fromall -n  -N ehuebner@sdsc.edu


To remove the user from a specific mailing list on a host, enter this, using the correct inventory file:

ansible hostname -l rds_env,aws_env -i inventories/prod_hosts.ini -a "sudo /usr/lib/mailman/bin/remove_members $mailing_list $email_address"
ansible hostname -l rds_env,aws_env -i inventories/non_prod_hosts.ini -a "sudo /usr/lib/mailman/bin/remove_members $mailing_list $email_address"
ansible hostname -l sherlock_env -i inventories/prod_hosts.ini -a "sudo /usr/lib/mailman/bin/remove_members $mailing_list $email_address"
ansible hostname -l sherlock_env -i inventories/non_prod_hosts.ini -a "sudo /usr/lib/mailman/bin/remove_members $mailing_list $email_address"

You should use a substring instead of the full name, for example kwoj instead of kwojo314, to be able to catch similar email addresses, for example kwojkovi@purdue.edu.

Find list owners, again for both inventories and both management hosts:

ansible -i inventories/prod_hosts.ini webservers -l rds_env,aws_env -m raw -a "sudo /usr/lib/mailman/bin/list_lists -b     | xargs -n 1  sudo /usr/lib/mailman/bin/list_admins | grep huebner"
ansible -i inventories/non_prod_hosts.ini webservers -l rds_env,aws_env -m raw -a "sudo /usr/lib/mailman/bin/list_lists -b     | xargs -n 1  sudo /usr/lib/mailman/bin/list_admins | grep huebner"
ansible -i inventories/non_prod_hosts.ini webservers -l sherlock_env -m raw -a "sudo /usr/lib/mailman/bin/list_lists -b     | xargs -n 1  sudo /usr/lib/mailman/bin/list_admins | grep huebner"
ansible -i inventories/prod_hosts.ini webservers -l sherlock_env -m raw -a "sudo /usr/lib/mailman/bin/list_lists -b     | xargs -n 1  sudo /usr/lib/mailman/bin/list_admins | grep huebner"

Remove and replace an owner with another (as root after login on the hub):

/usr/lib/mailman/bin/config_list -o - mailman | sed 's/ehuebner@ucsd.edu/pmeunier@ucsd.edu/' > /tmp/mailman.conf
/usr/lib/mailman/bin/config_list -i /tmp/mailman.conf mailman
rm /tmp/mailman.conf

Lists of Concern

These should be caught by the above commands and there's no need to check them manually one-by-one:

  • hubzero@hubzero.org
  • metrics@
  • support@
  • purchasing@
  • info@

MySQL Accounts

Check MySQL databases for individual accounts; in the past such individual accounts were discovered on hubs some time after the staff members had left. Here’s one way:

python /root/bin/do_predictated.py MYSQL_SERVER "mysql -D mysql -e "SELECT user, host, password from user where user like '%$username%';""

Reassign tickets to a new assignee

RDS Infrastructure

If applicable, send an email to support@sdsc.edu to remove access to:

  • PRTG monitoring
  • Grafana
  • Network firewalls
  • RDS Ansible git repository
  • management host:  hubzero.sdsc.edu

 

Sherlock Environment

  1. If applicable, create a ticket by sending an email to sherlocksupport@sdsc.edu, requesting that they perform termination procedures for (name) for the purposes of removing access privileges.  Please use the Sherlock Change Request form for this, or this termination template.
  2. Connect to the Sherlock VPN
  3. Update your Ansible copy with "git pull"
  4. If any IP addresses were removed in the RDS step above, run the roles:
    • hubzero.hubzero-apache2
    • hubzero.iptables
    • hubzero.mailman
  5. Disconnect from the Sherlock VPN

Slack

Remove the staff member from the Hubzero organization.

UCSD Termination Procedure

Watch for an email on sysadmins@hubzero.org with subject "checkout (date) name".  This is the signal for SDSC to perform termination procedures.  If no such email is sent, ask Amy Giang-Tran <amy@sdsc.edu> why.

 

Purdue (mostly historical)

Ogre Commands for Mailman (Purdue only)

python /root/bin/do_predictated.py HUB_WEB "/usr/sbin/find_member mdale"

Example:
hubzero:~# /usr/sbin/find_member pmeunier
pmeunier@purdue.edu found in:
     hubzeroteam
     hubzero-support
hubzero:~#

You should use a substring instead of the full name, for example kwoj instead of kwojo314, to be able to catch similar email addresses, for example kwojkovi@purdue.edu.

Users can be removed even if you aren't the administrator for the list, if you have root privileges on the machine, e.g., using

/usr/sbin/remove_members support dsk@purdue.edu

Also check if the user might have been the owner of a list:

/usr/sbin/list_admins `/usr/sbin/list_lists | grep ' - ' | awk '{print $1}'`

/usr/lib/mailman/bin/withlist -l support
del m.owner[m.owner.index('nikki@purdue.edu')]
del m.owner[m.owner.index('eahillery@purdue.edu')]
print m.owner
m.Save()

or "python /root/bin/do_predictated.py HUB_WEB "/usr/lib/mailman/bin/list_admins --all"

Datacenter Access (Purdue only)

If the staff member had data center access, create a Footprint ticket with ITaP to have that access removed, e.g., by emailing itap@purdue.edu

RCAC Resources (Purdue only)

Staff may have been granted special access to RCAC resources. For people leaving Purdue employment, RCAC states "The purge process is automatic from IAMO."  There is no point in emailing rcac-help@purdue.edu.  However if this is a position change, access needs to be adjusted.  This is managed from https://www.rcac.purdue.edu/account/ and leverages Purdue ACMaint groups.  Create a ticket with rcac-help@purdue.edu to be sure.  For example, a staff member may have received permissions such as:

You have been granted access to ITaP Research Computing resources.

You have been granted access to the following job submission queues, Unix groups, and other resources.

Unix group: purr (membership ready within 4 hours)
Unix group: purr-apps (membership ready within 4 hours)
Unix group: purr-data (membership ready within 4 hours)

Gitolite on help.hubzero.org (Purdue only)

Someone who is a gitolite administrator needs to manage the "gitolite-admin" repo, update it and push the changes.  Changes must NOT be done directly to /srv/gitolite/.gitolite or /srv/gitolite/.ssh/authorized_keys because they will be overwritten at the next push.  The file

/srv/gitolite/.gitolite/conf/gitolite.conf

has the lines (at the time of this writing):

repo gitolite-admin
        RW+             =               admin dbenham nkissebe zooley zweidner

So one of those must have a checked out copy of the "gitolite-admin" repo. When pushing changes, a hook will update  /srv/gitolite/.ssh/authorized_keys, which controls who can authenticate. It will also update the directory /srv/gitolite/.gitolite.  See http://gitolite.com/gitolite/concepts/ and in particular http://gitolite.com/gitolite/ct02.png which shows how the post-receive hook is involved.

Ogre Management of the Operating System (Purdue only)

For each username used by the staff member, search for references to that username in the Ogre configuration and remove them. The “find” command is used to avoid replacing symlinks:

username=xyz
cd /root/.predict
grep -l $username *
grab-ogre `grep -l $username *`
Message: "termination procedures for "
grep $username /usr/share/adm/ogre/private/config/classes/defaults.def
# Check the following file names:
grep -l $username /usr/share/adm/ogre/private/config/hosts/*
# Verify what's left in host definitions:
grep $username /usr/share/adm/ogre/private/config/hosts/*
# Use at your own risk:
find /usr/share/adm/ogre/private/config/hosts/ -type f -exec sed -i "s/$username.pub,//g" {} ;
find /usr/share/adm/ogre/private/config/hosts/ -type f -exec sed -i "s/$username,//g" {} ;
find /usr/share/adm/ogre/private/config/hosts/ -type f -exec sed -i "s/,$username.pub//g" {} ;
find /usr/share/adm/ogre/private/config/hosts/ -type f -exec sed -i "s/,$username//g" {} ;
find /usr/share/adm/ogre/private/config/hosts/ -type f -exec sed -i "s/$username//g" {} ;
# Verify what's left in all of Ogre:
grep -r $username /usr/share/adm/ogre | grep -v git
release-ogre

Also search all hosts for any local accounts belonging to that staff member, or any suspicious account (e.g., uid=0 that isn’t root) and delete them (e.g., “userdel” or “deluser”).

control:~# python /root/bin/doall.py "grep $username /etc/passwd"
control:~# python /root/bin/doall.py /usr/share/adm/scripts/find-questionable-accounts

Get the list of groups for that user. This may be helpful to create a ticket for the CMS part of the process (see below), and to find strange memberships.

python /root/bin/doall.py "groups $username"

Xymon System (Purdue only)

If the staff member is a recipient of Xymon emails, send a message to tickets-itiunix@purdue.edu

BlueCat and Network Firewall Contexts (Purdue only)

BlueCat is the system used at Purdue to manage DNS and things related to the IP space (e.g., DHCP). In addition the firewall contexts hubzero-dc-fw.tcom.purdue.edu and hubzero-vrf-fw.tcom.purdue.edu provide network access lists respectively for the data center networks (e.g., 128.46.18.0/24, 19 and 21) and the YONG network (128.46.16.0/24)

Access to these resources is managed by membership in the following groups:

PWL_319_HUBzero_DNS_Approvers   (Unix groupname: h0dnsapp)
PWL_319_HUBzero_DNS_Requesters  (h0dnsreq)
PWL_319_HUBzero_DNS_Read_Only   (h0dnsro)

Create tickets by sending emails to accounts@purdue.edu to change the memberships.

title: Disposal for Electronic-Based Media
content:
Purpose

The goal of this procedure is to follow or exceed the Purdue "Media Disposal Guidelines for Electronic-Based Media".  These guidelines center on using a "Multiple pass/DoD overwrite" defined in the guidelines.  However, the National Institute for Standards and Technology's (NIST) Special Publication "800-88 Revision 1: Guidelines for Media Sanitization" obsoletes it, and is the reference for data erasure compliance.  We will refer to Clear, Purge and Destroy as defined in 800-88.

Risks to be mitigated center around data leakage and exfiltration:

  • Disks could be lost or stolen whenever taken out of a data center and carried around campus
  • Disks are easier to steal when left free on top of a desk, in the period before reuse or destruction
  • Disks that aren't erased could leak some of the previous data when in use again
  • Disks returned for warranty service could carry confidential information
  • Leakage due to incomplete erasure:
    • disks have "spare" storage areas not normally accessible to regular programs like "scrub", "srm" or even "dd".
    • SSDs cannot be reliably erased simply by writing to the disk because the destination of writes is decided by the drive itself, and because it has reserved storage areas and internal data structures

Overall:

  • Prior to taking drives out of a data center, Clear them at least if they are unencrypted
  • To repurpose them, Purge them if they are unencrypted.
  • When sending drives for warranty replacement, perform a best-effort attempt to Purge them, or at least Clear them. 
    • If neither Purge or Clear are possible, consider Destroying the drive and buying a new one outside of warranty service
    • When setting up new systems, consider encrypting all drives or paying for "keep your hard drive" warranty
  • At end-of-life, Destroy them.
  • Document.

To Purge Magnetic Disks:

Send an ATA "Enhanced Secure Erase" command (see ATA Secure Erase wiki).  If the "Enhanced Secure Erase" command fails or isn't available, send a "Secure Erase" command instead.  This is easy to do with a dock like the StarTech Drive Eraser.  However, while drives are members of a hardware RAID array, I have not found a way to issue "ATA Secure Erase" commands directly to the drive.

To verify success, check the status displayed in the screen of the StarTech Drive Eraser and on its lights, at the end of the operation, or check the output of the commands given in the ATA Secure Erase wiki.

To Purge SSDs:

If externally encrypted, this is a No-op.  Otherwise, "Apply the ATA sanitize command" or use the "Cryptographic Erase" (see SP 800-88).  SP 800-88 states that the ATA "Enhanced Secure Erase" command is only a Clear operation for SSDs.

To Clear:

We should Clear, that is, overwrite media prior to transport even if the drive stays used by HUBzero, whenever it is taken out of a data center.  For SSDs, block erase methods such as described below are futile.  It should be done instead with an "ATA Secure Erase" command, while rebooting using a different drive.  For externally encrypted SSDs, this is not necessary.  HUBzero doesn't own self-encrypted drives so this procedure doesn't cover them.

Block Erase Wipe with "scrub"

1. Stop all services and unmount all logical volumes except the filesystem root (/)

2. List all the logical volumes.  For example this command lists the LVs along with their size.  Knowing the size can be useful later, e.g., after an incomplete wipe.

ncip:~# vgdisplay -v | grep -e Path -e Size
    DEGRADED MODE. Incomplete RAID LVs will be processed.
    Finding all volume groups
    Finding volume group "ncip"
  VG Size               930.26 GiB
  PE Size               4.00 MiB
  Alloc PE / Size       234673 / 916.69 GiB
  Free  PE / Size       3473 / 13.57 GiB
  LV Path                /dev/ncip/root
  LV Size                93.13 GiB
  LV Path                /dev/ncip/vz
  LV Size                158.56 GiB
  LV Path                /dev/ncip/home
  LV Size                100.00 GiB
  LV Path                /dev/ncip/apps
  LV Size                100.00 GiB
  LV Path                /dev/ncip/www
  LV Size                100.00 GiB
  LV Path                /dev/ncip/log
  LV Size                20.00 GiB
  LV Path                /dev/ncip/mysql
  LV Size                50.00 GiB
  LV Path                /dev/ncip/tmp
  LV Size                20.00 GiB
  LV Path                /dev/ncip/data
  LV Size                100.00 GiB
  LV Path                /dev/ncip/srv
  LV Size                175.00 GiB

3. Install and use the "scrub" utility, which supports "DoD" wipes

aptitude install scrub
for p in /dev/mapper/ncip-vz /dev/mapper/ncip-www /dev/mapper/ncip-apps /dev/mapper/ncip-home /dev/mapper/ncip-log /dev/mapper/ncip-mysql /dev/mapper/ncip-tmp /dev/mapper/ncip-data /dev/mapper/ncip-srv; do
   echo $p
   scrub -p dod $p
done

 

4. If the size information is no longer available, run scrub for every logical volume, using the information found in the previous step:

scrub -p dod --device-size 158G /dev/ncip/vz
scrub -p dod --device-size 100G /dev/ncip/home
scrub -p dod --device-size 100G /dev/ncip/apps
scrub -p dod --device-size 100G /dev/ncip/www
scrub -p dod --device-size 20G /dev/ncip/log
scrub -p dod --device-size 50G /dev/ncip/mysql
scrub -p dod --device-size 20G /dev/ncip/tmp
scrub -p dod --device-size 100G /dev/ncip/data
scrub -p dod --device-size 175G /dev/ncip/srv

If the disk is to be pulled, finish with a scrub of the root LV. While drives are members of a hardware RAID array, I have not found a way to issue "ATA Secure Erase" commands directly to the drive so block wiping is the best that can be done without rebooting into an external device. 

 

5. Verify by repeating the scrub commands. 

Verification passes are built into the "scrub" command, which reports success or failure, and also writes a flag on the partition upon success.  Verify the presence of that flag by running the "scrub" command one last time -- it reports that the logical volume was already successfully cleared or tries to wipe it again.

 

Block Erase Wipe with "Boot and Nuke"

Reboot a decommisioned server from a USB stick with a copy of DBAN.

 

To Destroy:

Physical destruction of the drives is accomplished by contacting Jeff A Storms, storms1@purdue.edu, Supervisor in the Purdue Surplus Store/Salvage Group.  They "punch a hole in the hard drives here and then ship them to a place that verifies they have shredded the drives."  They can transport the drives in a locked truck.  Request written (email) confirmation that the drives were destroyed.

To Replace Faulty Drives:

Request replacement drives as soon as a predictive failure alert occurs, and replace the drives as soon as possible. Replacing drives before a complete failure happens, could increase chances that a Purge or Clear will succeed or will be more complete. 

Hubzero doesn't buy self-encrypted drives, so we won't worry about trying to erase keys stored on the drive.  If the drive is externally encrypted, just send it back.  Otherwise, try to Purge the disk.  If that fails try to Clear it.  In cases of predictive failure replacement, there's a good chance that the operation will succeed, which reduces our risks.  If the process fails, send it on for replacement.  Dell says that they wipe drives that get repaired, but the Dell warranty return page states "We are not responsible for your confidential, proprietary or personal information", so exposures from mishaps when returning disks are our liability.

To Document:

When purging, label the drives (e.g., use a marker) with the operation performed and when.  For HIPAA-covered machines, add which operation was performed by who and when to the Record of the movements of hardware and electronic media.

First version: November 23, 2017
Last Edited: April 6, 2018 (warranty service: consider destroying a disk that can't be cleared or purged)

title: OpenVZ
content:
Procedures related for OpenVZ:  ploop images, etc

 

Troubleshooting

If you get the error "No ploop support in the kernel, or kernel is way too old." make sure that the vz service is running:

service vz start
chkconfig vz on

title: /vz is nearly full
content:
OpenVZ ploop technology has many advantages, but one issue is that the backing files keep getting bigger and bigger.  To recover space, one must run the command "ploop balloon discard".  For example, this will find the ploops in use:

catalyzecare:~# ll /vz/private/*/root.hdd/ -d
drwx------ 2 root root 4.0K Aug 24 22:42 /vz/private/1007/root.hdd/
drwx------ 2 root root 4.0K Jul 27 15:56 /vz/private/2000/root.hdd/
drwx------ 2 root root 4.0K May  7 07:05 /vz/private/2001/root.hdd/
drwx------ 2 root root 4.0K Aug 18  2016 /vz/private/2002/root.hdd/

After which the following commands will recover space:

ploop balloon discard /vz/private/1007/root.hdd/DiskDescriptor.xml
ploop balloon discard /vz/private/2000/root.hdd/DiskDescriptor.xml
ploop balloon discard /vz/private/2001/root.hdd/DiskDescriptor.xml
ploop balloon discard /vz/private/2002/root.hdd/DiskDescriptor.xml

The /vz logical volume went from 280G to 176G, a 104G savings.  However, having to remember to run this is an issue.

Quick, compact fix:

for ct in `ls -d /vz/private/*/root.hdd`; do
  ploop balloon discard $ct/DiskDescriptor.xml
done
df -hT /vz

title: User quotas inside OpenVZ containers
content:
Quotas can be read inside OpenVZ containers.

Quota errors such as described at https://help.hubzero.org/support/ticket/10540 can be fixed with something like:

mkdir /dev/mapper
ln -s /dev/dm-5 /dev/mapper/vg00-lv_home

Explanation

When using logical volumes (LVM) the device read on hardware nodes for quotas is /dev/mapper/vg00-lv_home:

# quotaon -ap
group quota on /home/diagrid (/dev/mapper/vg00-lv_home) is off
user quota on /home/diagrid (/dev/mapper/vg00-lv_home) is on

Note that this is actually a symlink:

# ll /dev/mapper/vg00-lv_home
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root 7 May  7 07:08 /dev/mapper/vg00-lv_home -> ../dm-5

OpenVZ containers can pass the quota information with a DEVNODES option like:OpenVZ passes the information through with:

DEVNODES="mapper/vg00-lv_home:rq"

However inside the OpenVZ containers, the bind mount makes /dev/dm-5 available instead.

The fix is just recreating the expected symlink inside OpenVZ containers.

title: Container root partition is full
content:
0. Find which directory is using the most space

for p in `ls /* -d`; do
  df -hT $p | grep ploop -q
  [ $? -eq 0 ] && ds $p
done

Then use the ds alias defined in /root/.bashrc:

ds /var/log/* | grep G

 

1. Ploop

The output of "df -hT" shows that the ploop container is full:

 

/dev/ploop21073p1        ext4       20G   20G     0 100% /var/lib/vz/root/2005

A. Try to recover wasted space with "ploop balloon discard"

ll /vz/private/*/root.hdd/ -d
cd /vz/private/
ploop balloon discard 1007/root.hdd/DiskDescriptor.xml
ploop balloon discard 2000/root.hdd/DiskDescriptor.xml
ploop balloon discard 2001/root.hdd/DiskDescriptor.xml

B. Allocate more disk space with "ploop resize"

ploop resize -s size DiskDescriptor.xml


Example:

 

ploop resize -s 40G /var/lib/vz/private/2005/root.hdd/DiskDescriptor.xml

# df -hT /var/lib/vz/root/2005
Filesystem        Type  Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/ploop21073p1 ext4   40G   20G   18G  53% /var/lib/vz/root/2005

 

2. SimFS

See https://openvz.org/Disk_quota

vzctl set <ctid> --diskspace $SoftLimit$:$HardLimit$ --save

and change the Ogre configuration to match

DISKSPACE="$SoftLimit$:$HardLimit$"

Example:

DISKSPACE="4G:5G"

title: HIPAA Hub Configuration
content:
DRAFT

1. Force SSL Usage for the entire site

  • /administrator/index.php?option=com_config#server  
  • Site -> "Global Configuration" -> "Server Settings"
  • change "Force SSL" to "Entire Site"

2. Set the configuration management system (Ogre or Puppet) to perform appropriate configuration changes.  In Ogre, add "@define FLAG_HIPAA_SERVER" and @define FORCE_HTTPS_CONNECTIONS.

  • SSH configuration
    • MaxAuthTries 4 (decrease from 6),
    • LogLevel VERBOSE to log key fingerprints as suggested in NIST IR 7966
    • Disable logins for the hubadmin account, and other privileged accounts (including sudo-capable accounts) from AWS
    • If full HIPAA data will be used, set "PermitRootLogin without-password" for all users to disable password-based logins.
  • Apache
    • /etc/php5/apache2/php.ini:session.cookie_secure = 1
    • Remove conditions so this always happen for plain HTTP connections: RewriteRule    ^(.*)$        https://hubname.org$1 [R,L]
    • Use the 2-factor authentication plugins for /administrator (can they be required only for /administrator?) "Authfactors - Authy" and "Authfactors - Certificate"

3. Password Strength

  • See the Account Management policy for the correct settings
  • Use the Account Management procedure to make changes
  • Force the expiration of passwords on all accounts (how?) so we can be sure the new passwords meet the policy

4. Set session timeout to 15 min (based on PCI requirements as an example of a secure setting)

  • Go to /administrator
  • Site -> "Global Configuration" -> "System"
  • Change "Session Lifetime" to 15

5. Review Account Privileges

Using the Account Review Procedure, verify that accounts:

  • still require all of the privileges they have
  • have legitimate needs
  • are authorized
  • are still active
  • do not belong to terminated staff

5. Update Hub policies, including those displayed as articles by the web site, especially the privacy policy

6. Force all users to agree again to the new policies

title: Web Application Vulnerability Scanning
content:
HUBzero uses the service "Detectify" provided at "detectify.com" to perform vulnerability scanning.  Each HIPAA-covered hub should have a dedicated "scan profile" on the service, and each scan will be recorded separately.  The following procedure is for production servers;  vulnerabilities found on non-production servers that have restricted access, and that do not exist on a production server, should be given less priority, depending on circumstances.

  • Go to the dashboard, https://detectify.com/dashboard and login if needed
  • Go to "Assets" and click "Add asset".  Select the manual method and enter the domain name of the hub.
  • To create a scan profile, select an asset, and the "Scan profiles" tab.  Click on "Create Scan profiles"
  • Configure profiles by clicking on "
    • Scan profile settings (tab)
      • How often do you want to run a scan?  Should be set to "Recurring scans:  every month"
      • Should we automatically start a scan when new security tests are added?    Yes
      • How long should we keep the reports before deleting? 90 days
      • Opt-in for the following beta features
        • Missing security header
        • Run missing security header tests against all paths
    • Deep Scan Settings (tab)
      • Should we crawl subdomains?  YEs
      • Which subdomains must we avoid? None
      • Which paths/URLs must we include?
        • /administrator
        • /api
        • /app/site
        • /app/templates
        • /infrastructure
        • /tools
        • /webdav
      • Should we scan common ports?  Yes
      • Which ports must we avoid? None
      • Which predefined analytics services should we avoid? (Only avoid Google and Twitter)
      • How should the scanners be recognizable?  Use the Detectify user agent.  Do not attempt to define and MSIE user agent to avoid the false positives for IE-only XSS, because then the scanner will be completely banned from the site!
      • How fast can we go? 100 requests/second
         
  • When notified that a scan has ended, check scan results from the dashboard, by clicking on the links "Finished..."
    • Analyze the findings by severity
      • Try to reproduce the finding from the URL and any submitted POST data, to remove false positives
      • Determine if this affects only the hub where it was reported, or if it's something that affects all hubs
      • Determine if this is something that could be fixed by changing the configuration of services like Apache, the configuration of the HUBzero CMS, or if it is a code issue
    • Create Trello cards:
      • in the "Sprint" board for findings with CVSS >9 scores and label them as an "incursion"
        • Request from a manager that the card be assigned ASAP to someone available with appropriate skills
        • If a code update is not scheduled within a week and this is a code issue, ask a Communications Manager to contact the affected hubs about the issue, with the goal of determining if patching needs to be scheduled
        • If this is a configuration issue, a system administrator will implement the change through Ansible
          • If it can be fixed simply by restarting a service like Apache, determine an appropriate time and do it after notifying other system administrators and the Slack "trouble" channel
          • If more involved tasks are involved, a special time may need to be scheduled.  Ask a Communications Manager to help
      • in the "Backlog" board for other vulnerabilities
        • label "High" impact vulnerabilities with CVSS scores <=9 as "Next Sprint"
        • label all vulnerabilities as "security"
    • For FISMA-Low certified hubs, additionally the actions and timelines described in control (CA-5) "Plan of Action and Milestones" must be followed.
    • Control SI-2 "Flaw Remediation" also requires the following timelines for resolution:
      • "The following remediation timelines must be met, or the affected device may be removed from the network:"
        • Critical within 30 days;
        • High within 60 days;
        • Medium within 1 year; and
        • Low within 1 year.
    • If a hub has a FISMA certification other than plain baseline Low, refer to its SSP (System Security Plan) for the appropriate timelines.

title: SDSC RDS Hub Decommission
content:
Hubzero

  • Schedule decommission date with client.  Wait for date to be scheduled.  Continue on the scheduled date.  Clients should copy their data or make a list of data we need to copy for them.
  • In PRTG, move hosts and service IPs to the “non-prod” group.  (may submit a ticket to RDS specifically for this, wait until complete to continue).
  • Move hosts to nonprod inventory in Ansible, and rename the group_vars file from “prod_hubname” to “nonprod_hubname”.  Use “grep” to make sure that inventories/prod_hosts.ini has no references left to the hub.
  • In Ansible inventory, remove the “prod_hubname” group from the production inventory file and merge it with the “nonprod_hubname” group in the nonprod inventory.  Example:
    • [hubname:children]
    • nonprod_hubname
    • [nonprod_hubname]
      • web01.int.hubname.org
      • exec01.hubname.org
      • stage.hubname.org
  • In the host_vars file for the webserver, set “decommissioned: true”.
  • Run the appropriate Ansible maintenance playbook “hubzero.only_web.maint.yml” to restrict web and SSH access to the hub hosts to behind the UCSD firewall.  If the maintenance playbook fails for some reason, at least run the hubzero.iptables role.
  • Copy docker images from an execution host to the webhost for final backup.  (Execution hosts will not have a final backup created).
  • Perform data exports and archived backups for hub owners via provided script. The full procedure is described in the script (https://gitlab.hubzero.org/hubzero/hub_backup_script ).
  • Decommission can proceed when backups for clients have been provided on help.hubzero.org, we do not need to wait for them to pick them up to continue.
  • Client backups will be available for 1 month.  Storage on help.hubzero.org can be expanded temporarily for client pickup via USS.
  • Submit a support ticket to RDS to complete the decommission procedure below (specifically list all hosts).


RDS

  • Perform full backup (VM snapshot) of all hub hosts specified except for execution hosts.
  • This backup should be retained for 1 year from the date of decommission.
  • Other backups may be removed.
  • Remove VMs from PRTG.
  • Shut down the VMs associated with the decommissioning hub.
  • Remove VMs from Ansible inventory (host vars, group var, non_prod_hosts file).  Commit changes back to the Ansible repository.
  • Update network firewall.
  • Release subnet and reclaim IPs.
  • Add a note to the support ticket with billing updates, if applicable.
  • Add a note to the support ticket that the decommission procedure is complete and close the ticket.

title: Ansible for Configuration Management, Provisioning and Disaster Recovery
content:
The Ansible playbooks and roles used by SDSC HUBzero apply to the SDSC RDS, SDSC Sherlock, and AWS environments.  We use Ansible playbooks to provision systems and manage their configurations.  We also use Ansible to update the HUBzero CMS code, for which there is a separate documentation page.  We recommend running Ansible as a way of detecting and fixing configuration issues, and during disaster recovery when applicable, e.g., to provision new VMs.  Do not make manual changes to hosts;  all changes should be done through Ansible, so that during Disaster Recovery, a host can be completely rebuilt by running the appropriate Ansible playbooks.

Getting Started

To start using Ansible, get a copy of the Ansible repository:

git clone git@gitlab.com:sdsc-rds/systems/hubzero-ansible.git

Note that there are 2 inventories of hosts, one for production (inventories/prod_hosts.ini) and one for non-production (inventories/non_prod_hosts.ini).  Make sure to use the right inventory for the host's status (use the "-i" option for the "ansible-playbook" command). 

Provisioning

Provisioning is done by running the appropriate playbook for the host type.  To setup a "web server without tools" for the first time:

  • Make sure the hostname is in the "only_web" group in the inventory
  • Run playbooks/hubzero.only_web.new_install.yml
  • Run playbooks/hubzero.only_web.maint.yml

To setup a web server with tools, first set it up as a webserver without tools as above, then:

  • In the inventory, move the hostname from the "only_web" group to the "web_with_tools" group
  • Run playbooks/hubzero.web_with_tools.new_install.yml
  • Run playbooks/hubzero.web_with_tools.maint.yml

To setup an execution host:

  • Make sure the hostname is in the "exec" group in the inventory
  • Run playbooks/hubzero.exechost.maint.yml

Configuration Management

Run the playbooks with ".maint" in their name, for the appropriate host type.  It is fine to run separately the roles that apply.

Disaster Recovery and Upgrades to new VMs

Running the above playbooks works for new hubs and existing hubs.  However, during disaster recovery or even procedures like Operating System upgrades, the data from an old VM may need to be migrated to a new VM.  In that case, the storage from the old VMs, or a backup image in the case of disaster recovery, can be mounted at /mnt on the new VM.  The playbook "playbooks/hubzero.copy_data_webservers_upgrade.yml" will migrate the data from the /mnt mounts to the new storage locations in the new VM.

title: Gitlab Upgrade
content:
Hubzero maintains a Gitlab CE installation on AWS at gitlab.hubzero.org (real hostname gitlab.aws.hubzero.org).

To process an upgrade for "gitlab-ce at gitlab.hubzero.org"

Check that a "gitlab-ce" package update is available (yum check-update), but don't do the update (yum update).  Sometimes a vulnerability is reportly fixes in a new version of Gitlab but that version of Gitlab isn't available yet in the Yum repo.  Please wait for a Gitlab package update, never update Gitlab manually.


1) Check that there is disk space available to do a backup (df -h). Gitlab backups are stored in "/srv/gitlab/backups/".  Keep a couple backups and typically remove the oldest before doing the next update. Pay attention to the size of the backup files. Gitlab may do incremental backups.  A full backup for us is about 14GB at this time of this writing (more disk is needed to process the backup too.)

2) Create a new backup "sudo gitlab-rake gitlab:backup:create STRATEGY=copy" .  Watch for any failure messages.  Backup failures are often due to lack of disk space.

The final output of the backup command should results should be similar to:
""
Deleting old backups ... skipping
Warning: Your gitlab.rb and gitlab-secrets.json files contain sensitive data
and are not included in this backup. You will need these files to restore a backup.
Please back them up manually.
Backup task is done.
""

3) "yum install gitlab-ce" to update Gitlab.  Other host updates can be done at the same time, but I usually update those first and then update Gitlab individually to be able to traceback what changed if Gitlab has issues after the ugprade.

4)  Check that "https://gitlab.hubzero.org/" is back up.  It likely will display an error.  Gitlab's infrstructure is huge and takes a few minutes to reload.  If after 10 minutes an error is still shown, you can restart Gitlab's processes with "gitlab-ctl restart"

 

Gitlab upgrade docs are located at https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/update/package/ .  Do not use these instructions directly - look for notes like "For the GitLab Community Edition, replace gitlab-ee with gitlab-ce."

 

Some useful Gitlab commands I've used in the past:

gitlab-ctl restart

gitlab-rake gitlab:check

gitlab-rails dbconsole

gitlab-psql

**You shouldn't really need to access the rails or psql console unless something has really gone wrong.  It was only needed once since we have been using Gitlab.
