title: Physical
content:
This page describes physical procedures, such as those when visiting a datacenter, preventing shoulder surfing, and preventing people slipping in behind you when you unlock a building door.

 

Historical:

A copy of the official ITaP Data Center Security Policies and Procedures with Purdue letterhead is available for download.  The subpage we have here is the result of copying and pasting of the contents.

title: ITaP Data Center Security Policies and Procedures (Historical)
content:
ITaP Data Center

Security Policies and Procedures

 

1.0 Introduction

 

The security of the equipment and data in the ITaP Data Centers is vitally important to the daily functioning of Purdue University. Computer systems, networking and telecommunications hardware and software, and the data that is stored and transmitted must be protected and preserved.

 

The purpose of this document is to communicate the polices and procedures by which IT Infrastructure Operations and those customers who make use of the Data Center will maintain an appropriate level of security within the Data Center.

 

1.1 Provisions

 

  1. Data Centers will be protected from unauthorized access.

  2. Data Centers or ITaP facilities, which house sensitive or high-risk equipment, will be protected against fire, water, and other hazards.

  3. Devices that are critical to the operation of Purdue University business processes will be protected against power failure.

  4. Records will be kept (e.g. manual sign in sheets, door access logs, etc.) to track all staff and visitors accessing facilities and data centers.

  5. Reception areas will be designated to receive visitors to the facilities/data centers.

  6. Monitoring equipment/devices will be installed in data centers to monitor door access, environmental conditions (e.g. temperature, humidity, fire, smoke, water).

  7. Security awareness program will be instituted to educate staff as to proper security policies and procedures.

  8. Procedures will be developed for the secure disposal of computing equipment containing sensitive data.

  9. Incident Response Team (IRT) will be created and escalation procedures established.

  10. Business Impact Analysis (BIA) will be conducted on all systems, applications, and platforms.

  11. Security Risk Assessment will be completed to assess physical security at all facilities.

 

 

2.0 Policies

 

2.1 Access to an ITaP Data Center

 

  1. All personnel entering an ITaP Data Center must have proper authorization.

    1. Level I Authorization provides for access to data center after identity verification by Operations Staff.

    2. Level II Authorization provides for access to data center via card key access.

    3. Non-ITaP staff members are restricted to Level I Authorization.

  2. A “Data Center Access Authorization” request must be on file for each individual who is authorized to enter the Data Center. Enter a ticket via support.purdue.edu (New Issue – Quick Templates – SO.DatCenAccess)

  3. Visitors to the Data Center are to adhere to the visitors’ guidelines (see section 3.2).

  4. A data center management employee must accompany visitors in the Data Center, or another authorized employee, at all times while in the Data Center. Exceptions to this policy must have approval of the Data Center Manager or Data Center Coordinator (Jon Miller/Todd Turner respectively).

  5. All persons, with the exception of Infrastructure employees, must sign in when entering the Data Center to document the time and purpose of their visit. They must also sign out when leaving.

  6. For the Freehafer Hall Data Center all visitors and authorized staff must enter through the south entrance.

 

Note: The term “visitor” is defined as anyone who:

 

  1. does not work in the Data Center;

  2. is not an Infrastructure staff member;

  3. does not have Level I authorization to the Data Center;

  4. does not have Level II authorization to the Data Center.

 

2.2 Equipment in an ITaP Data Center

 

In an effort to maximize security and minimize disruptions, the following policies apply to all equipment housed in an ITaP Data Center.

 

  1. An electronic request must be completed for all equipment installations, removals, and renames via support.purdue.edu.

  2. Operations staff will deny entry to authorized staff who intends to install, remove, or rename equipment without an installation form on file.

 

2.3 Hardware/Software Maintenance & Upgrades of Production Equipment

 

  1. Authorized employees may perform maintenance/repair on an as-needed basis 24 hours/7 days a week.

 

 

3.0 Procedures

 

3.1 Access Authorization

 

All employees must have proper authorization to gain access to an ITaP Data Center. Based upon the frequency of access and the home department of the person requesting access, there are two levels of authorization. The procedures to acquire authorization, at each level, are detailed below:

 

3.1.1 Level I Authorization

 

  1. The employee requesting access to a Data Center must complete an electronic request using the SO.DatCenAccess Quick Templates at support.purdue.edu.

  2. His/her director/manager will authorize the request submitted via item 1.

  3. After director/manager approval, the Hardware Services & Operations (HSO) Director will approve via the tech notes in the electronic request

  4. After approval by the HSO Director approves the request, the IT Infrastructure Operations Security Coordinator will then process the request.

  5. The employee will be added to the authorization database.

  6. The Security Coordinator will provide quarterly audits on who has access to the data centers.

  7. The employee will be authorized to enter the Data Center, but will NOT have card swipe access. The Operations staff on duty will verify employee authorization before allowing the employee to enter the Data Center.

  8. The employee must log in/out when entering/exiting the Data Center. The purpose of the visit must be documented.

  9. Level I Authorization is the standard access policy for non-ITaP staff members.

 

3.1.2 Level II Authorization

 

  1. The employee requesting access to a Data Center must complete an electronic request using the SO.DatCenAccess Quick Templates at support.purdue.edu.

  2. His/her director/manager will authorize the request submitted via item 1.

  3. After director/manager approval, the Hardware Services & Operations (HSO) Director will approve via the tech notes in the electronic request

  4. After approval by the HSO Director approves the request, the IT Infrastructure Operations Security Coordinator will then process the request.

  5. The employee will be added to the authorization database.

  6. The Security Coordinator will provide quarterly audits on who has access to the data centers.

  7. The employee will be authorized to enter the Data Center and will be given card swipe access.

  8. The employee must log in/out when entering/exiting the Data Center. The purpose of the visit must be documented.

 

3.2 Visitor Guidelines

 

Anyone who does not does not report to the Data Center on a daily basis, is not an Infrastructure employee, or who does not have Level I/Level II authorization is considered a visitor. All visitors to an ITaP Data Center must adhere to the following guidelines:

 

  1. Visitors must log in/out when entering/exiting the Data Center. The purpose of the visit must be documented.

  2. A data center management employee or another authorized employee must accompany visitors at all times while in the Data Center. All exceptions must have the approval of the Data Center Manager or Coordinator (Jon Miller/Todd Turner respectively).

  3. Visits to an ITaP Data Center should be coordinated through the Data Center Coordinator at least 24 hours in advance.

 

3.3 Audit Procedures

 

  1. The IT Infrastructure Security Coordinator will send a list of authorized employees to each director on a quarterly basis (January, April, July, and October) for his/her review and verification.

  2. Each director will review and update the list of authorized employees and return it to the Security Coordinator within two weeks.

  3. Each Semester, all student employees will be removed from the access data base and must renew access authorization if employment continues.

  4. Each (non-data center management) employee must renew access authorization annually during the announced renewal period.

 

3.4 Equipment Installation

 

The employee performing the installation will follow the procedures outlined under the ITaP Change Management Program (http://www.itap.purdue.edu/infrastructure/operations/change/).

 

3.5 Equipment Removal

 

The employee performing the removal will follow procedures outlined under the ITaP Change Management Program (http://www.itap.purdue.edu/infrastructure/operations/change/).

 

3.6 Equipment Renaming

 

The employee performing the rename will follow procedures outlined under the ITaP Change Management Program (http://www.itap.purdue.edu/infrastructure/operations/change/).

title: Key Resources and Processes
content:
Developing roles and responsibilities for process is often difficult.  It commonly begins with the question of ownership and responsibility as an organization begins to understand the value of process and implement actions to manage those processes.  Assignment of process ownership is one of the indicators of an increasing level of process maturity.  One of the most important questions to consider when embarking on a process journey is "Who should we select as our Process Owner(s)?"  Regardless of the maturity model being used to assess processes, the creation or assignment of process ownership normally occurs one level up from status quo.  Ironically, one of the most neglected areas of transformation in any type of change is definition and assignment of roles and responsibilities.  Although there is now a general acknowledgement that people are one of (if not the most) critical success factors in any type of business transformation, most organizations are not very accomplished at implementing 'people' oriented changes.

Process owner Definition:

One of the biggest impediments to capitalizing on a good, strategic idea is that changes must often be made across multiple departments such as support, code deployment, and system development.  Each of may have its own manager, projects, and priorities. So,  is no small task.

Unlike your standard department head, the business process owner oversees a process. And that process usually spans at least several departments. Therefore, the process owner has to become familiar with the inner workings of multiple segments of a company and figure out how to  in order to achieve the strategic goal.

Skills of an effective business process owner role:

The business process owner role is less traditional than other leadership roles, and therefore requires a special skill set. Here are some strengths to look for in a candidate:

  • Perspective: A good process owner learns and understands the details of the operational process while keeping their eye on the bigger strategic picture (which is ultimately geared toward customer satisfaction).

  • Leadership: Effecting change  who can motivate others, negotiate appropriately, and coordinate efforts across multiple departments.

  • Level-headed: Change is easier for some than others. The process owner should be able to handle pushback and resistance in a calm, measured way. But as new information comes to light, they should also be willing to recalibrate the plan if necessary.

  • Driven: It is antithetical to the business process owner role to simply “go through the motions” because many of those motions are what need to change. An effective process owner must be ok with the nitty-gritty and be .

  • Broad experience: Having a wide-ranging background often means the business process owner is familiar with multiple ways of getting things done and at various levels.

Process owners are a vital part of successful DMAIC (Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control) and DFSS (Design for Six Sigma) projects. Process owners are responsible for the management of processes within the organization. In some cases process owners are current leaders/managers, and in other cases process owners may be taken from non-leadership positions. They are the people who receive the solutions created by an improvement team, and end up being responsible for managing the improved process. A process owner should be:

  1. A subject matter expert of the process.

  2. Someone who feels the pain of the poorly functioning process, and will experience the gain of the improved process.

  3. A person who can positively influence the improvement team members.

  4. Someone who is able to communicate effectively with the current or subsequent leaders of the process and who either have an effect on the process or are a recipient (customer) of the process.

  5. A person who has the aptitude for process thinking and improvement.

In addition, the process owner is responsible for acquiring key performance measures for the process, and they must make sure that the process is continually monitored, studied and improved even after the Six Sigma improvements have been implemented.

Process Owner Responsibilities

The Process Owner is responsible for the governance of the process's performance, process changes or improvements, and include the following on an on-going basis:

  • Defines the process mission, vision, tactics, goals, objectives, KPIs (Key Performance Indicators) that are aligned with the organization goals.

  • Monitors and reports process performance against KPIs.

  • Synchronizes process improvement plans with other process owners within the value chain and other interfacing processes.

  • Ensures appropriate process designs, including business requirements.

  • Defines and sponsors business process change and capability investments, which continuously increase the maturity of the process and sustain each level of maturity.

title: Support Tickets
content:
This process owner is responsible for:

  • Processing new tickets as they are submitted including attempting to solve the reported question, issue, or request as quickly as possible.  Asking for additional information from the ticket submitter may be required.
  • Categorizing and assigning the ticket to appropriate person for work to be done. 
  • Monitoring ticket metrics for last activity, etc. and send reminders as necessary.

 

  •  
  •     Record and classify received Incidents and undertake an immediate effort in order to restore a failed IT Service as quickly as possible
  •     Assign unresolved Incidents to appropriate Tier 2 Support Group
  •     Log all Incident/Service Request details, allocating categorization and prioritization codes
  •     Keep users informed about their Incidents’ status at agreed intervals
  •     Associate Incidents with other records (i.e. Incidents, Changes, Problems, Knowledge Articles, Known Errors, etc.)
  •     Provide first-line investigation and diagnosis of all Incidents and Service Requests
  •     Verify resolution with users and resolve Incidents in ITSM tool
  •     Escalate Major Incidents to the Incident and/or Problem Manager
  •     Escalate Incidents at risk of breaching Service Level Agreement to the Incident Process Coordinator.
  •     Owns all Incidents and Service Requests throughout the lifecycle
  •  
  •     Investigate and diagnose Incidents to restore a failed IT Service as quickly as possible
  •     Resolve Incidents within the specified Service Level Agreements/Operational Level Agreements
  •     Document troubleshooting steps and service restoration details
  •     Create and submit knowledge articles
  •     Provide specialized investigation and diagnosis of all Incidents and Service Requests
  •     Identify Problems
  •     Verify resolution with end-users and resolve assigned Incidents
  •     Escalate Major Incidents to the Incident and/or Problem Manager
  •     Escalate Incidents at risk of breaching Service Level Agreement/Operational Level Agreement to the Incident Process Coordinator
  •     Escalate unresolved Incidents to Tier 3
  •     Restore a failed IT Service as quickly as possible
  •     Escalate unresolved incidents to external support, e.g. Software and Hardware Vendors
  •     Services are requested by Tier 1/2 Support if required for solving an Incident
  •     Liaison between IT and external support provider
  •     A subject matter expert for a specific service
  •     Responsible for planning and coordinating all the activities required to perform, monitor, and report on the process
  •     Remediate deviation of a process for its particular division/department/school
  •     Responsible for communicating with the Incident Process Owner
  •     Point of contact for all Major Incidents
  •     Responsible for the effective implementation of the process "Incident Management" and carries out the respective reporting procedure.
  •     Represent the first stage of escalation for Incidents
  •     Monitor the workload per Tier 1 Analyst
  •     Monitor the incidents to ensure that the Service Level Agreement are respected
  •     Identify, initiate, schedule and conduct incident reviews
  •     Ensure the closure of all resolved and end-user confirmed Incident records
  •     Provide guidance to the Incident Process Coordinators
  •     Establish continuous process improvement cycles where the process performance, activities, roles and responsibilities, policies, procedures and supporting technology is reviewed and enhanced where applicable.

 

 

 

 

Tickets must be assigned to an individual at all times.  All unassigned tickets should be assigned to the Process owner for categorization and delegation.

title: Code Deployment
content:
Software Development Lifecycle

Requirement gathering and analysis

Business requirements are gathered in this phase. A Requirement Specification Document is created.

Documents should be stored in https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/16gkCdmAmjYw2tphexOyIbE75w0eTa1_U

Design

In this phase the system and software design is prepared from the requirement specifications.  Integration points determined, end-user user-cases defined, etc.  A Design Specification document is created.

Documents should be stored in https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/16gkCdmAmjYw2tphexOyIbE75w0eTa1_U

Implementation / coding

The work is divided in modules/units and actual coding is started based on the previous two steps. This is the longest phase of the software development life cycle.

Code Review

The currently working code-set is demostrated to the technical team for feedback.  A code review is done by a senior developer and the Hubzero Security officer and ahead to the Secure Programming Policy at https://help.hubzero.org/documentation/itppr/policies/secureprogramming.  The new code in this phase may be considered an alpha release.

Please use the Code Review template at https://docs.google.com/document/d/1UPe_ub7lUwKTNRX7C2M8cgNR3trSWXwCOL_9yrdflgs

Code Review documents should be stored in https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1vZYXkRBqMS1IbzfJ-Hm1X9sgz8hyLMZu

 

Testing

During this phase unit testing, integration testing, system testing, end-user acceptance testing are done confirming the features in the Requirement Specification Document.  The new code is placed on a stage hub host during this phase. The new code in this phase may be considered an beta release.  A final release candidate is chosen at the end of this phase.

Deployment to client

After successful testing the product is delivered / deployed to the customer for their use.  The new code is promoted to a production host.

Maintenance

Bug fixes, adjustments to dependency upgrades, etc.

title: Deprecated Git Deployment Process
content:
Git Deployment Process (deprecated, do not use)

Why git?

Git provides a convenient way to track features, bug-fixes, and development history across managed deployments. Git is a decentralized version control system which allows many developers to work on the same codebase, manage conflicting code revisions, and provide a history of changes to document features inline with the code.

Git is considered an industry standard among developers and since the prevalence of github.com and BitBucket, has become the go-to source code version control system.

Current implementation

Git is currently used a deployment mechanism across all HUBzero-supported production environments. It has worked out well, however has become somewhat cumbersome to administer in its current form. The first problem is that there are two workflows depending on whether the hub’s pipeline has a stage machine or not.

Dev & Prod Pipeline

In the case that a customer’s deployment has a dev and prod configuration only, the customer has their own repository which is a point where their hub’s custom code is merged in with HUBzero’s distribution. This was more profound prior to 2.0.0 Hubzero CMS releases as there was no distinction between customized code and hubzero core code. Since 2.0.0 the hubzero core directory contains code maintained by HUBzero developers and the app directory contains customized code and configurations per hub.

In this setup, the hub’s repository is on the dev.domain.org host usually in the filesystem directory /www/dev. A developer would make changes within /www/dev, commit the changes. The repository would pull from hubzero-cms repository and merge in customizations. When production was to be updated, it would pull from the repository located on the dev host.

The strokes to update the entire pipeline with bleeding edge code would look like:

  1. Log in as a normal user
    1. ssh user@dev.hub.org
  2. Become a privileged user
    1. sudo su - hubadmin
  3. Get the latest CMS code
    1. git pull
      1. This appeared to rebase local commits on top of hubzero-cms/-production branch
      2. Fetch was set to https://hubzero.org/git/hubzero-cms.git
  4. Run composer
    1. cd core && ./bin/composer install
    2. cd ../
  5. Run database migrations
    1. ./muse migration -i -f
  6. Fix permissions (affects Ogre managed systems primarily)
    1. sudo /usr/share/adm/scripts/check_group_access_php.py

Dev, Stage & Prod Pipeline

The Dev/Stage/Prod pipeline is the general direction we would like to take most deployments. In this configuration, custom code contributions from our clients are introduced on dev which is a clone of the repository hosted on stage. Stage becomes the merge point between hubzero-cms core code and customized code. The production host then pulls from the bare repo (located on stage).

This configuration’s strokes appear as such:

  1. Log in as a normal user
    1. ssh user@dev.hub.org
  2. Become a privileged user
    1. sudo su - hubadmin
  3. Get the latest CMS code
    1. git fetch --all
    2. git merge {{ branch }} -X theirs
      1. This appeared to rebase local commits on top of hubzero-cms branch
      2. Fetch was set to https://hubzero.org/git/hubzero-cms.git
  4. Run composer
    1. cd core && ./bin/composer install
    2. cd ../
  5. Run database migrations
    1. ./muse migration -i -f
  6. Fix permissions (affects Ogre managed systems primarily)
    1. sudo /usr/share/adm/scripts/check_group_access_php.py

Rethinking the Distribution of HUBzero CMS

Separation of the app and core Directories

Releases prior to 1.3.1 the hubzero-cms was distributed as a single directory where customized code was intermixed with "core" code. This means that every production deployment of software was truly it’s own version based on a HUBzero release. Git was relied upon to manage these deployments, keeping track of revisions, merges, and replacement on a per-deployment basis.

In the past when a customer requested a particular functionality there were two entry points for code through:

  1. The HUBzero Core
  2. The Deployments Dev/Stage Environment

This caused the deployment to become convoluted as each update meant merging the customer’s code with the HUBzero code.

In HUBzero-CMS version 2.0+, the distinction of customized code and core code was created. This allows deployment-specific code and configuration to reside apart from the CMS’s core. Idealistically speaking, this allows for the core code to be updated independently of a customer’s special features. The next step would be to create a complementary Git workflow that allows developers (considering third-party developers) to contribute functionality to a specific deployment without breaking the core feature set.

HUBzero Core Git Flow

With the advent of moving to monthly releases it is desired to keep new features out of the “stable” branch. The stable branch is defined as the line of code which currently is installed on production hosts.

Guideline - All development should be done on the master branch and bug-fixes targeting a specific version should be cherry-picked from master to the version branch.

Repository Hosting Scheme

By changing the location and software used to host the repositories required for a HUBzero CMS deployment, the codebase can gain more visibility, contributions, and stability. In this proposed model, “flagship” production-ready code will be presented on github.com for community members to clone and install on their own.

Development Workflow on an AWS CentOS Box

  1. Log into the development environment
    1. ssh centos@.aws.hubzero.org
  2. Go to the web root directory
    1. cd /var/www/
  3. Backup the existing code which will be necessary to preserve the configuration files
    1. cv hub hub.bak
  4. Clone the development repository, naming it “hub” to preserve the preconfigured location that the web server (Apache) expects
    1. git clone https://gitlab.aws.hubzero.org/hubzero/hubzero-cms.git hub
  5. Copy the configuration, contained within the app directory, to the new installation
    1. cp hub.bak/app hub/
  6. Run composer to pull in external dependencies (including the HUBzero Framework)
    1. cd core && php ./bin/composer install
    2. cd ../
  7. Run database migrations
    1. php muse migration -i -f
  8. Go to the /var/www/ directory
    1. cd /var/www
  9. Change the owner and group of the hub directory to something that the web server agrees with
    1. chown apache:apache hub -R
  10. Change the file mode back to something permissible for development purposes. In production environments this is a little more locked down.
    1. chmod 775 hub -R
  11. Pull the latest code. Use the rebase command if you already have some commits that you haven’t pushed yet. This puts your work on top of the changes that come downstream.
    1. git pull (--rebase)
  12. Make some valid changes to the code such as fixing a bug.
  13. Add the file(s) to the commit.
    1. git add <file>
  14. Form the commit and add a descriptive message meeting the standardized message formatting requirements.
    1. git commit -m "[fix] Descriptive message"
  15. Push your changes upstream
    1. git push
  16. Open Merge Request on Gitlab
    1. This starts the code review process. Another developer must approve the code submission(s) before they enter the mainline.
    2. Once approved, an event triggers the change to be pushed into the production branch (located on github.com)

Situation: Deploying a hotfix to Stable/Production deployments

  1. Make the code fix.
  2. Create a commit on the development branches (2.1.0 and master).
  3. Push the commit, so that it may be included in the next release.
  4. Make a patch file.
    git format-patch -1 0c0e8b6213d5f5e26fb326ad51fb17db5f5df210 -o ~/patches/.
  5. Upload it to ansible directory.
    ansible-playbook update-production.yml -i hosts -u hubadmin --private-key=~/.ssh/kwojo-hippa-ansible --ask-vault-pass
  6. Run the ansible script (hotfix-prod).

0001-NCIPHUB-1288-PLG_AUTHENTICATION_SHIBBOLETH-Removing-.patch

Place the patch file into the patches directory in the ansible-cms-update repository.

Situation: Developing a feature targeting a future release

In order to prevent breaking commits from entering an idealistically production-ready

title: External Information System Services
content:
- REQUIRED for FISMA COMPLIANCE, DO NOT MOVE OR DELETE -

This documents how HUBzero connects to external information system services, and implements parts of controls SA-5 and SA-9.  Sub-pages document a specific external service or connection mechanism to external services, e.g., Shibboleth, Google Auth, Amazon SES.

title: Shibboleth
content:
Shibboleth is deployed using packages from a Linux Operating System's repositories, for example the libapache2_mod_shib2 in Debian Linux.  This module handles the SAML-based communication between the hub and the single sign-on providers, and places any user attributes that were established across a login into the environment variables for the request. These variables consist of users' email addresses at the SSO institution, their names, and an eduPersonPrincipalName, which is basically a username on the providers domain. Of these, only the last is required but the others can be used as shortcuts to fill in registration fields on the hub.

(attributes exchanged: https://spaces.internet2.edu/display/InCFederation/Research+and+Scholarship+Attribute+Bundle)
(module documentation, the only configuration we use is to require a valid user for the /login/shibboleth url: https://wiki.shibboleth.net/confluence/display/SHIB2/NativeSPApacheConfig)

In addition to the Apache module, the package includes a daemon that is configured separately (/etc/shibboleth/shibboleth2.xml)

Our configuration of this part of the service is as-shipped, except that we configure the service to use InCommon's metadata to federate with SSO services in the research and scholarship category (and as a special case with NIH):

       <MetadataProvider type="XML" uri="https://wayf.incommonfederation.org/InCommon/InCommon-metadata.xml" backingFilePath="federation-metadata.xml" reloadInterval="7200">
           <MetadataFilter type="RequireValidUntil" maxValidityInterval="2419200"/>
           <MetadataFilter type="Signature" certificate="inc-md-cert.pem"/>
       </MetadataProvider>

This configuration is in accordance with the service agreement with InCommon.

Additionally we add routing through our content management system code for the redirect stage of user login:

           <SSO discoveryProtocol="SAMLDS" ECP="true" discoveryURL="https://nciphub.org/login?authenticator=shibboleth&wayf">
                  SAML2 SAML1
           </SSO>
           <SessionInitiator type="Chaining" Location="/login/shibboleth" isDefault="true" id="Login">
               <SessionInitiator type="SAML2" template="bindingTemplate.html"/>
               <SessionInitiator type="Shib1"/>
               <SessionInitiator type="SAMLDS" URL="https://nciphub.org/login?authenticator=shibboleth&wayf"/>
           </SessionInitiator>

What this does is to set up that URL on the hub as a service that answers the question "where do I redirect a user requesting to log in with this particular entity ID?" The Shibboleth software is capable of doing something like this without the intermediate step but we'd like to check in with the content management system's database to be sure that any given entity is enabled, a precaution that helps us avoid offering logins through institutions that will not supply the required EPPN attribute or that misbehave in any other way.

(documentation about this configuration file: https://wiki.shibboleth.net/confluence/display/SHIB2/NativeSPShibbolethXML)

Finally, there is public-facing configuration, which can find in its entirety by searching for nciphub in the InCommon metadata here: https://wayf.incommonfederation.org/InCommon/InCommon-metadata.xml

This is pretty standard, containing a note about our research & scholarship affiliation, which enables more providers to release attributes to us, the technical information needed by their software to interface with us (public key and endpoint URLs), some user-facing information like the site name, description, and support contacts, and the list of the attributes our service is interested in.

Source:  Description provided by Steven Snyder, author of the Shibboleth plugin, at https://help.hubzero.org/support/ticket/8065

title: Google Authentication
content:
"Sign in with Google" implemented by HUBzero uses OAuth 2.0 as follows:

  • The majority of the code uses the Google API Client library provided by Google (/libraries/google-api-php-client).  The google php client library follows the standard OAuth2 protocol.  
  • All of our customers should have separate client ids/secrets as the Google api console requires the redirect domain to match the application domain.  These (client ID and client secret) are stored as plugin param values (params are a JSON encoded string in the 'params' field of the #__extensions database table).
  • It doesn't use a refresh token. Refresh tokens apply primarily to longer lived access to the Google api.  Because we only make one call (to the authentication endpoint), which by definition includes explicate authentication from the user, the need for a refresh token is irrelevant.  The refresh token would come into play if, for example, people were able to do other google related api actions (like posting something to their google plus account) without explicitly authenticating for each action.
  • The access token is stored in the user's session data.

Source: Shawn Rice and Samuel Wilson in https://help.hubzero.org/support/ticket/8064

title: Outgoing email via Amazon SES
content:
The Sherlock environment doesn't allow outgoing emails.  In order to send emails, we use Amazon SES.  For example, we need to notify users of ticket updates.  The confidentiality of tickets is preserved on HIPAA-covered hubs by not emailing the contents of the tickets, and only sending notices that there were updates to the ticket (this is a configuration item).   The connection to Amazon SES is done as follows:

1. Request Port 587 to be allowed through the Sherlock HTTP proxy to the Amazon SES SMTP server we are using "email-smtp.us-east-1.amazonaws.com" .

2. Install the required SASL packages

3. Configure Postfix on the hub host to relay email to the AWS STMP server via port 587 with the appropriate AWS SES username and SASL password and the following options. 

SASL options:
smtp_sasl_auth_enable = yes
smtp_sasl_security_options = noanonymous
smtp_sasl_password_maps = hash:/etc/postfix/sasl_passwd
smtp_use_tls = yes
smtp_tls_security_level = encrypt
smtp_tls_note_starttls_offer = yes
smtp_tls_CAfile = /etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt

title: Sherlock Change Request Form
content:
The Request for Change email format below is intended to provide an easy to understand tag or bullet approach to convey critical information, to set expectations and to convey urgency or lack thereof for the requested change.

 

A new email should be written and configured to include all of the following and at least one option from each:

TO field.

CC field.

A tag of [Issue] or [Request].  ** [Issue] is to be used when requesting a change to resolve an issue. [Request] is to be used for all other requests.

A tag of [Dev], [Stage] or  [Prod].  ** Refers to a development, staging or production host environment.

A tag of [Work Impaired: Unknown],[Work Impaired: Yes], or [Work Impaired: No].  ** Refers to whether or not an end-uses, client, or staff member's work is directly impacted by what is needed in the request.

A tag of [Requested Max Resolution: "time_frame" ] ** "time_frame" should be an integer of days or weeks and refers to the time to completion that may be needed.

A tag of [Impact:  "impact_description"].  ** "impact_description" is a description that provides a sense or urgency or lack thereof for the request on a user or group of users.

 

Body of the email should describe the request.  Examples are below.

(Click here to start an email with all the options above)

title: log4j Vulnerabilities circa December 2021
content:
Hubzero systems have been inspected and found not to be vulnerable to the reported Log4J security issues found in December 2021.

Hubzero uses Log4J version 1.2 as part of the hubzero-solr package where JMSAppender or JNDI are not configured.  Both the version of Log4J and lack of concerning configuration options result in the system not being vulnerable to this particular incident.

Hubzero is aware that Log4J 1.2 has reached end of life. Upgrading to a more recent version has been planned in the near future.

title: Hubzero VPAT (v.2.2.22)
content:
A Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT™) is a document that explains how information and communication technology (ICT) products such as software, hardware, electronic content, and support documentation meet (conform to) the Revised 508 Standards for IT accessibility. VPAT™ help Federal agency contracting officials and government buyers to assess ICT for accessibility when doing market research and evaluating proposals.

Government solicitations which include ICT will specify accessibility requirements, indicating which provisions are required to ensure the deliverable is accessible. A VPAT™ is a good way to address the accessibility requirements defined in the solicitation.

We recommend that vendors generate a VPAT™ for any ICT that’s intended to be marketed to the Federal government. Use the VPAT™ to make specific statements in simple recommended language to demonstrate how the features and functional characteristics of your product meet the Revised 508 Standards.

 

 

In 2022, Hubzero preformed an accessibility review on the Hubzero Platform through the NCIhub production instance:

Hubzero VPAT - v2.2.22, updated June 3, 2022

title: Catalyzecare
content:
SOLR uses for CatalyzeCare:

The only SOLR instance running on catalyzecare.org is HUBzero's version related to our instance of SOLR search. REMEDI utilizes a separate SOLR instance to act as REMEDI's database, which is running on a db.catalyzecare.org.

VPN profile webvpn.purdue.edu/rche-hub

This VPN profile grants access to the 128.46.20.0/24 network, utilized for the Hadoop cluster (see below) and possibly other projects related to Adib's work.  Membership in the Active Directory group "PWL_319_HUBzero_Rche" allows the use of that VPN.  Membership in that group is changed via emailing activedirectory@purdue.edu (not accounts@purdue.edu);  they currently expect requests to come from pmeunier@purdue.edu.

This VPN gets a dedicated IP pool from which all connections will be made: 172.21.83.0/24.  A rule in the network firewall rule allows those IP into the Hadoop cluster network 128.46.20.0/26.

 

CatalyzeCare Hardware:

CatalyzeCare has additional hardware - dash.catalyzecare.org, db.catalyzecare.org, and the mimic mini-cluster.

There is a direct cable link between db.catalyzecare.org and catalyzecare.ogre.hubzero.org, used for unencrypted communications between db and all the containers on catalyzecare.ogre.

Catalyzecare also hosts the Mimic project using SciDB, with a mini-cluster:

  • mimic.catalyzecare.org
    • Runs Apache as an authenticating proxy in front of R-Shiny
      • listens on port 3838
      • Basic password authentication
      • Change a user's password with "htpasswd /etc/httpd/htpasswd.users username"
    • Runs multiple instances of PostGreSQL, one is for scidb, a different one for R-Shiny access
      • /etc/init.d/postgresql-shiny.8.4 manages shiny (version 8.4, PGPORT=5433, configuration at /opt/scidb/postgres-datadir/data-shiny/postgresql.conf)
      • /etc/init.d/postgresql-scidb.9.3 manages scidb (version 9.3, PGPORT=5432, configuration at /var/lib/pgsql/9.3/data/postgresql.conf)
    • All access to the MIMIC database must follow this procedure, through a project in Physionet.org:

      1. The person is added to the project https://physionet.org/works/MIMICPurdue/

      2. MIT verifies the person is approved for the use

      3. Felipe Torres Fabregas ftorres@mit.edu creates the account using the script /root/mkshinyusr.sh

      4. This procedure applies to both Purdue and Non-Purdue users

         

  • mimic2.catalyzecare.org
  • mimic3.catalyzecare.org
  • mimic4.catalyzecare.org

In addition, a Hadoop cluster is in MATH G190 rack E-33 using VLAN 128.46.20.0/26, dual-stack network with 2607:AC80:201::/64 for IPv6.  It uses the name space hdp1.catalyzecare.org.  Its nodes are:

  • mgt.hdp1.catalyzecare.org (VM for availability/uptime/packages)
  • edge1.hdp1.catalyzecare.org ("login" node)
  • ma01.hdp1.catalyzecare.org (Name node 1)
  • ma02.hdp1.catalyzecare.org (Name node 2)
  • dn01-8.hdp1.catalyzecare.org

Security information:

The host dash.catalyzecare.org has both a host and a network firewall.  Port 22 is allowed by both, but only to specific whitelisted IPs and small networks.  In addition, dash is configured to allow logins to complete only from those IP addresses and small networks.  Therefore, dash is protected by 3 layers of enforcement, in addition to only allowing authentication via strong SSH keys.  

upload.dash.catalyzecare.org

Only the host upload.dash.catalyzecare.org (a stripped-down, hardened container dedicated to use for uploads only) allows port 22 from the world.  

upload.dash.catalyzecare.org is used as a one-way drop-box for HIPAA-covered information.  People can SSH from the world over, but must use an SSH key, and can only use SFTP to their own drop-box (no terminal).  Catalyzecare staff move files out of there to dash for processing.

 

db.catalyzecare.org MySQL Access

db.catalyzecare has a dedicated, shared user account allowing port forwarding to MySQL and only that.  Public SSH keys are added to /hometunneler/rche_ipi_tunnel/.ssh/authorized_keys so there are no shared credentials, and individual users can be added and removed without having to reset a password.  The account doesn't accept a password anyway:  password login is disabled.  Users don't get a shell, can't forward X11 or do port forwarding to another host.  Usage and port forwarding to the MySQL server are as described in the "Access through SSH" section of our MySQL procedures at /documentation/infosec/procedures/technical/mysql

title: MyGeoHub
content:
Code repos: https://gitlab.hubzero.org/mygeohub

Projects

/srv/irods is from projects iData storage, /srv/mygeohub/projects is from the standard "default CMS storage provider", i.e., it is stored on the mygeohub.org web server.  The two are separate, and /srv/mygeohub/projects is expected to contain the files intended to be public.  The standard project area needs to be exported to any execution hosts over NFS.

iRODS Project Storage

This storage is provided by the server gabbs-irods.rcac.purdue.edu,128.211.140.84, to irods_user_name "mygeohub". 

iRODS Firewall Rules

The service needs access to client ports 2093, allowed by a host firewall rule like:

-A TCPIN -s 128.211.140.84/32 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 2093 -j ACCEPT

and network firewall rules like:

access-list 128.046.019.000/24-Outside_access_in extended permit tcp host 128.211.140.84 host 128.46.19.45 eq 2093

access-list 128.046.021.000/24-Outside_access_in extended permit tcp host 128.211.140.84 host 128.46.21.63 eq 2093

access-list 128.046.021.000/24-Outside_access_in extended permit tcp host 128.211.140.84 host 128.46.21.64 eq 2093

OpenVZ containers need to reach that server with host firewall rules like:

-A FORWARD -d 128.211.140.84/32 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 1247 -j ACCEPT

-A FORWARD -d 128.211.140.84/32 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 20000:20199 -j ACCEPT

For development (dev.mygeohub.org), port 2090 is used instead:

-A TCPIN -s 128.211.140.84/32 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 2090 -j ACCEPT

iRODS Fuse Patch Compilation

Obtain the patch file "irods-fuse.patch" and apply to the latest 4.1 release of iRODS.  See also the Debian version, with an archived version of the patch at https://help.hubzero.org/groups/production/wiki/irodsfs

git clone https://github.com/irods/irods.git
cd irods
git show-branch -a
git checkout 4-1-stable
cd
cd irods/iRODS
yum install patch
patch -p 2 < ../../irods-fuse.patch
cd ..
git submodule init; git submodule update
yum install gcc-c++ make python-devel rpm-build help2man unixODBC fuse-devel curl-devel bzip2-devel zlib-devel pam-devel openssl-devel libxml2-devel perl-JSON
packaging/build.sh icommands
ls ./build/
mv ./build/irods-icommands-4.1.12-64bit-centos5.rpm  ..
yum install irods-icommands-4.1.12-64bit-centos5.rpm

Make sure "fuse" is installed, and www-data or apache setup for it:

yum install fuse
# check if group fuse exists... if needed create it
# groupadd fuse
# chgrp fuse /bin/fusermount
# on an execution host, you might have to create a user because www-data/apache won't exist
# adduser apache --system --home /var/www -g apache
usermod -aG fuse apache
chown -R apache /var/www
vi /etc/fuse.conf 
# add line user_allow_other

 

iRODS Authentication and Debugging

User www-data needs to have a directory /var/www/.irods, containing a file irods_environment.json, and needs to be a member of the group "fuse".  The fuse configuration file must allow this:

# cat /etc/fuse.conf
user_allow_other

The iRODS mount show up like this:

exec031:~# mount -l -t fuse.irodsFs
irodsFs on /srv/irods type fuse.irodsFs (rw,nosuid,nodev,allow_other,user=www-data)

The mount is done with this command as user www-data:

su www-data -s /bin/bash
irodsFs -o nonempty,allow_other /srv/irods

You can debug access with the command "ils".  If you don't have the correct password you'll get an error:

exec031:~$ ils
Enter your current iRODS password:
failed with error -826000 CAT_INVALID_AUTHENTICATION
ienv

Finally the "iinit" command lets you enter the required password and store it for future use.  Without this step, the irodsFs command will not fully succeed and file operations will have an error like "ls: cannot access /srv/irods: Input/output error"

You should probably have a cron job doing something like this:

4-59/5   *  *  *  *    apache    mount -l -t fuse.irodsFs | grep -v vz > /dev/null; if [ $? -eq 1 ]; then echo 'iRods mount missing, trying to mount again'; irodsFs -o nonempty,allow_other /srv/irods; fi || true

Hydroshare

Tool sessions attempt to access files from Hydroshare.  When a session is started, table jos_auth_link is used to find  the Hydroshare "username" from the MyGeoHub "user_id", where "auth_domain_id" is "2" (Hydroshare is 2).   Then /srv/irods/hydroshare/username is mounted inside the tool session at /srv/irods/hydroshare.

mysql> describe  jos_auth_link;
+----------------+--------------+------+-----+-------------------+-----------------------------+
| Field          | Type         | Null | Key | Default           | Extra                       |
+----------------+--------------+------+-----+-------------------+-----------------------------+
| auth_domain_id | int(11)      | YES  |     | NULL              |                             |
| email          | varchar(255) | YES  |     | NULL              |                             |
| id             | int(11)      | NO   | PRI | NULL              | auto_increment              |
| params         | varchar(255) | YES  |     | NULL              |                             |
| password       | varchar(255) | YES  |     | NULL              |                             |
| user_id        | int(11)      | YES  |     | NULL              |                             |
| username       | varchar(255) | YES  |     | NULL              |                             |
| linked_on      | timestamp    | NO   |     | CURRENT_TIMESTAMP | on update CURRENT_TIMESTAMP |
+----------------+--------------+------+-----+-------------------+-----------------------------+

See MyGeoHub Ticket #999

title: Creating a Special Nanohub subversion repository
content:
Nanohub has a historical precedent of providing various "special" subversion
repositories.

These repositories are manually maintained in
/etc/apache2/nanohub.conf.d/svn-extra.conf This file is not automatically
regenereated so any changes to the LDAP authentication connection
settings (hostname, password, etc) have to be manually updated.

The me581 group has historically been re-created every fall. If creating a new
one rename the old (replace YEAR with the year the previous repository was
made for)

$ mv /opt/svn/group/me581 /opt/svn/group/me581-YEAR

To create "special" group repository:

$ cd /opt/svn/group
$ svnadmin create REPO_NAME --fs-type fsfs
$ chown www-data:www-data REPO_NAME

Sometimes special repository can get made in the "infrastructure"
subdirectory, although this is less common in recent history and its
future use is discouraged.

$ cd /opt/svn/infrastructure
$ svnadmin create REPO_NAME --fs-type fsfs
$ chown www-data:www-data REPO_NAME

Once the repository is created edit /etc/apache2/nanohub.conf.d/svn-extra.conf
and copy a similar group or infrastructure stanza and replace the copied
repository name with your new one. Typically such a stanza will look similar
to:

<Location /groups/REPO_NAME/svn>
        DAV svn
        SVNPath /opt/svn/groups/REPO_NAME
        AuthType Basic
        AuthBasicProvider ldap
        AuthName "REPO_NAME" Subversion Repository"
        AuthzLDAPAuthoritative on
        AuthLDAPBindDN "cn=search,dc=nanohub,dc=org"
        AuthLDAPBindPassword "LDAP_PASSWORD"
        AuthLDAPGroupAttributeIsDN off
        AuthLDAPGroupAttribute memberUid
        AuthLDAPURL ldap://nanohub.org/ou=users,dc=nanohub,dc=org
        Require ldap-group cn=REPO_NAME,ou=groups,dc=nanohub,dc=org
</Location>

With REPO_NAME replaced with your new repository name and LDAP_PASSWORD
replaced with the current nanohub ldap password. You should copy a stanza
from the current file to be sure to get latest format. "groups" could also
be replaced with "infrastructure" if you wanted to create an "infrastructure"
group (discouraged).

Special Authorization (e.g., ME581)
===================================

You can create per directory access control in subversion. This has been
done for the special /tools/nemo/svn repository (a special case of the standard
tool repository configuration) and the special /group/me581/svn repository.
It is create by adding the file /opt/svn/groups/REPO_NAME/conf/svnauthz.conf

The format of the file for me581 looks like

[groups]
me581=username1,username2,username3
me581-admin=lzentner,marisol,yourname,ta_names

[/]
@me581-admin = rw

[/username1]
username1 = rw

[/username2]
username2 = rw

[/username3]
username3 = rw

A small bash script can be written to generate the [/usernameN] segments, or
it can be done manually. The users in the @me581-admin SVN group have access
to everything in the repository. The individual usernameN accounts only have
access to the directory named after them as indicated.

To use the svnauthz.conf file you will need to change your configuration
stanza in svn-extra.conf by replacing

Require ldap-group cn=REPO_NAME,ou=groups,dc=nanohub,dc=org

with

AuthzSVNAccessFile /opt/svn/groups/REPO_NAME/conf/svnauthz.conf
Require valid-user

To initialize this repository it is necessary to create each of those
usernameN directories and commit them to the repository. Technically this can
be done by anyone in the me581-group but historically has been done by the
person creating the repository. (if you already have an me581 directory from a
previous year you will want to remove or rename it)

$ cd
$ svn checkout https://nanohub.org/groups/me581/svn me581
$ cd me581
$ mkdir username1 username2 username3
$ svn add username1 username2 username 3
$ svn commit "create initial user directories"

A small bash script can be written to create all the directories or they can
be created manually.

If you later add a username to the svnauthz.conf file be sure to create and
commit a corresponding user directory.

 

This information is also located at /etc/apache2/nanohub.conf.d/svn-extra.README

title: Verilog-A Checker
content:
NanoHUB tool "VALint: the NEEDS Verilog-A Checker" has a dedicated CMS-defined user, runvacheck, which is used to analyze code in various projects.  This was a project completed by Jeff Turkstra circa early 2016.  It works like this:

  • www-data runs /opt/hubzero/vacheck
  • /opt/hubzero/vacheck uses VirtualSSH to start tool sessions as user runvacheck
  • Code of various projects can be checked using /srv/projects/<projectname>/vacheck
  • Sends emails to jeff+vacheck@purdue.edu
  • See /apps/vachecker/current

Questions:

  • Is there a cron job running it?
  • Are the tests still being run?

title: MySQL replication to db2.nanohub.org
content:
Production MySQL is replicated to db2.nanohub.org located at Purdue through an SSH tunnel.

SSH tunnel

The SSH tunnel is monitored and re-established as necessary by the cron fragment /etc/cron.d/replication_sshtun, checking every 10 minutes.

*/10 * * * *   root   /usr/sbin/lsof -i :2000 -P | grep -q localhost:2000;  [ $? -ne 0 ] && ssh -i /root/replication_ssh_tunnel/id_rsa  -f db2replication@web01.int.nanohub.org -L 2000:127.0.0.1:3306 -N

The tunnel appears as local port 2000 and connects using the account db2replication which is local to the web server.  The SSH key pair is in root/replication_ssh_tunnel.

 

Account "db2replication"

db2replication has uid 417, home /home/db2replication.  The authorized_keys file is restricted to the IP address of db2.nanohub.org (128.46.19.131).  The account needs to be in the group "access-sshfwd".  If it's not, then trying to start replication while the SSH connection is up, will produce errors like "channel 2: open failed: administratively prohibited: open failed".


Procedure to setup replication

logical copy of nanohub_annualreport and nanohub_annualreport2019 using backups

# on db2.  Because db2 is not exposed to internet.
scp -i /root/.ssh/rsync_id_rsa nanohub.org:/var/log/mysql_backups/nanohub_annual* /root
gunzip -dc /root/nanohub_annualreport.sql.gz | mysql
gunzip -dc /root/nanohub_annualreport2019.sql.gz | mysql
/bin/rm -f /root/nanohub_annual*
# Verify that # rows match by getting counts on both db2 and nanohub2
for table in `mysql -B --skip-column-names nanohub_annualreport -e "SHOW TABLES"`; do
  echo $table
  mysql -B --skip-column-names nanohub_annualreport -e "select count(*) from $table"
done
for table in `mysql -B --skip-column-names nanohub_annualreport2019 -e "SHOW TABLES"`; do
  echo $table
  mysql -B --skip-column-names nanohub_annualreport2019 -e "select count(*) from $table"
done

Logical transfer of nanohub databases except annualreports

# on web01.int.nanohub.org, flush tables so the dump is faster
echo flushing tables
while :
do 
  { time mysql -e "FLUSH TABLES;" > /dev/null; } 2>&1 | grep real  | grep 0m0 > /dev/null
  if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then 
    break
  else
    echo flushing again until it takes less than 1 second
  fi
  sleep 1
done
mysql -e "FLUSH TABLES WITH READ LOCK; FLUSH LOGS; SHOW MASTER STATUS; system /usr/share/adm/scripts/replication_dump;

Where /usr/share/adm/scripts/replication_dump is a one-liner that is awkward to put into the system command:

mysqldump --opt --dump-slave --apply-slave-statements --quote-names --routines --databases nanohub narwhal nanohub_centers network citations | /usr/bin/pigz --no-name > /var/log/mysql_backups/db2_dump.sql.gz
# transfer the mysql backup files to db2.nanohub.org
scp -i /root/.ssh/rsync_id_rsa nanohub.org:/var/log/mysql_backups/db2_dump.sql.gz /var/lib/mysql/
# on nanohub:  /bin/rm -f /var/log/mysql_backups/db2_dump.sql.gz
# dump metrics too:
mysqldump --opt --quote-names --routines --databases nanohub_metrics | /usr/bin/pigz --no-name > /var/log/nanohub_metrics.sql.gz
# stop mariadb on db2.nanohub.org
service mariadb stop
# on db2:
rm /etc/cron.d/ogre_crontab
vi /etc/cron.d/mysql_crontab
# prepare to load by resetting slave
screen -L -S "mysqld_safe" 
/bin/rm /var/lib/mysql/mariadb-relay-bin.*
/bin/rm /var/lib/mysql/relay-log.info 
mysqld_safe --skip-slave-start

# new db2 terminal
# for some reason "RESET SLAVE" fixes things that "RESET SLAVE ALL;" doesn't
mysql -D mysql -e "RESET SLAVE;"
mysql -D mysql -e "RESET SLAVE ALL;"

# drop old databases to ensure we have new data only
# mysql
drop database nanohub;
drop database narwhal;
drop database nanohub_centers;
drop database network;
drop database citations;
ctrl-D

# all the sql dump contains to help set slave values is statements like these:
# STOP SLAVE;  CHANGE MASTER TO MASTER_LOG_FILE='mysql-bin.015706', MASTER_LOG_POS=15944032;  START SLAVE;
# we need more, still need to set correct username and password, SSL_CA, etc...
replicate_pwd=`cat /etc/mysql/replicate_metric.pwd`
mysql -D mysql -e "CHANGE MASTER TO 
  MASTER_HOST='127.0.0.1',
  MASTER_USER='replicate_metric',
  MASTER_PASSWORD='$replicate_pwd',
  MASTER_PORT = 2000,
  MASTER_CONNECT_RETRY = 1;"

# load SQL
screen -L -S "load nanoHUB SQL" 
TMOUT=0
time gunzip -dc /var/lib/mysql/db2_dump.sql.gz | mysql
rm /var/lib/mysql/db2_dump.sql.gz
ctrl-a-d
tail -f screenlog.0 

# ctrl-C in mysqld_safe --skip-slave-start window
service mariadb start
mysql -D mysql -e "STOP SLAVE;"

# transfer and load metrics

scp -i /root/.ssh/rsync_id_rsa nanohub.org:/var/log/nanohub_metrics.sql.gz /var/lib/mysql/
time gunzip -dc /var/lib/mysql/nanohub_metrics.sql.gz | mysql
rm /var/lib/mysql/nanohub_metrics.sql.gz
# nanohub: /bin/rm /var/log/nanohub_metrics.sql.gz

mysql -D mysql -e "START SLAVE;"
mysql -e "SHOW SLAVE STATUS\G"
# if slave has trouble starting due to duplicate statements:
# mysql -e "SET GLOBAL SQL_SLAVE_SKIP_COUNTER=1
# mysql -D mysql -e "START SLAVE;"
while :; do  st=`mysql -e "SHOW SLAVE STATUS\G" | grep "Seconds_Behind_Master" | cut -d ":" -f2`; if [ $st = "NULL" ]; then    mysql -e "SET GLOBAL SQL_SLAVE_SKIP_COUNTER=1; START SLAVE";   echo "skipping..."; else   echo slave is running;   break; fi; sleep 1; done

mysql -e "SHOW SLAVE STATUS\G"

title: Instanton server
content:
The caching server instanton2.nanohub.org caches tool results, uncompressed.  Periodic compression runs are necessary or else the /home partition will run out of space, due to space consumed in /home/users/instanton/ for the cached results.  There is a cron job in /var/spool/cron/instanton that runs compression scripts daily as user "instanton":

@daily /home/users/instanton/bin/packArchive.sh; /home/users/instanton/bin/packEnqueued.sh

title: Salesforce Links
content:
nanoHUB has an integration with Salesforce. The ability for a user to follow a single-click instant login link provided by a Safesforce campaign to modify their profile fields.


Current Solution:

Set to expire: May 1, 2023

The expiration is now set to next year.  Nick identified the table and I took it from there.  For future reference:

update jos_reply_access_codes set expiration = '2023-05-01 23:59:59';

The expiration was set to '2022-05-01 23:59:59' for all codes so it seemed to be the right table.

 

[Issue reported on September 15, 2022]

Generated codes were not occuring from the connected cron_job, "Generate com_reply access codes for new users". Pascal investigated and discovered the following:

  • The existing plugin doesn't log any commands in the code to display errors
  • The plugin has a notion of "active pages" and these pages have an expiration date. Active pages are those that aren't expired yet.  It only generates codes if there exists an active page, and there isn't any that isn't expired.
  • The pages in there expired last May 2022, "2022-05-01 23:59:59"

Resolution: Pascal changed the expiration date on those pages and manually ran the cron plugin again. The new access codes were generated for the missing accounts.

Solution: update jos_reply_pages set next_expiration = '2023-05-01 23:59:59';

 

Future Development:

See document: https://docs.google.com/document/d/189MeCnRlJNQQuUJUKN8wSYDuFS-nqmG0ZlCJPm2uut4/edit?usp=sharing

title: Purdue Communityhub
content:
Storefront

ECN and ITaP have "storefronts" on Communityhub.  The filesystem area is located at /www/communityhub/app/storefront/, with subdirectories "ecn" and "itap". Memberships in the groups "access-ecn" and "access-itap" are respectively required to modify them.  That membership is controlled by Ogre.

 

Data Depot Usage

Larry L Biehl's account is used to connect to Data Depot via SSHFS.

biehl@data.rcac.purdue.edu:/depot/phenosorg/data/purdue is mounted on /data/communityhub/groups/phenosorg/depot type fuse.sshfs (rw,noatime,user_id=0,group_id=0,allow_other)

Despite the "allow_other" flag, the mount is somewhat protected by the permissions on the enclosing directory, /data/communityhub/groups/phenosorg:

drwxrws--- 3 www-data phenosorg

 

This allows people in the phenosorg group to share data, in particular "to use the file launcher capability (like MultiSpec and other tools) to be able to view the data."

See ticket request by Larry Biehl at https://communityhub.purdue.edu/support/ticket/129

 

One interesting thing is that the ownership and group are set by the mount operation to always be www-data:phenosorg no matter who writes in the directory. This is in /etc/fstab:

sshfs#biehl@data.rcac.purdue.edu:/depot/phenosorg/data/purdue    /data/communityhub/groups/phenosorg/depot  fuse  defaults,_netdev,intr,IdentityFile=/etc/sshfs-keys/phenosorg_id_rsa,uid=33,gid=1014,noatime,nonempty,reconnect,allow_other  0  2

Note the use of /etc/sshfs-keys/ to store the private key, perhaps this is something we could use across hubs.

Because files are owned by www-data, they could be managed and made available for download by code at: /www/communityhub/app/site/projects/phenosorgprojec

title: PURR
content:
Code repos: https://gitlab.hubzero.org/purr

Public Anonymous FTP Access to Publications

PURR offers anonymous FTP access to publications, using "passive mode", using the software "Pure-FTPD".   The home directory of user "ftp" is the directory being served (/var/www/purr/app/site/publications/ftp). 

Manual Access

With "anonymous access" you can enter any value for username and password;  they are ignored.  "Passive mode" must be selected in the client or the connection will fail.  An example access with a command line client is:

$ ftp -p purr.purdue.edu
Connected to purr.purdue.edu.
220-Public Anonymous Access to Purdue University Research Repository
220-All activity is monitored and may be recorded and audited.
220-Usage indicates consent to monitoring and recording.
220-Username and password do not matter, press "Enter" when prompted
220 Only anonymous FTP is allowed here
Name (purr.purdue.edu:user):
331 Any password will work
Password:
230 Any password will work
Remote system type is UNIX.
Using binary mode to transfer files.
ftp> cd ftp
250 OK. Current directory is /ftp
ftp> ls

227 Entering Passive Mode (128,46,19,76,200,62)
150 Accepted data connection
drwxrwsr-x    2 1000       121                 4 Sep 12 12:28 .
drwxrwsr-x 1842 1000       121              1843 Sep 12 12:53 ..
-rw-rw-r--    1 1000       121         117645298 Aug 10 09:35 03046.02111.zip
226-Options: -a -l
226 3 matches total
ftp> get 03046.02111.zip
local: 03046.02111.zip remote: 03046.02111.zip
227 Entering Passive Mode (128,46,19,76,202,37)
150-Accepted data connection
150 114888.0 kbytes to download

Users are expected to use the "ftp" directory but can also dig in the numbered pulications if they know which they need.

Automatic Access

PURR is supposed to automatically provide FTP URI instead of HTTP ones for large publications, when clicking the "Download Bundle" link.  For example, https://purr.purdue.edu/publications/2879/1 should be downloaded using FTP.  Browsers should open these URI without any further user intervention, e.g., clicking on this link:  ftp://purr.purdue.edu/ftp/03046.02111.zip should download the same file as in the manual example above.

Implementation Details

  • The banner is set in the file /etc/pure-ftpd/welcome.msg
  • The root directory of the FTP service is /www/purr/app/site/publications/ftp
  • URI are expected to refer to the ftp subdirectory, which contains hard links to the publications
  • The hard links are the same files as in app/site/publications/NNNNN/NNNNN/bundles/bundle.zip
  • FTP access is read-only
  • The service reads files as user "ftp", so the files must be readable by "others", as they are owned by www-data and group "access-content"
  • (historical) The publications directory is a ZFS filesystem using storage on iscsi1.hubzero.org (see below)

Storage

PURR values 3 storage areas critical to its mission:

  • AIPs, stored at /srv/aip
    • /bin/mount -n --bind -o noatime /export/srv-zfs/aip /vz/root/2001/srv/aip
    • ZFS filesystem from storage on iscsi1.hubzero.org
  • Projects, stored at /srv/projects
    • /bin/mount -n --bind -o noatime /export/protection/datadepot-nfs/data/production/projects /vz/root/2001/srv/protection/projects
    • NFS mount from Data Depot
  • Publications, stored at /var/www/*/app/site/publications
    • /bin/mount -n --bind -o noatime /export/publications /vz/root/2001/www/purr/app/site/publications
    • ZFS filesystem from storage on iscsi1.hubzero.org

Data Depot proxy over NFS (historical)

Connecting to Data Depot requires channeling everything through a single user acting as a proxy.  It's easy to move /srv/projects to Data Depot because everything is owned by www-data.  The user www-data will therefore initiate and maintain the connection ("mount") to Data Depot.  It would be more complicated to move publications under /www due to the security model which allows other users than www-data to read and write files.  Trying to proxy this storage under a different user would result in security issues.  Either people who shouldn't would have access would have access due to the use of the "allow_other" option, or people who should have access, won't because only www-data would be able to access it.

Projects on Data Depot via SMB Connection (historical)

We tried to connect PURR to Data Depot via SMB and via SSHFS. Lessons learned are summarized here as a policy article.  We're now using NFS.

On Data Depot, everything written is owned by the dedicated service account, purrnfs.  Projects data is stored in /group/purr/data and access is controlled by membership in the group purr-data.   Only the dedicated service user purrnfs is in that group, as explained below.

As SMB access is public to Purdue, does not require 2-factor authentication and is only a password that could be exposed by the use of a weak authentication mechanism, everyone who has a career account and is in the purr-data group could act as a conduit for attackers to read or modify projects. To protect projects, stored in the /group/purr/data directory, "purrnfs" must be the only member of the purr-data group.

Data Depot Password

The password is changed via https://www.purdue.edu/apps/account/ChangePassword

Data Depot SSH

For additional management of the Data Depot storage (e.g., to resolve file ownership issues on the Data Depot side), it is possible to use SSH from production (purr.purdue.edu) to the purrnfs account using the key pair stored at /root/.ssh/datadepot_rsa, like so:

# ssh purrnfs@data.rcac.purdue.edu -i /root/.ssh/datadepot_rsa

Using the password to login is also possible but the password could expire.

Data Depot Storage Status

See https://www.rcac.purdue.edu/account/myquota/

Also, on purr.ogre.purdue.edu, by running this command:

df -hT --block-size=2k /export/protection/datadepot-nfs

Running df without the block-size option will return an incorrect value.

 

Sensitive project review/approval

PURR has a sensitive project approval group where Sara Rumpke from the FERPA Purdue Group approves projects via https://purr.purdue.edu/projects/browse/?reviewer=sensitive. When a project selects "Yes, my project is will be working on sensitive data" the group "sensitive_data_reviewers" receives an email.

title: Outage Record
content:
07/07/2019 - 07/09/2019

On 07/07, PURR had an annual reboot in which com_publicatons was not connecting after the reboot. Pascal was able to restore services 07/09/2019.

 

04/08/2019 - 04/09/2019

On 04/08 at 11:24 AM, the PURR team reported that files were not accessible via projects, which Claire assigned to the CMS team at 11:27 AM. Around 12:50 PM, after an investigation from the CMS team and after delays due to absences on the team, a ticket was submitted to RCAC. Claire emailed Michael Witt and Sandi Caldrone with information that the HUBzero would have to involve the data depot team to achieve a fix at 1:10 PM.

The HUBzero team did not hear anything from the ticket and by 2:24 PM, Claire contacted Betsy Hillery, the manager of the group, to escalate the ticket. Betsy reported back at 2:46 PM and set-up a quick meeting with Claire and Shawn to share information that the way we have connected is not as reliable as another method, which they would share in the ticket. They shared the additional information at 5:24 PM with this message, "the NFS mount you've listed seems incorrect, as it is mounting directly from a single backend server and not making use of the clustered, highly available NFS exports for the Data Depot (granted, the address you were given could pre-date us setting up the clustered NFS system, which would certainly explain things).  Can you try mounting the Data Depot from depot-nfs.rcac.purdue.edu:/depot/purr?  That should provide failover so that in the event one of the servers becomes unresponsive, the rest of the servers in the cluster will take over for it. Can you please change the mount to depot-nfs.rcac.purdue.edu:/depot/purr and let me know if that resolves the issue?". At 5:54 PM, Claire messaged Pascal to see if the fix would be appropriate to help PURR, and also sent another notification to the PURR team that we heard back from the data depot team and were implementing a fix. Pascal was able to implement the fix from 6:30 - 6:42 PM.

Morning of 04/09, Claire closed the ticket at 8:26 AM. Sandi reported at 9:20 AM that the issue with folders not loading data was not resolved. HUBzero system administrators were contacted at 9:25 AM to reevaluate the issue. Upon spending the morning and until 1:23 PM rebooting and checking the connection with data depot, the issue was deemed to be related to the web interface, not system side. The issue was discussed upon by the entire team and at 2:25 PM the issue was pinpointed and a hotfix was submitted to PURR at 3:07 PM. Testing occurred after and Claire confirmed that project files were appearing again, and asked for confirmation from the PURR team in ticket #2016 at 3:11 PM.

 

12/18/2018

Around 3:30 PM scripts started alerting that multiple Data Depot mounts were unavailable, including the PURR mount on the backup server, archive4.  Due to a large number of alerts, I believed it was a complete outage of the Data Depot service. 

Further investigation with the help of RCAC, revealed that the NFS service on production PURR was OK.  It was only an SSH service outage, due to the SSH keys of the Data Depot server having unexpectedly changed.  The reason for the change was that it had been rebuilt on new hardware, and the host keys not copied.  I deleted the keys and accepted the new ones and SSH service was available again around 10:45 AM on 12/19. I deleted the incorrect backup that was made yesterday with the bad SSHFS mount.  So, there was no actual impact on production PURR.

title: SmarterAgriculture
content:
Code repos: https://gitlab.hubzero.org/smarterag

Data Depot and com_uav

Data Depot is mounted at /www/dev/app/components/com_uav/datadepot on dev, production and qa, for the specific purpose of making contents from Data Depot available through SmarterAg. The mount is NOT made via /etc/fstab because that would require the "allow_others" option, which decreases security. The private SSH key is stored at /etc/sshfs-keys/datadepot. The cron job "/etc/cron.d/sshfs" checks every 10 minutes that the mount is still OK and remounts it otherwise. This also allows restarting Apache, which is necessary when remounting it.

  It connects to smartag@data.rcac.purdue.edu:/depot/smarterag/data and is read-only.  It is readable by www-data only:

dev:~# su www-data
h:w$ ls /www/dev/app/components/com_uav/datadepot
From SMS program  PAC_fields  datadepot.pub  drone_data  test  trait_ontology.txt  trait_ontology_raw.txt  trait_ontology_short.txt  zegami_test

Apache must be configured to not execute PHP files in the directory com_uav/datadepot.  This is done by Ogre with the configuration option:

@define NO_PHP_DIRS {"app/components/com_uas/datadepot"}

which creates this in /etc/apache2/sites-available:

        <Directory /www/smartag/app/cache>
                <FilesMatch  ".(php|phtml|pht|phps|php3|php3p|php4|php5|php6)$">
                  deny from all
                </FilesMatch>
                AllowOverride None
        </Directory>

As of October 2019, this stores a lot of data:

$ du -hxs /depot/smarterag/data
99T    /depot/smarterag/data
 

Data Depot and /data

Data Depot is mounted with sshfs at /data/smartag/groups/demogroup/depot from gcore@data.rcac.purdue.edu:rick_working, on production.  This uses /etc/fstab and the "allow_other" option.  The parent directory, "/data/smartag/groups/demogroup" restricts access to www-data and members of the group "demogroup".

title: Intro: The Hubzero Platform
content:
Hubzero® is an open source software platform for building powerful websites supporting scientific discovery, learning, and collaboration. Some refer to such web sites as “collaboratories” or  “team science.” We call them “Hubs” because each site becomes a focal point for its user community.

Originally created by researchers at Purdue University in conjunction with the NSF-sponsored Network for Computational Nanotechnology to support nanohub.org, the Hubzero platform now supports dozens of Hubs across a variety of disciplines, including cancer research, pharmaceuticals, climate modeling, volcanology, and more.

A Hub provides a powerful content management system including features facilitating scientific activities such as Simulation, Publication and Collaboration.

  • Simulation - Interactive computation and analytical tools can be deployed on a hub using Linux or even web-based widgets in your favorite coding language - all hosted on the Hub and accessible through a web interface.
  • Publication - Publishing research results, datasets, tools, and papers via a guided process.
    • Resources - Many types of content can be published as determined by the individual hub leadership team.  Simulation Tools are included at a type of resource to be published.
    • Publications - A parallel guided process to Resources where all published research materials will procure a DOI.
  • Collaboration - Spaces for research teams and collaborators to discuss research topics, share files, etc.
    • Groups  - A Group is a collection of users, content, and discussions to connect people with a common interest privately or publicly with the world.
    • Projects - A Project is a collection of users and content focused on publishing data, papers or publications.

See our documentation site at https://hubzero.org/documentation.

title: Attendance Policy
content:
The attendance policy is designed to clearly communicate attendance expectations, and procedures for reporting absences or tardiness. Consequences for absences and tardiness may include disciplinary action up to and including termination. A total of two excused absences are allowed throughout the course of an academic semester. No unexcused absences are permitted.
  • Scheduling: Students are required to coordinate with their supervisor and determine a regular work schedule for each semester.
  • Notification of Tardiness: Students who find they will be tardy are required to notify the supervisor via email at least 15 minutes prior to the start of their shift.
  • Excused Absences: Students are allowed two excused absences due to illness, personal time or academic scheduling during a semester without penalty. Students are required to notify their supervisor as soon as possible when a a scheduled shift will be missed due to illness.  Students are required to notify their supervisor 48 hours prior to the scheduled shift that will be missed. Subsequent absences due to illness will be considered unexcused, unless proof of illness (physician’s note) is provided to your supervisor upon return.  If a note from a medical visit is provided for an illness, the absence(s) will be considered excused.
  • Unexcused Absence: Failure to attended a scheduled work time or tardiness greater than 15 minutes without any communication with your supervisor will be considered an unexcused absence.
  • Disciplinary Measures: Students will be notified when they are approved both of their excused absences. If a student accumulates an unexcused absence, a meeting with their supervisor will be arranged for disciplinary action.
