title: Windows Tools
content:
The windows tool functionality on a Hub is not quite as comprehensive as the linux tool side, but we felt even limited Windows based tool support was a critical feature our team needed to add to meet our users' growing needs.

HUBzero utilizes Amazon's AppStream service to allow a Hub to offer windows based tools to its users. AppStream based Windows tools look and behave just like ordinary Windows applications, but they require a much different setup process than their Linux based X11 counterparts on a Hub.

title: Setup
content:
Overview

The HUBzero platform:

  • Offers an easy and convenient way to organize and present your AppStream Windows tools to your users. Windows tools are just another resource type in a hub, they launch seemlessly just like our regular tools, right inside the web browser.

  • Provides secure access to your tools to specific groups that can be closely managed and monitored.

  • Tracks detailed AppStream Windows tool usage.

  • Can map your users' HUBzero home directory to a drive inside your windows container.

The initial setup for Windows based tools on a hub is a two step process that requires a separate setup in Amazon Web Services AppStream service as well as your Hub.

Once your have the initial setup complete, you'll have to follow a brief setup for applications you wish to deploy on your hub.

AWS Security Setup (one time)

Your AWS User Account

Your HUBzero hub needs to be able to communicate with Amazon. You need to create a special user to allow this access in a secure way.

Create user policy

From your AWS console, click on the the 'Identity & Access Management" section. Click the "Policies" menu item from the left side menu. Click on the "Create Policy" button, then select the "Create Your Own Policy" section.

On the "Review Policy" page, enter the following:

Policy Name - AppStreamPolicy
Description - used by my hubzero hub to get access to AppStream sessions
The "Policy Doc" should contain the following text:

{
    "Version": "2012-10-17",
    "Statement": [
        {
            "Sid": "Stmt1456777171000",
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Action": ["appstream:*"],
            "Resource": ["*"]
        }
    ]
} 

Create user

From the 'Identity & Access Management" section, select 'Users" and then click on the "Create New Users" button. Enter "AppStreamOnly" user and click the "Create" button.

The next page will show you the User Security Credentials. Make a note of the "Access Key ID" and the "Secret Access Key", this will be the only time you can view all this info. If you do lose this, you can create another Key later if necessary, but the only time you'll be able to see the "Secret Access Key". Once you have made note of this, click the 'Close' button.

From the "Users" page, select your newly created user. Then select the "Permissions" tab and press the Attach policy button. Find your AppStreamPolicy, select it, then click the 'Attach' button in the lower right.

Hub Setup (one time)

setup your hub

Application setup steps

Application Setup

From your Amazon Web Services Management Console, there is a section for managing AppStream applications.

[SCREENSHOT 1 - AWS console]

On the AppStream applications page you'll see a list of available applications. You might have none. Click on the "Deploy an application" button. 

[SCREENSHOT 2 - Applications Page]

The "Set up your application" page has basic info about your application, complete the form. 

[SCREENSHOT 3 - Set up your application page]

When you have completed naming and describing your application, click on the "Open Windows & install your application". This will open up remote connection to a windows host, where you can install your application just like you would if you were installing it on your own computer. The Amazon AppStream Instruction page outlines the process 

  1. Copy your application to the Windows host - you have to get your application to this setup server. There are a number of ways you can do this, but utilizing a cloud file solution is often most simple method. Once you have uploaded your file to a cloud storage provider, you can log into the cloud service inside the web browser on this Windows host.

    In addition to installing your application on the windows host, you must also install a small Hubzero application available [here]. You should save it in the root of your c: drive on the windows host, so the path is "c:hubzerowrapperapp.exe".
  2. Install the application - This step is identical to how you would install your application on your laptop or desktop.
  3. Set the launch path - In order to have your AppStream application work with your hub, you need to have Amazon first launch the hubzerowrapperapp.exe program, and then launch your final application. When you click on the 'Set launch path" button, locate the hubzerowrapperapp.exe file by clicking on the 'Browse..." button. Once you have located the file click on 'open'.

    In the "Parameters (optional)" textbox, enter the text maphubdrive <path to your application>, so you should end up with something that looks like this:

    [SCREEESHOT 4 - Set Launch Path dialog box"]

Final step is to click "Deploy Application". AppStream will take a while to setup your application, anywhere from 30 minutes to several hours, but this is a one time setup.

After your Application is available

On your 'Applications' page, once your new application has a status of 'Running', click on it. There is some basic information about your application on thsi page, but the most important is the "Application ID". Make note of this value, you'll need this value later.

Now, we have to tweak several values on this page. Click the Log details section and then the 'Edit' button.

  1. Click the check mark for "Yes save application logs.
  2. Enter the text "C:UsersPublicAppStreamAppStream_OpaqueData.xml" in the text area below the checkbox
  3. And use the default bucket for "Save Location"
  4. Then press "Save"

title: Components
content:
Introduction

The Components section will house all internal documentation that specifies details affiliated with various components.

Extendable Project Description Documentation

Functional Specification

Project description pages will have a setting to allow PlantingScience.org administrators to add custom fields including i) text fields, ii) tags, iii) urls, iv) choice boxes.

The users, including teachers and students, will be able to edit these items throughout the life of the project.

Even if already filled in, they will be able to go back and edit them more when they click on the edit description area for a project.

Each such fill­in item will have the capability to have a short description above it that appears in the project description edit area, but which is not present when the project description is viewed in the normal, non­edit mode.

Administrative Usage Instructions

Hub administrators are responsible for configuration of the Custom Description Template before Projects may utilize the feature. Projects created before this option has been configured may retroactively populate the Custom Description Template after the setup is complete.

Enabling Custom Description

Administrators may log into the administrative backend to configure this option. By default, this feature is turned off and must be enabled by going into Components >> Projects >> Options >> Setup >> Allow Users to Edit Project Settings? >> Yes ­ Use custom description

Creating the Custom Description Template

Once the custom description has been enabled, a new button will appear on the administrative toolbar under the Projects Component.

Clicking this button will direct the administrator to the form builder. Clicking on a field type will allow the administrator to configure the element’s properties such as name, options, and description.

In this example, the “Text” field type has been chosen.

 

Clicking “Save” or “Save and close will set the Custom Description Template hub­wide for all projects.

 

 

Non­administrator usage instructions

Project managers may edit the project’s information at any time. If the Custom Description Template is configured, a project manager role may fill in the information requested by administrators.

 

 

Project Information Non­edit mode (before updating)

To project members, the following information is presented by default. It is created when the project is in the setup state. This view is accessed from within the project by clicking on the “Info” tab on the side navigation bar. To edit the project information, click on the Edit Project button in the top right­hand corner.

 

 

Project Information ­ Edit Mode

Within edit mode, the Project Manager may edit the fields that are presented in the information section of the project settings. Notice there fields under the set “Edit Info” which are mandatory for all projects. Fields in the “Edit Extended Info” are those configured in the Custom Description Template.

 

 

After filling out the requested information, click “Save Changes” to save the project information.

 

 

Project Information Non­edit mode (after updating)

Once the project information is saved, it will appear in the Project information section.

 

Handlers

Handlers - (plugin group that needs to be turned) scans through the files and can preview a detailed map with placeholders

HUBzero CMS Authentication - Fail2Ban Integration

Objective

To have the CMS handle user login banning in an attempt to deter brute force attacks.

 

CMS Configuration Page

The following settings are accessible from the CMS administrative backend.

These options are accessible by going to the User Menu ­ Members and Member Options.

User Password Reset Limit

The number of password resets per time period is limited. If the user attempts to reset their password at a threshold deemed by the HUB administrator as excessive, the following message is displayed.

User Failed Login Limit

The number of failed logins per time period is limited. If the user attempts to reset their password at a threshold deemed by the HUB administrator as excessive, the following message is displayed. This means that an individual's account is temporarily blocked until the time period expires.

IP­based Blocked User Limit

When the threshold of blocked user accounts per IP network is met, the CMS will trigger a Fail2Ban rule which will block incoming requests from an IP address for a period of time. This is the last line of defense as blocking an IP address may have unintended consequences ­ such as blocking a NAT­ed IP address which several valid users are using to access the hub.

Assumptions

This approach assumes that the system administrator has configured a jail and a system user account to execute (with sudo) Fail2Ban via the fail2ban­client utility.

On Debian Hosts, Fail2Ban should be version 0.9.5.

0.9.5­1~nd70+1 from http://neuro.debian.net/debian/ wheezy/main amd64 Packages

Setup & Configuration

There are a number of subsystems which need to be configured for this scheme to work properly.

 

sudo Configuration

A privileged user which can execute:

(root) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/fail2ban­client set hub­login banip [0­9.]* (root) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/fail2ban­client set hub­login unbanip [0­9.]*

This can be accomplished by adding a sudoers rule in /etc/sudoers.d/ that looks like:

www­data   ALL=(root)NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/fail2ban­client set hub­login banip [0­9.]*

Fail2Ban Configuration

The system administrator should configure Fail2Ban to create jails which the CMS can add offending IP address into. The amount of time that the ban is valid is configured in Fail2Ban.

The CMS will simply add IP addresses to the Fail2Ban jail which will trigger the Ban Action as specified in the rule set.

The following configuration are more of an example than anything. A seasoned system administrator will have crafted better rules.

[Sample] Jail Configuration

#

# JAILS

# /etc/fail2ban/jail.local

#

[hub­login] enabled  = true

port      = http,https filter      = hub­login

logpath = /var/log/messages banaction = hublogin­failure bantime = 600

findtime = 1

maxretry = 1

 

 

 

[Sample] Filter Configuration

/etc/fail2ban/filter.d/hub­login.conf

Developer Commentary

This feature has been designed primarily with HUBzero’s production environment in mind. While it would be nice to implement a generalized feature set for all distributions, it simply is not within the scope of this undertaking. This feature should be revisited frequently to determine whether or not it is appropriate to keep within the code base ­ or implemented as a plugin. I chose not to implement this as a plugin as I did not necessarily see the need to separate this from the HUBzero Authentication Plugin as it’s the only vector which is vulnerable to brute­force attacks which we have direct control over.

 

 

User Impact

When a large number of people intend on using the CMS, it may be wise to temporarily disable this feature (e.g. conference, class activity, etc). In the past, many conference goers have mistyped their password in a short period of time creating a false positive for normal Fail2Ban operation. This risk is mitigated by the fact that the number of blocked users is observed before triggering Fail2Ban.

 

This can be accomplished by turning this check off by going to the /administrator ­> Members ­> Member Options ­> Login Settings ­> Fail2Ban set to “Off”.

 

This implementation should give HUB owners more flexibility over their settings.

The task, then, is to combine these so that all the fields are complete, and the technical details all correspond exactly to what was generated in the second document by the software.

First, let’s clean up the generated metadata. A few things are going on that we need to unwind

  1. There is an XML comment at the very top that will soon be misleading, so we can delete it.
  2. The _ID=“some hex string” attribute is not actually used by InCommon, as seen in the example document, so we can delete that too.
  3. The XML namespacing is different in the generated document

OPTIONAL SUPPLEMENTARY MATERIAL ABOUT #3

Regarding the last, in XML you can define document that describe how particular tags work, and then link to those descriptions in documents using the tag in order to make their semantics self-documenting.

One of these descriptions is linked in the generated metadata and assigned a namespace of md: xmlns:md=“urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:metadata”`

These names are used so that even if two linked descriptions had two incompatible explanations of what an is, you can still specify that you’re talking about a particular definition with the prefix you see scattered throughout the document, md:

By leaving off the namespace, and simply using an attribute like xmlns=”(some URI that responds with the descriptive document)” you can set the global descriptive document for tags. If the opening tag here just read xmlns="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:metadata" none of the md: prefixes are required.

If you look at the very top of the InCommon metadata you can see that in the final home for the hub’s metadata this is exactly the case:

A lot of related descriptions are linked, but the important thing to note is that the global descriptive document matches what we have defined in the md: namespace.

So, imagining that the document is situated as one entity among many in this large document, we can see that the md namespace is superfluous. Thus,

LONG STORY SHORT FOR #3

We don’t need the md: prefix on any of the tags, nor we need the xmlns:md=“urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:metadata”

Newsletter Digest

Design Specification

This section outlines some of the technical considerations and original use­cases considered during the development of this feature. The functionality of this feature is best experienced when using the functionality in its intended use­case.

Objective

On a scheduled basis aggregate content from various sources (forums, resources, etc.) into digest emails to be sent to site members. Multiple digests may be active with varying timed intervals.

 

Solution

Since digest recurrence, email lists, and subscription handling are existing features of the Newsletter compo­

nent, it will be expanded to include auto­generated newsletters, built from a selectable list of data sources such as Publications and Resources.

 

Auto­Generated Newsletters

An option will be added to the Newsletters component for building an auto­generated newsletter. When this option is selected, the user will be presented with a list of various data sources to include in the newsletter.

 

Data Sources

Each data source will be a plugin that the Newsletter component can request data from and will represent an existing component and/or plugins on a hub.

Specifically:

  • Events
    • Latest Created
  • Resources
    • Latest Created
  • Feedaggregator (Approved Posts / Curated Newsfeed)
    • Latest Approved
  • Jobs
    • Latest Posted

 

Assumptions & Considerations

The solution outlined in this proposal is based upon the assumption of working from the current “core” or latest, default HUBzero CMS release with no modifications, overrides, or additions.

Any and all alterations to the standard CMS install will need to be evaluated on a case­by­case basis and may affect any proposed timeline. Alterations to 3rd­party extensions are not covered by the scope of this project and any such inclusion will necessitate extensions to the estimated timeline and cost.

 

Using the Newsletter Digest Feature

The newsletter digest feature is accessible to Hub administrators through the administrative backend. The creation of a digest email and scheduling the mailing is done via the Newsletter component interface.

 

Creating a Newsletter Digest

  1. Navigate to the Newsletter Component interface by clicking “Components” in the menu and then “Newsletter”.
  2. Assuming no newsletters have been created, you will be prompted to “Click here to create a new one!”. If you have already created a newsletter, you may click the “+” button located in the upper right­hand portion of the screen.

  1. Fill out the New Newsletter form with a name, alias, template, visibility preference, tracking preference, and the frequency of the digest mailing. Digest mailings may occur daily, weekly, or monthly.
  1. Click the “Save and Close” / (✓) button to create the newsletter. Stories may be added to the newsletter only after it has been created.

  1. Reopen the newsletter in order to add stories to the newsletter by clicking the title of the newsletter.

  1. To add content to a Digest Newsletter, click “Add Auto­Generated Story” located below the general information form that was filled out earlier.

  1. Choose a Data Source, a Title, the number of items to include, and a story template. The Story Preview will preview the data currently stored in the Hub’s database. This may change over time as more content is generated in the Hub and may differ between mailings.

  1. Repeat step 6 and step 7 for all desired content.
  2. Once finished, click the “Save” / (☆) Button, to add the story to the Newsletter Digest.
  3. After adding all desired stories to the Newsletter, give it a quick look­over by checking the checkbox next to the Newsletter and clicking the “Preview” / (☉) button.

  1. Although the template may vary, the content should be presented in the layout selected in step 7.

  1. In order for the Newsletter Digest to be sent out on the scheduled frequency (set in step 3), the initial mailing must be manually configured. To do so, highlight the checkbox next to the newsletter and click the “Send” / (✉) button.
  2. Select the Schedule and the Mailing List for the initial mailing. The frequency will update automatically and schedule future mailings. The selected mailing list will be inherited in future mailings as well.

  1. NOTE: The mailing list may grow or shrink between mailings as Hub users interact with the mailing system.
  2. NOTE: The “lookahead” scheduler may not handle “unsubscribes” between mailings. Recipients are added at the time of the previous mailing, if the user chooses to add or remove themselves from the mailing list between mailings, it will be reflected in the NEXT mailing.

 

  1. Once the initial mailing has been created click the “Send” / (✉) button. This will place the Newsletter in the queue to be processed and mailed out.
    1. This is handled by the CRON task
  1. A look at the Mailing tab under the Newsletter Component interface shows the successfully processed mailing, and the next scheduled mailing.

  1. If an attempt is made to resend the newsletter, it will indicate that there already is a scheduled mailing.

Notes and Recommended Use

  • It is advised that separate newsletters are created for each desired frequency. Eg: If it is desired to have a weekly and monthly digest sent out, create one newsletter for weekly content and frequency, and create another newsletter for monthly content and frequency.
  • In order to facilitate various layouts, HTML is utilized for layouts. It is highly recommended to use an HTML template and email for this content.
  • There is a hard limit at 20 items of content per story. Despite this hard limit, 3­5 items per story is recommended.
  • Changes to the auto­generated content is not supported.
  • Additional content sources may be added, however this is not a user­accessible feature and may require development time.

    • Not set up to automatically syncs
    • You have to manually sync files
    • In the Publication process on the Files attachment step you see all the different turned on File systems and you select the file you want to attach to your Publication then go next, once you click “Publish” the publication will grab the file, add it to the Project, then publish the file in the Publication
  • New Development
    • (2.1.0) Added Dropbox and GitHub adapters 
    • (Future Development) Globus adapter in the works – waiting on Globus to finish integrating on their end before we add it to core
      • Developers need to know: Projects connections (Connection types) needs to be populated with the names of the file system adapters which is a manual process; this process should be automated in the future
      • Reason: to appease GABBS and iRods to change the name

Publications - Series

Series - A publication that links to other publications; aggregations same as Resource series

  • Short Version: Table of context of a series of publications with one DOI for Series
  • Long Version: When you are contributing a Publications the file types you attach are actually other Publications; these Publications change to links; each individual Publication maintains it's DOI but there is also a "master DOI" for the series Publicaiton
    • Master Type of Publication - has to be enabled on the backend

Search

Search – History

  • (Before 1.3.0) Com “X” search; didn’t like mambos search
    • Basic Search: Written it to be a plugin search because it use basic sequel like statements
  • (Before 1.3.0) Created “Y” search (called com_Y search) 
  • (1.3.0-2.0.0) Built a graph search called “Hubgraph” build directly for nanohub’s use case
  • (2.1.0) Integrated Solr – java open source publication
    • Saves off and achieves its inventory
    • API allows an administrator to remove and blacklist content
      • Search for item
      • Click Kill
      • Removes it from the index and blocks it from being added again
    • Gains Speed
      • All of HabriCentrals data
        • Hubgraph 60 seconds
        • Solr less than a second
    • Used by multiple other services so a trusted open source
    • Powerful and scalable over multiple Solrs instances
      • All documented in the Hubdev group - Wiki
    • Each Hub type (member, project, citation, etc.) is searched
    • Solr is only available on the Hub's overall search but not under every specific component 
      • In the future will build a module that fits in to Component Browsing pages and Solr can search specifically in the component’s content
    • Can only search by keywords and phrases
      • Don’t advertise that you can use easter egg tags to increase the search inventory – internal knowledge
        • FieldName:
        • AND
    • List of searchable sections on the Hub:
      • Blogs
      • Courses
      • Events
      • Groups
      • Members
      • Resources
      • Projects
      • Publications
    • Can turn on logging that states what the user community is searching
    • Map functionality
      • Search for a term
      • Draw a box over a geographical area
      • Click Search
      • Only spits out data that was given a specified location
        • Will be developed later for overall hubs
        • Only works well for GABBS
    • Admins: Can see everything through search (private, public)

Language Overrides

Sometimes Hub owner's ask for language overrides to change the verbiage of a link, etc. Follow these steps to create a new language override:

  1. Navigate to the /administrator interface
  2. Hover over Extensions and click Languages Manager
  3. Select the Overrides tab and click New
  4. Search for the text to override you want to change by adding keywords in the box and clicking Search
  5. Select the section you want to override and change the content in the text box and click Save & Close
  6. Check the site to make sure your verbiage is correct

Project File Connectors

Hubzero allows for files to be shared either on a repository owned by the Hub or connect to other file management platforms. Project File Connectors allow for these third party file management systems to enable files uploaded on the Hub yet stored in their system. Follow these instructions to set-up and provide Project File Connectors to your users:

  1. Navigate to the third party file management system of your choosing, such as Google Drive or Dropbox
  2. Set-up either a new project or application and fill in information about the Hub in order to obtain an API key and API secret upon saving
  3. Make sure you set the callback address to your Hub and indicate the appropriate file system
    1. Example: When setting up a Google Drive API connector to redirect to YourHub, the following callback should be used - https://yourhub.org/callback/googledriveAuthorize (?)
  4. Once the API key and API secret have been created successfully, navigate back to the /administrator interface and login
  5. Hover over Extensions and select from the dropdown Plug-in Manager
  6. Search or locate the appropriate plugin connected to the file system
    1. Example: If the file system chosen is Google Drive, one would select the Filesystem - Google Drive plugin
  7. Click on the title of the plugin and change the status to Enabled
  8. Insert the API Key in the Client ID and the API Secret in the Client Secret
  9. Fill in an further information as necessary then click Save & Close
  10. While still at the Plug-in Manager, search for and click the Projects - Files plugin.
  11. Scroll down until you see an option for Default Action, and set it to Connections (view available connections).
  12. Navigate to a Project you would like to setup a new file system
    1. Note: You must be a manager of the Project in order for you to set-up the File System
  13. Click on Files and then click on New Connection and choose the file system from the dropdown
  14. Choose to bypass the secondary step of connecting to the same API..... 

Setting up an External Application (Dropbox, Google Drive, AWS S3)

For using external services via OAuth2 the Hub needs a client identifier and secret for use with that service.  The methods of obtaining these values vary from service to service and are subject to change at the provider's discretion.  Below are the instructions for setting up a developer application on some services (adapting the instructions with some searching should yield similar results for other services or services that have changed their process in the future).

[Creating an application on Dropbox]

  1. Navigate to https://www.dropbox.com/developers
  2. Sign in using the Dropbox credentials that you would like your Hub (the server itself) to authenticate against, this is usually an account owned by the group or organization.
  3. On the left menu, click "My Apps".
  4. On the top right, click "Create App".
  5. Select the access level you would like to grant your Hub to your users Dropbox accounts.
  6. Give the application a name (this name will be displayed to users when they authorize access to their Dropbox account).
  7. Read and agree (or disagree) to Dropbox's terms.
  8. Click "Enable additional users".
  9. In the redirect URIs section, add the URI of "https://<yourhub.org>/developer/callback/dropboxAuthorize".
  10. At this point you should save the "App key" and show and save your "App secret", you will need to input these on cdmHUB in a later step.
  11. You can now click on the branding tab and brand the application to your Hub's needs (adding icons, links to the website, etc.).  These are all used when a user is asked to enter their Dropbox credentials on behalf of your Hub.

Dropbox currently limits development accounts to 500 users per id/key, this can be raised by contacting Dropbox support and applying for a production key once that limit has been reached.

title: Plugins
content:
Introduction - What is a plugin?


A software component that adds a specific feature to an existing section of the HUB. By allowing plugins to exist the HUB becomes more pliable and flexible to the needs of different users and different functionalities that are not needed in the basic version of the component. Hooks on events.

Supported Plugins

Antispam – Black List: This is a Spam Detector that detects black-listed words. Only flags new content – this plugin is not retroactive.

Antispam – Link Rife: This is a Spam Detector that detects link frequency in a body of text. Has a link to text ratio that can be set. Only flags new content – this plugin is not retroactive.

Antispam – Bayesian Filter: This is a Spam Detector that employs a basic Bayesian filter. Recursive Bayesian estimation that can be trained based on what is flagged as spam (Hubzero Abuse Reports). The more content you train it with, the better the plugin will preform. Only flags new content – this plugin is not retroactive.

Antispam – Baba Ji Spam Detector: Developed by Hubzero to counteract the Baba Ji specific spammer. Only flags new content – this plugin is not retroactive.

Antispam – Akismet: A third party spam detecting service. Has a limit of 5,000 posts a day for a free service. If a Hub goes over that limit then the plugin starts flagging all new content as false, which causes submit problems. Only flags new content – this plugin is not retroactive.

Antispam – Mollom: This plugin uses the remote Mollom service to scan posted content and determine is content has a high probability of being spam or not. Only flags new content – this plugin is not retroactive.

Antispam – SpamAssassin: This plugin scans posted content with SpamAssassin to determine is content has a high probability of being spam or not. This service was developed for email. Only flags new content – this plugin is not retroactive.

Authentication – Hubzero: Handles HUBzero default user authentication. Can send emails to administrators when a new account is created.

Authentication – Facebook: Handles user authentication against Facebook. Does not set a local password.

Authentication – Google: Handles user authentication against Google. Does not set a local password.

Authentication – Linkedin: Handles user authentication against LinkedIn. Does not set a local password.

Authentication – Pucas: Handles user authentication against Purdue's CAS. Does not set a local password.

Authentication – Twitter: Handles user authentication against Twitter. Does not set a local password.

Authentication _ Certificate: Handles user authentication against client side SSL certificates. Does not set a local password.

Authentication – ORCID: Handles user authentication against ORCID. Does not set a local password.

Authentication – Shibboleth: Handles user authentication with Shibboleth/InCommon. Does not set a local password.

Authfactors – Certificate: Alternative to “Authfactors – Certificate”. Handles using a client SSL cert as a secondary auth factor. Does not set a local password.

Authfactors – Authy: Alternative to “Authfactors – Certificate”. Handles using the Authy service as a secondary auth factor. Does not set a local password.

Captcha – ReCaptcha: This CAPTCHA plugin uses the reCAPTCHA service to prevent spammers while it helps to digitize books, newspapers and old radio shows. To get a public and private key for your domain, go to http://www.google.com/recaptcha. To use this for new account registration, go to Options in the User Manager and select Captcha - reCaptcha as the Captcha.

Captcha – Math: A simpler captcha service that uses an math equation to prevent spam bots. It is suggested to use “Captcha – ReCaptcha”.

Captcha – Image: A simpler captcha service that uses an image to prevent spam bots. It is suggested to use “Captcha – ReCaptcha”.

Citation – Default: Imports Text File data - sends off to other plugins. Enable all citation plugins for everything to work.

Citation – Bibtex: Imports BibTex data from the cited material. Enable all citation plugins for everything to work.

Citation – Endnote: Imports Endnote data. Enable all citation plugins for everything to work.

Content – Categories: Does category processing for core extensions. A Joomla! plugin that is used for core filtering.

Content – Page Navigation: Enables you to add the Next & Previous functionality to an Article. Joomla! plugin.

Content – Vote: Add the Voting functionality to Articles

Content – Email Cloaking: Cloaks all emails in content from spambots using JavaScript

Content- Code Highlighter (GeSHi): Displays formatted code in Articles based on the GeSHi highlighting engine

Content – Xhubtabs: Process XHUB tags in com_content items. Used for adding in css templates and modules into content/article pages.

Content – Pagebreak: Allow the creation of a paginated article with optional table of contents. Insert page breaks through the use of the page break button normally found in beneath the text panel in an Article. The location of the page break in an article will be displayed in the editor as a simple horizontal line. The text displayed will depend on the options chosen and may be either the title, alternate text (if provided) or page numbers.

Content – HTML Format Handler: Content handler for HTML content. Allows various macro parsing and optional filtering of incoming content. Plugin that transforms Wiki Style macros in content/article pages. If this plugin is turned off then the Wiki Macros will no longer work.

Content – Baba Ji Spam: Anti-spam plugin that looks at content posted by a very well known spammer. This spammer posts content that contains certain characters, words, and patterns. That plugin looks for those patterns and tries to deny/flag content as being recognized from that spammer.

Content – Open Graph: Adding Open Graph meta information to the site. The Open Graph protocol enables any web page to become a rich object in a social graph. http://ogp.me. Helps search engines, outside of Google’s search, to help content be picked up. A Search Engine Optimization (SEO) plugin.

Cron – Cache Handler: Cron events for Hub cache. Removes old system CSS files and trashes expired cache data at designated intervals.

Cron – Courses: Cron events for courses. Runs a specific job(s) at a set interval linked to the Courses component. Syncs passport badge statuses and can email instructors with a digested update at designated intervals.

Cron – Publications: Cron events for publications. Runs a specific job(s) at a set interval linked to the Publications component. Set to email monthly publication stats to authors, compute unique user stats from text logs, issue master DOI and achieve publications (via mkAIP) when grace period expired – PURR ONLY.

Cron – Support: Cron events for support. Runs a specific job(s) at a set interval linked to the Support component that processes the support queue based on predetermined parameters. Has the ability to close tickets, email reminders for open tickets, email for tickets with specified parameters and remove temporary upload files and directories at set intervals.

title: Dataviewer:  Databases within Projects
content:
Databases within projects are also known as "dataviewer".  This is a plugin called "Projects - Databases".  This software uses different database users, one to write, and one to view data. 

Setting up dataviewer

 

# /usr/bin/hzcms configure dataviewer --enable
enabling dataviewer
creating database user: dataviewer, password = ...
creating database user: datawriter, password = ...

 

The above should setup the passwords also, which can be verified by looking at  /administrator -> Plug-in Manager: Plug-ins -> Projects - Databases

This should do something equivalent to: 

function generate() {
  openssl rand -base64 15
}

function rand_alnum() {
  generate | sed 's/[^a-zA-Z0-9]//g' | cut -c1-16
}

MYSQL_PASS_VIEW=`rand_alnum`
MYSQL_PASS_WRITE=`rand_alnum`

echo run the echoed statements below in MySQL and copy the passwords into Plug-in Manager: Databases
echo "GRANT USAGE ON *.* TO 'dataviewer'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY '$MYSQL_PASS_VIEW';"
echo "GRANT SELECT ON `prj_db_%`.* TO 'dataviewer'@'localhost';"

echo "GRANT USAGE ON *.* TO 'datawriter'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY '$MYSQL_PASS_WRITE';"
echo "GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, DROP ON `prj_db_%`.* TO 'datawriter'@'localhost';"

echo "flush privileges;"

 

Symptoms that this needs to be setup:

Log entries in /var/log/syslog like:

Sep 22 11:32:14 dev.qubeshub.org mysqld: 170922 11:32:14 [Warning] Access denied for user 'datawriter'@'localhost' (using password: YES)

title: Design Documents
content:
Introduction

This section is dedicated to archiving and storing design documents.

 

All hard copies of the design documents and documentation are kept in the Hubzero Development Group's Collection: 

https://hubzero.org/groups/hubdev/collections/development-artifacts

External Production Contribution Procedure

A guide to contributing to your production environment.

Version 1.0

Kevin Wojkovich < kevinw@purdue.edu >

 

Objective

To contribute custom HUBzero CMS components, modules, plugins, templates, language

overrides, and migrations as an external developer to your HUBzero supported & hosted CMS

installation.

 

Technical Implementation

The app directory on the dev / stage production environment has been placed under version

control on https://gitlab.hubzero.org . In order to check this out, you’ll need an account on

https://gitlab.hubzero.org .

 

Once you have an account, you’ll need to join the PURR development group.

 

In order to make a contribution, you will need to place your code into the appropriate directory

within app. For instance, if you modified com_publications under

core/components/com_publications , you must copy that directory to

app/components .

 

*Important*

At this point, the external developer will be required to port the patches that are contributed by

the HUBzero development team in the core/components/com _publications directory.

To help facilitate tracking these changes, you can navigate to the to directory ( cd

core/components/com_publications ) and then run “git log .”.

 

Code Flow

In order to facilitate deployment while implementing a code review process, Gitlab will be the

entry point for the developer to contribute code. On the local development environment, the

developer will clone the gitlab repository into the app directory. The developer will make

changes to the code, make a commit, and push to Gitlab.

 

The developer will need to open and submit a merge request to the HUBzero Development

Team. The HUBzero Development Team will review the code and offer feedback on the

submission.

 

The HUBzero Development Team will may accept OR reject the submission in accordance to

the feedback. The HUBzero Development Team typically can process external submissions in 3 - 5 business days depending on the size of the submission.

 

Developer Local VM Setup

(NOT dev.purr.purdue.edu)

  1. cp app ~/app.bak
    1. Make a backup of the app directory
  2. rm R app
    1. Remove the app directory
  3. git clone git@gitlab.hubzero.org :purr/purrapp.git
    1. Clone the app directory to app
  4. Restore the logs, cache, site, mkAIP, config, and temp directory
    1. Maintenance of mkAIP may move into this new repository. Will require some changes.
  5. Make appropriate changes
    1. Might include copying changes from core/* directories
    2. Could be custom code
  6. git add
    1. Add changed files
  7. git commit m “Message describing changes in clear language.”
    1. Make the commit
  8. git push
    1. Push the commit to gitlab.hubzero.org
  9. Go to https://gitlab.hubzero.org , create merge request.

 

Developer Notes

Please refer to the Contribution Guide (https://hubzero.org/about/contributions) for guidelines on submissions.

 

Please refer to the Style Guide (https://hubzero.org/documentation/current/webdevs/conventions)

for guidelines on coding standards.

 

Please refer to the Web Developer Documentation for general documentation

(https://hubzero.org/documentation/current/webdevs/).

 

The HUBzero Development team reserves the right to reject any submission that does not meet

these standards, that may interfere with existing functionality, or introduces security concerns

into the production environment.

title: Supported Hub Specific Documentation
content:
Creating a Special Nanohub subversion repositoy

Nanohub has a historical precedent of providing various "special" subversion
repositories.

These repositories are manually maintained in
/etc/apache2/nanohub.conf.d/svn-extra.conf This file is not automatically
regenereated so any changes to the LDAP authentication connection
settings (hostname, password, etc) have to be manually updated.

The me581 group has historically been re-created every fall. If creating a new
one rename the old (replace YEAR with the year the previous repository was
made for)

$ mv /opt/svn/group/me581 /opt/svn/group/me581-YEAR

To create "special" group repository:

$ cd /opt/svn/group
$ svnadmin create REPO_NAME --fs-type fsfs
$ chown www-data:www-data REPO_NAME

Sometimes special repository can get made in the "infrastructure"
subdirectory, although this is less common in recent history and its
future use is discouraged.

$ cd /opt/svn/infrastructure
$ svnadmin create REPO_NAME --fs-type fsfs
$ chown www-data:www-data REPO_NAME

Once the repository is created edit /etc/apache2/nanohub.conf.d/svn-extra.conf
and copy a similar group or infrastructure stanza and replace the copied
repository name with your new one. Typically such a stanza will look similar
to:

<Location /groups/REPO_NAME/svn>
        DAV svn
        SVNPath /opt/svn/groups/REPO_NAME
        AuthType Basic
        AuthBasicProvider ldap
        AuthName "REPO_NAME" Subversion Repository"
        AuthzLDAPAuthoritative on
        AuthLDAPBindDN "cn=search,dc=nanohub,dc=org"
        AuthLDAPBindPassword "LDAP_PASSWORD"
        AuthLDAPGroupAttributeIsDN off
        AuthLDAPGroupAttribute memberUid
        AuthLDAPURL ldap://nanohub.org/ou=users,dc=nanohub,dc=org
        Require ldap-group cn=REPO_NAME,ou=groups,dc=nanohub,dc=org
</Location>

With REPO_NAME replaced with your new repository name and LDAP_PASSWORD
replaced with the current nanohub ldap password. You should copy a stanza
from the current file to be sure to get latest format. "groups" could also
be replaced with "infrastructure" if you wanted to create an "infrastructure"
group (discouraged).

Special Authorization (e.g., ME581)
===================================

You can create per directory access control in subversion. This has been
done for the special /tools/nemo/svn repository (a special case of the standard
tool repository configuration) and the special /group/me581/svn repository.
It is create by adding the file /opt/svn/groups/REPO_NAME/conf/svnauthz.conf

The format of the file for me581 looks like

[groups]
me581=username1,username2,username3
me581-admin=lzentner,marisol,yourname,ta_names

[/]
@me581-admin = rw

[/username1]
username1 = rw

[/username2]
username2 = rw

[/username3]
username3 = rw

A small bash script can be written to generate the [/usernameN] segments, or
it can be done manually. The users in the @me581-admin SVN group have access
to everything in the repository. The individual usernameN accounts only have
access to the directory named after them as indicated.

To use the svnauthz.conf file you will need to change your configuration
stanza in svn-extra.conf by replacing

Require ldap-group cn=REPO_NAME,ou=groups,dc=nanohub,dc=org

with

AuthzSVNAccessFile /opt/svn/groups/REPO_NAME/conf/svnauthz.conf
Require valid-user

To initialize this repository it is necessary to create each of those
usernameN directories and commit them to the repository. Technically this can
be done by anyone in the me581-group but historically has been done by the
person creating the repository. (if you already have an me581 directory from a
previous year you will want to remove or rename it)

$ cd
$ svn checkout https://nanohub.org/groups/me581/svn me581
$ cd me581
$ mkdir username1 username2 username3
$ svn add username1 username2 username 3
$ svn commit "create initial user directories"

A small bash script can be written to create all the directories or they can
be created manually.

If you later add a username to the svnauthz.conf file be sure to create and
commit a corresponding user directory.

 

This information is also located at /etc/apache2/nanohub.conf.d/svn-extra.README
